title: Agential Efficiency Measurement
text: Agential Efficiency Measurement When building agential coding infrastructure, measure token consumption and execution time as proxies for energy usage You are building systems where AI agents perform significant computational work (code generation, analysis, search). Agential coding can increase productivity and enable new capabilities Current energy usage patterns for AI inference are non-trivial; without measurement, efficiency claims are unfounded Instrument all agent operations to measure: tokens consumed (input + output), wall-clock time, retries/failures. Log these metrics per mission/session. Compare agent-assisted work against human-only baseline where possible. (1) Planetary: Energy efficiency matters. If agential coding is less efficient than human coding, that's a real cost. (2) Economic: People will pay for proven efficiency gains. Unmeasured efficiency is a claim, not a fact. (3) Optimization: You can only improve what you measure. Metrics reveal where agents waste tokens on unproductive loops. evidence[futon3a/P4 (mission queue) includes pass criterion for token/time measurement per mission] evidence[futon3a sidecar logs include session duration and turn counts (proxy for token use)] next[Add token counters to all fucodex/fuclaude sessions (input tokens, output tokens, total)] next[Log mission-level metrics: tokens/mission, time/mission, success rate] next[Baseline: measure human time for equivalent tasks (where feasible)] next[After 10+ missions: analyze whether night-shift automation is more efficient than equivalent human work] next[If efficiency gains are proven: document them; if not: identify waste and optimize]

title: Agential Open Source Infrastructure
text: Agential Open Source Infrastructure When agents write significant code in open-source contexts, make learning loops explicit via tool-use logging (PSR/PUR, sidecar audit trails) You are building infrastructure for agent-assisted or agent-authored open-source software. Agential programming is real — agents write, review, and maintain significant portions of codebases You remain committed to open-source principles: transparency, auditability, collaborative improvement Develop explicit open-source infrastructure for agents: tool-use logging (sidecar), pattern selection records (PSR), pattern use records (PUR), confidence scoring, evidence chains Human OSS relies on tacit learning loops (code review norms, testing practices, maintainer judgment acquired through socialization). Agents don't learn through socialization — their learning loops must be explicit, machine-checkable, and auditable. This makes certain economic and coordination patterns visible that were previously implicit. evidence[futon3a sidecar implements PSR/PUR logging for pattern-guided agent work] evidence[musn_chat_supervisor.clj aggregates pattern traces for review] evidence[p4ng paper (Patterns for a New Generation) describes PSR/PUR as audit mechanism] next[Document how sidecar logging enables new coordination patterns beyond traditional OSS] next[Identify which tacit human OSS practices need explicit agent infrastructure] next[Consider: does this infrastructure frighten traditional OSS communities? If so, how to frame it gently?] next[Explore post-OSS economic models that emerge when learning loops are explicit]

title: Agential Pattern Hygiene
text: Agential Pattern Hygiene When using design patterns as agent governance, teach agents to maintain pattern quality by promoting evidence and updating core reasoning You are using flexiarg patterns as a control layer for agential coding infrastructure. Patterns guide agent behavior through IF/HOWEVER/THEN/BECAUSE reasoning and accumulate evidence in EVIDENCE/NEXT-STEPS sections Agents don't automatically know to maintain patterns — they may treat patterns as write-only logs, appending evidence without updating core reasoning or promoting next-steps to evidence when completed Explicitly teach agents pattern hygiene: (1) move completed NEXT-STEPS to EVIDENCE when done, (2) update core IF/HOWEVER/THEN/BECAUSE if evidence refutes or refines the reasoning, (3) prune obsolete next-steps, (4) mark patterns for promotion (:stub→:greenfield→:active→:settled) when criteria met Patterns can increase in quality through use and become living documents that reflect learned experience, rather than degrading into unmaintained dumping grounds. This keeps the library curated and trustworthy. evidence[2026-01-22: During futon3a.devmap review, Joe spotted that P3 (Meme Layer) had dependency direction wrong and P2 (Compass) was missing prior art from futon2/fulab. These were fixed by updating EVIDENCE section and refining BECAUSE clause — pattern improved through review] evidence[library/control patterns themselves model this: effort-estimation, agential-oss-infrastructure, agential-efficiency-measurement were created when meta-patterns became clear during devmap work] next[Add pattern hygiene instructions to fucodex/fuclaude system prompts] next[When agent completes a next-step, prompt it to move that step to evidence] next[In morning review protocol (futon3a/P5), include pattern hygiene check: any next-steps that should be promoted?] next[In library evidence feedback (futon3a/P6), flag patterns with stale next-steps (not updated in 4+ weeks) for hygiene review] next[Test: run 5 sessions with explicit hygiene prompts, measure whether patterns improve vs degrade]

title: Effort Estimation with Token & Human Time
text: Effort Estimation with Token & Human Time When estimating work for devmap prototypes, track both token consumption (AI work) and human time (decision/review), with confidence levels You are planning development work that involves both human decision-making and AI execution (via Codex/Claude). Traditional effort estimates use person-hours, but AI-assisted work splits effort between human (design, review, decisions) and tokens (implementation, search, analysis) Tracking only time misses token costs; tracking only tokens misses human bottlenecks; neither captures uncertainty Use effort schema: {:tokens {:context Nk :implementation Nk :review Nk} :hours {:joe N :codex N} :confidence :high|:medium|:low} This format is machine-readable, separates concerns (reading vs building vs checking), makes token budgets explicit, and flags uncertainty via confidence evidence[Introduced in futon3a.devmap (2026-01-22) for prototype effort tracking] next[Apply effort-estimation schema to all futon3a prototypes] next[After 5+ prototypes have estimates and actuals, compare predicted vs actual] next[Update schema if token/hours split doesn't match reality] next[Add :elapsed field once we have actuals to compare against estimates]

title: Coordination Argument (Gate Pipeline)
text: Coordination Argument (Gate Pipeline) A six-gate pipeline over typed evidence records is the minimal structure that turns messy activity into organized knowledge with auditable records. Futon3 already has working pieces (transport, check DSL, trails, workday intake, pattern retrieval bridges), but they are not composed into a single boundary that enforces pattern use and durable evidence. you want FUTON3 to reliably produce records that other futons can use to learn and act when pattern selection, execution, validation, and persistence are scattered, the system cannot enforce invariants like "no work runs without PSR" or "no success acknowledged before durability" compose the existing implementations through a gate pipeline: - G5 defines TaskSpec and binds intent to mission + success criteria - G4 authorizes an agent and records an Assignment - G3 requires PSR (or gap declaration) and records candidates - G2 runs bounded execution and registers an Artifact - G1 produces PUR by evaluating criteria against artifacts - G0 gates success on durability and requires PAR to close the loop this structure is checkable (gate ordering, typed rejections, evidence shapes) and creates a proof-path that can be replayed, audited, and fed into glacial library evolution next[Define a machine-checkable exotype diagram and concrete instantiation, and stop-the-line when concrete ports/edges drift from the exotype.] next[Wire futon3b gate modules to futon3 transport surfaces (WS/HTTP) while preserving the "first failing gate wins" invariant.]

title: Artifact Registration (G2)
text: Artifact Registration (G2) If you want validation and durability to be meaningful, require execution to emit a registered artifact record with stable identifiers and provenance. "Something happened" is not enough; we need an artifact we can point to. you want later gates to validate outcomes and persist evidence without an artifact record, later gates cannot refer to the product of execution make artifact registration an explicit G2 output, and treat missing artifacts as a gate failure artifact identity is the join-key that makes PSR→PUR→PAR compositional

title: Assignment Binding (G4)
text: Assignment Binding (G4) If you want replayable proof-paths, record an explicit assignment evidence record that binds agent-id to task-id and treat conflicting assignments as a gate rejection. Coordination needs a durable "who is responsible" record. you want artifacts and validation outcomes to be attributable without a recorded assignment, later evidence cannot be traced to accountable actors emit an Assignment record at G4 and reject when a task is already assigned to another agent (exclusive binding) attribution is a core coordination invariant; ambiguity becomes debt

title: Bounded Execution (G2)
text: Bounded Execution (G2) If you want safe and predictable coordination, execute tasks under explicit budgets (time, tokens, side effects) and reject when budgets are exceeded. Coordination must treat execution as a resource-consuming action with a defined budget. you want an execution gate that cannot run away or wedge the system unbounded execution produces unpredictable latency and failure modes that break multi-agent systems enforce a budget at G2 and short-circuit with a typed rejection when exceeded budgets create selection pressure and prevent hidden coordination costs

title: Capability Gate (G4)
text: Capability Gate (G4) If you want reliable coordination, gate task execution on an explicit capability match between the task requirements and the registered agent. "Agent can do it" must be checked, not assumed. you want to route tasks to heterogeneous agents (humans, Codex, Claude, services) without authorization, tasks can be executed by agents that lack tools, permissions, or responsibility require the agent to be present in the registry and validate capability match at G4 otherwise failures are silent and attribution is unclear (who was supposed to do what?)

title: Cross Validation Protocol (G1)
text: Cross Validation Protocol (G1) If you want robustness against self-serving validation, define a cross-validation path where another agent (or a deterministic harness) can re-run the validation on the same evidence. Validation should be replayable by someone other than the executor. you want to reduce confabulation and improve trust in PUR outcomes a single agent validating its own work can silently lower standards require validation evidence to be sufficient for replay, and define a cross-validation protocol that can be invoked from the PUR chain coordination quality depends on independent verification of claimed progress

title: Intent to Mission Binding (G5)
text: Intent to Mission Binding (G5) If you want progress claims to be comparable across sessions, bind each task to an explicit mission reference and success criteria before authorization or execution. Intent strings are not enough; the system needs mission-scoped obligations. you want the same "kind of work" to be evaluated consistently over time free-form intent without mission binding makes evidence drift and prevents traceability to devmaps require `:task/mission-ref` and `:task/success-criteria` and verify mission is active at G5 mission binding is the only stable anchor that makes later PSR/PUR/PAR meaningful

title: Mandatory PSR (G3)
text: Mandatory PSR (G3) If you want execution to be pattern-governed rather than post-hoc rationalized, require a Pattern Selection Record (PSR) before execution, or a typed gap declaration. Pattern use must be chosen before acting, not retroactively claimed. you want work to be guided by shared patterns and constraints letting execution proceed without PSR makes validation ambiguous and invites confabulated explanations require PSR (pattern selected) or Gap PSR (pattern missing) at G3 before G2 can run this makes the pipeline auditable: you can compare chosen pattern vs outcome later

title: Mandatory PUR (G1)
text: Mandatory PUR (G1) If you want the system to produce organized knowledge, require a Pattern Use Record (PUR) that evaluates success criteria against produced artifacts. Pattern selection only matters if we evaluate whether it worked. you want coordination outputs to be evidence-driven without PUR, you cannot distinguish successful pattern use from failure, drift, or luck require G1 to emit a PUR for the PSR, and reject when criteria are not met this creates a stable learning signal for the library evolution loop

title: PAR as Obligation (G0)
text: PAR as Obligation (G0) If you want the library evolution loop to have usable signals, require a PAR (post-action review) before closing a coordinated session and treat its absence as a gate rejection. Without PAR, the system accumulates execution without learning. you want the system to improve patterns and coordination over time evidence without retrospective interpretation does not produce tensions or canonicalization candidates require a PAR record at G0, minimally capturing what worked, what did not, and suggested improvements PAR is the bridge between Level 0 execution and Level 1 library evolution

title: Pattern Search Protocol (G3)
text: Pattern Search Protocol (G3) If you want pattern selection to be reviewable and improvable, log the candidate search process (query, candidates, scores) as part of PSR evidence. A PSR should explain not just the winner but the considered alternatives. you want pattern retrieval quality to improve over time without candidate logs, retrieval is a black box and failures cannot be debugged record `:psr/candidates` and a short rationale in the PSR output of G3 the search protocol is part of the evidence, and it feeds the glacial library evolution loop later

title: Session Durability Check (G0)
text: Session Durability Check (G0) If you want coordinated work to compound, gate successful responses on durable persistence of the full proof-path and its evidence records. If evidence is not durable, coordination is theater. you want an audit trail that can be replayed after the session ends acknowledging success before persistence creates silent loss modes (accepted-but-not-stored) verify durability at G0 and reject success when persistence fails a proof-path is only real if it can be reconstructed later

title: Task Shape Validation (G5)
text: Task Shape Validation (G5) If you want coordination to be auditable and repeatable, gate execution on a minimal well-typed task specification and reject malformed tasks with gate attribution. A coordination pipeline must not accept "do stuff" inputs; it must accept a task with mission binding and success criteria. you want multiple agents and tools to execute work safely accepting underspecified tasks makes later evidence unverifiable and failures ambiguous validate the task shape at the boundary (G5) and reject with structured errors carrying `:gate/id` and `:error/key` early rejection is cheaper than running execution/validation on nonsense and later arguing about what was meant next[Define TaskSpec shape and enforce it for all inputs crossing the gate pipeline boundary.]

title: Carrying One's Own Question (Apprentice → Independent Investigator)
text: Carrying One's Own Question (Apprentice → Independent Investigator) Carrying One's Own Question You are helping a researcher move from mentor-defined problems to a self-owned line of inquiry. A researcher has gained methodological competence but still relies on supervisors to define the next inquiry step. Independence emerges when a doctoral candidate can articulate, justify, and refine a question they claim as their own line of inquiry. Support them in naming that question explicitly—write a brief rationale for why it matters, revisit and document how it evolves, and surface it inside presentations, draft sections, and supervisory dialogue so ownership is unmistakable. Independence is not the absence of supervision; it is the presence of a clearly owned line of inquiry. Making ownership visible strengthens confidence, clarifies expectations, and aligns supervisory teams around the researcher’s judgement. + next[Ask them to draft a one-page "own question" memo and review it together.] + next[Add the question to their research log and revisit it at each check-in.]

title: Relationship to existing doctoral training
text: Relationship to existing doctoral training The CORPS Five Arrows clarify the developmental transitions that support effective participation in research environments. [🚴/五] Doctoral programmes provide discipline-specific training and supervision, yet the shifts that enable researchers to act with confidence, collaboration, and responsibility often remain implicit. Doctoral programmes aim to produce confident, collaborative, responsible researchers. The transitions that build those capacities are rarely made explicit or scaffolded. Provide a structured developmental scaffold that enables researchers to practise these transitions through small adjustments to their workflows and reflective documentation, without altering existing supervisory arrangements or disciplinary expectations. Programmes such as talk4real may build on these transitions by linking individual development to collective inquiry routines, though such integration is not required for CORPS. The five transitions—student to colleague; apprentice to independent investigator; individual contributor to collaborative team member; private learner to public practitioner; project-focused worker to systems-aware researcher—already occur within doctoral pathways, but without a shared framework they are difficult to recognise, support, or evaluate. Making these transitions explicit helps align supervisory expectations with cohort development and with the institutional research culture that doctoral programmes aim to foster. next[Draft a one-page summary of the five arrows that supervisors can review with candidates.]

title: Letting the Trace Teach (Private Learning → Public-Facing Identity)
text: Letting the Trace Teach (Private Learning → Public-Facing Identity) Letting the Trace Teach You are helping a researcher move private learning into a public-facing identity. Doctoral researchers accumulate tacit knowledge but keep it inside informal notes, calls, or unshared materials. Without public artefacts their emerging expertise stays invisible to collaborators, employers, and interdisciplinary partners. Encourage the release of small, well-scoped artefacts—annotated examples, brief reflections, walkthroughs, explanatory notes—into venues where relevant peers already circulate. Public-facing traces signal identity and invite collaboration; they provide low-risk entry points for others to understand, support, or extend the researcher’s work while helping the researcher build confidence as a contributor. + next[Select one trace-worthy insight from the last month and publish it in a shared venue.] + next[Invite one collaborator to respond or extend the artefact.]

title: Seeing the Surrounding Conditions (Project → System)
text: Seeing the Surrounding Conditions (Project → System) Seeing the Surrounding Conditions You are helping a researcher situate a project inside institutional systems and dependencies. A doctoral project sits inside wider institutional systems—data governance, shared infrastructure, ethics boards, administrative rhythms—but the researcher only sees the immediate task. Responsible decisions about methods, data, and collaboration require awareness of upstream dependencies and downstream effects. Guide the researcher through mapping dependencies, meeting governance partners, and reflecting on how their actions touch technical, administrative, and academic stakeholders so the surrounding system stays in view. Systems-level awareness improves decision quality, anticipates bottlenecks, and prepares researchers for future roles with broader responsibility by teaching how individual work affects the collective environment. next[Use this pattern to guide the CORPS sketch expansion toward system-level dependencies.]

title: Standing in the Circle (Student → Colleague)
text: Standing in the Circle (Student → Colleague) Standing in the Circle You are helping a doctoral researcher shift from student to colleague inside a research team. Doctoral researchers are expected to participate in research teams, represent their work, and contribute to shared decisions, yet their reasoning and trade-offs remain invisible to peers. When a researcher is always positioned as “learner receiving instruction,” collaborators miss the moment when they are ready to act as colleagues. Provide structured opportunities for them to narrate decisions in a peer-facing format—decision notes, reflective summaries, short presentations of provisional conclusions—so their judgement is legible to the team rather than hidden inside supervisory conversations. Explicit reasoning creates recognition: supervisors and peers can respond at the appropriate level, collaboration becomes more mature, and the researcher internalises professional discourse norms that move them from student to colleague. + next[Ask them to produce a decision note after the next team meeting.] + next[Schedule a short peer-facing update where they present one provisional conclusion.]

title: Working Where Others Can See (Individual Contributor → Collaborative Team Member)
text: Working Where Others Can See (Individual Contributor → Collaborative Team Member) Working Where Others Can See You are shifting an individual workflow into a collaborative team setting where visibility matters. A project depends on mutual visibility of tasks, decisions, and intermediate outputs, yet the researcher’s workflow remains private or idiosyncratic. Teams cannot coordinate or intervene early when work stays on personal drives or in opaque notebooks. Move key elements of the workflow into shared spaces—open notes, reproducible scripts, transparent task boards—and annotate decision points so colleagues can interpret and respond without extra meetings. Collaboration relies on visible work surfaces. When intermediate steps are reviewable, teams reduce duplication, coordinate effectively, and offer support before issues harden into blockers. + next[Choose one shared workspace (notes, repo, or task board) and migrate the next deliverable there.] + next[Add a brief decision log so teammates can respond asynchronously.]

title: A Mission Can Warm an Outward EoI That Is Cold on the Recipient's Side
text: A Mission Can Warm an Outward EoI That Is Cold on the Recipient's Side An outward EoI can be cold on the recipient's side yet warm on yours when a Mission is its unlock-precondition. Model the (Mission → EoI) relation as a first-class edge, gate the EoI on the mission producing a showable artefact, and the asymmetry — cold-for-them, warm-for-you — becomes precisely what makes the eventual contact non-arbitrary instead of a fan note or a bare ask. A strawman names an outward contact whose honest hook is a *convergence* between your work and theirs (not "I used your theory" but "a system built for other reasons landed on your structure"). For a peer this is sendable now; for a senior or cold recipient the convergence isn't yet legible — there is no artefact that makes it visible in thirty seconds. The temptation is to send on enthusiasm or to defer indefinitely; both waste the lead. You hold a strawman for an outward EoI where (a) the hook is a real convergence with the recipient's work, and (b) the recipient is cold or senior enough that the convergence must be *shown*, not asserted — and (c) some mission of yours, run for its own reasons, would produce exactly the artefact that makes the convergence legible. Sending while the convergence is invisible burns a one-shot first impression and reads as fan-mail or an ask; indefinitely deferring loses the lead and lets the territory move. Treating "cold" as a single property hides the real structure: the contact is cold on *their* side (they don't know you) but can be made warm on *yours* (you have something worth showing) — and the bridge between the two is a specific mission's deliverable. Record the EoI as DEFERRED with an explicit gate that names the mission and its done-condition — the (Mission → EoI) edge as a first-class object. The mission is the warming precondition: when it yields the showable artefact, the contact becomes warm-on-your-side (legible convergence, concrete thing to show) even though it stays cold on theirs, and *that* asymmetry is the EoI's justification. The strawman carries the hook and the predicted tensions; the edge carries the WHEN. Do not collapse the gate into a vague "later." The quality of a cold outward contact is set by what you can make legible at first glance, not by your enthusiasm. Naming the unlocking mission converts an open-ended "someday" into a checkable trigger, keeps the lead alive without spending it prematurely, and makes the eventual EoI self-justifying ("I built X for other reasons; here it is; it converges with your Y"). It also turns a connector-node mission into a generator of well-timed EoIs that point through it at downstream nodes, rather than terminating in a verdict. - In the strawman frontmatter, set `status: DEFERRED` and a `gate:` field naming the unlocking mission + its done-condition (the showable artefact). - Record the (Mission → EoI) edge where the interest-network / buckets can see it, so the EoI surfaces automatically when the mission's artefact lands — don't rely on remembering. - Keep the strawman's hook and predicted-tensions current; the gate changes WHEN, not WHAT. - Distinguish the two failure modes the gate prevents: premature-send (cold on both sides, nothing to show) and lead-decay (deferred with no trigger, so it never fires). - Honest scope: the mission warms the contact on YOUR side only. The recipient is still cold; the EoI's discipline (concision, one striking hook, no overclaim) still applies in full.

title: This Grant Proposal Could Have Been a Consulting Pitch
text: This Grant Proposal Could Have Been a Consulting Pitch Reframe finished grant-style capability demonstrations as consulting pitches for recipients with immediate needs, so the same craft stops producing only long review cycles and starts producing revenue opportunities. An academic practitioner writes grant proposals that demonstrate capability, methodology, and relevance to a funder's priorities. The same skill - framing what you can do in terms of what the recipient needs - is exactly what consulting proposals require. The practitioner has experience writing grants (UKRN, EPSRC, etc.) and has demonstrable capabilities (Bayesian modelling, pattern languages, knowledge management, AI integration). Grant proposals go to institutions with long review cycles and uncertain outcomes. Consulting pitches go to organisations with immediate needs and shorter cycles. The same skill applied to the wrong recipient produces months of waiting instead of weeks of revenue. For each capability demonstration (working paper, tool, methodology), ask: "who would pay for this as a service rather than fund it as research?" Reframe the grant narrative as a consulting proposal. The Bayesian logic model becomes "evaluation consulting." The pattern language becomes "structured methodology." The knowledge graph becomes "enterprise knowledge management." The inverse also applies: a successful consulting engagement generates evidence that strengthens future grant proposals. The pattern is bidirectional, not a one-way conversion. The fabrication "I need a grant to do this work" dissolves when you realise the work is already done and the question is who values it. Grants fund potential; consulting pays for demonstrated capability. The practitioner who has built the stack already has the demonstration. next[Review each completed grant-style artifact and write one concrete consulting version aimed at a recipient with a present-tense operational need.]

title: Scan -> Talk -> Frame
text: Scan -> Talk -> Frame Combine a recurring scan, a live conversation, and a fixed frame so pipeline-building becomes a repeatable practice that turns fantasy about getting paid for passion into concrete assessment. A practitioner has capabilities but no pipeline. The gap between "what I can do" and "who will pay for it" feels like an abyss. Fantasy fabrication fills the gap: "wouldn't it be nice to get paid for what I love doing." The practitioner has a systematic scan (probes), an agent to talk with (structured conversation), and a frame schema (what to record). Scanning alone produces data, not direction. Talking alone produces narrative, not structure. Recording alone produces archives, not momentum. Combine all three into a daily hour: scan the landscape (5 min automated), talk through each item as a braindump (45 min), structure the output as a frame (10 min). The frame is the artifact. The conversation is the adapter. The scan is the stimulus. This is intentional samskara - the deliberate fabrication of mental formations that serve the practitioner. The "unhelpful fabrication" is the dream of being paid for passion. The "helpful fabrication" is the daily discipline of scanning, assessing, and recording. Both are fabricated; one produces evidence, the other produces fantasy. Fantasy dissolves when confronted with specifics. "Wouldn't it be nice" becomes "Logseq has $50K on OpenCollective and 913 open tickets - do I want to close tickets or pitch a roadmap?" The pattern replaces vague aspiration with concrete assessment, repeated daily until the pipeline either materialises or the approach is revised. next[Run the daily scan-talk-frame hour until each probe turns into either a concrete pitch target or an explicit rejection of the current approach.]

title: Upstream Patches as Consulting Signal
text: Upstream Patches as Consulting Signal Treat merged upstream patches as consulting signal: a public change to a codebase the client already cares about says more than self-promotion ever can. A practitioner wants to signal expertise to potential clients or employers but dislikes self-promotion. Blog posts, talks, and social media feel performative. The practitioner uses open-source dependencies deeply enough to find bugs, missing features, or design improvements. Sending one patch to one project is invisible. Writing blog posts about capabilities feels hollow without evidence. Systematically identify patch opportunities in the upstream dependency network. Prioritise patches to projects with commercial ecosystems (XTDB, Datahike, Logseq) or active communities (Reagent, Malli). Each merged patch is a permanent, verifiable signal that says "I understand your codebase well enough to improve it." The Drawbridge CIDER adapter is the prototype instance: a real gap (no existing adapter), deep expertise (daily use of Drawbridge in the stack), and high visibility (every CIDER user would benefit). Estimated effort: 2-3 days. Signal value: permanent. A merged PR is the strongest possible consulting signal. It is not self-promotion - it is demonstrated competence, publicly verifiable, attached to a real codebase the client cares about. The practitioner's dependency graph IS their professional network; patches are introductions. next[Maintain a ranked patch target list drawn from the dependency graph and treat each merged upstream contribution as both depositing and lead-generation evidence.]

title: Baseline Freeze & Audit Hooks
text: Baseline Freeze & Audit Hooks declare a baseline freeze window, capture canonical transcripts/configs/seed graphs, and wire audit hooks (`check!`, graph exports, viriya deltas) so every new change proves it still matches the frozen reference You should implement a baseline freeze to maintain integrity by capturing key configurations and setting up audit hooks. a futon layer claims to offer a "known-good" transport or memory baseline that downstream futons rely on baselines tend to rot—golden transcripts drift, flags diverge, and the story of "what already works" fractures across READMEs declare a baseline freeze window, capture canonical transcripts/configs/seed graphs, and wire audit hooks (`check!`, graph exports, viriya deltas) so every new change proves it still matches the frozen reference dhammavicaya is about investigating what *already* exists; without explicit freezes and audit hooks, every promise of determinism becomes oral history next[Name a freeze window, then snapshot the canonical transcripts/configs/seed graphs into a fixed location.] next[Add a `check!` or export hook that compares current state to the freeze baseline on each release.]

title: Devmap Scope Discipline
text: Devmap Scope Discipline scrub each clause so it references only the layer’s own mechanisms, blockers, exports, and guarantees; move projections into the appropriate futon or retire them until evidence exists. To ensure your devmaps accurately describe a layer's mechanisms, avoid referencing unrelated projections that dilute clarity. devmaps are supposed to describe the guarantees and mechanisms intrinsic to a layer. entries often drift into upstream/downstream speculation (agents, policies, future futons), diluting responsibility boundaries. scrub each clause so it references only the layer’s own mechanisms, blockers, exports, and guarantees; move projections into the appropriate futon or retire them until evidence exists. sharp scope makes layers composable and keeps stack blockers observable. evidence[library/devmap-coherence/prototype-alignment-bridge.flexiarg:1] next[Apply this check to FUTON1–4 devmaps; annotate clauses that mention external futons without bridges.]

title: IFR — FUTON0 Mindful Apprehension (sati)
text: IFR — FUTON0 Mindful Apprehension (sati) verify that vitality signals (git activity, recording cadence, tai-chi prompts) flow into FUTON3 telemetry, that epistemic rhythm reviews happen on schedule, and that the mindful ground for wondrous apprehension is observable rather than assumed FUTON0 provides the embodied/experiential base through which all other futons perceive. Its signals must be traceable. FUTON0 claims to supply dependable vitality indicators and epistemic rhythm without added lifelogging friction vitality signals scatter across cron jobs, notes, and implicit habits; without explicit telemetry hooks, the mindful ground becomes oral history verify that vitality signals (git activity, recording cadence, tai-chi prompts) flow into FUTON3 telemetry, that epistemic rhythm reviews happen on schedule, and that the mindful ground for wondrous apprehension is observable rather than assumed sati is the quality of presence that makes all other factors possible; FUTON0 must prove its signals are actually reaching the stack, not just claimed next[Add a vitality telemetry check to the FUTON3 morning review that confirms F0 signals arrived.] next[Log any missed rhythm reviews (weekly/monthly) as drift markers for F0 health.]

title: IFR — FUTON1 Graph Memory Seed (dhammavicaya)
text: IFR — FUTON1 Graph Memory Seed (dhammavicaya) run the FUTON3 `check!` DSL against Pattern Canon entries that certify the MUSN transport baseline, verifying that each CLI/ingest transcript has a reproducible twin in futon1 graphs You are expected to validate that all CLI transcripts have a match in futon1 graphs to ensure consistent baseline transport. the system maintains a deterministic graph-memory snapshot of the personal stack (CLI transcripts, NLP tags, XTDB mirrors) focus headers, ingest scripts, and CLI demos drift unless transport invariants are checked and documented run the FUTON3 `check!` DSL against Pattern Canon entries that certify the MUSN transport baseline, verifying that each CLI/ingest transcript has a reproducible twin in futon1 graphs without codified dhammavicaya, higher futons cannot inspect “the system model of me” with confidence next[Run `check!` for the MUSN transport baseline on each ingest and store the transcript hash.] next[Publish a short report listing any missing transcript-to-graph matches.]

title: IFR — FUTON2 Active Inference Energy (viriya)
text: IFR — FUTON2 Active Inference Energy (viriya) for every recorded episode, check that pivot streams, graph adapters, and presence bridges emit data usable by the FUTON3 proof engine and FUTON7 civic dashboards Ensure the data emitted from your processes is usable by the FUTON3 proof engine to allow for effective collaboration. FUTON2 exposes narratable AIF loops whose agents export state into FUTON1 and FUTON3 ants risk becoming isolated war-game toys unless their exports feed graph memory, presence buses, and viriya metrics for every recorded episode, check that pivot streams, graph adapters, and presence bridges emit data usable by the FUTON3 proof engine and FUTON7 civic dashboards viriya means kinetic collaboration—without these hooks, energy cannot circulate through the stack next[Add a validation step that checks each episode's exports against the proof engine and civic dashboard schemas.] next[Publish a dashboard panel showing missing or malformed exports by agent and episode.]

title: IFR — FUTON3 Flexiformal Proofwork (pīti)
text: IFR — FUTON3 Flexiformal Proofwork (pīti) batch-run `check!` against each devmap obligation, log proof states, emit follow-on obligations, and surface joy metrics (time-to-proof, obligations cleared) for everyone doing workday submissions Regularly log proof states and surface joy metrics to demonstrate your effective actions during work submissions. FUTON3 keeps the pattern canon, similarity field, and check DSL running so daily work can be certified as empowered action without regular audits, the proof trails drift from the devmaps and joy devolves into aimless play batch-run `check!` against each devmap obligation, log proof states, emit follow-on obligations, and surface joy metrics (time-to-proof, obligations cleared) for everyone doing workday submissions pīti is the pleasure of effective action; FUTON3 must constantly show that pattern checks move real obligations forward next[Add a `check!` summary section in the workday report that shows obligations cleared and follow-ons emitted.] next[Add a short note linking proof state changes back to the devmap or pattern ID that motivated them.]

title: IFR — FUTON3A Pattern Guidance & Audit (pīti-audit)

Without explicit maturity tracking, readers cannot tell which are speculative vs. battle-tested. devmap prototypes progress from initial idea through implementation to stable operation without explicit maturity tags, all prototypes look equally authoritative; stubs masquerade as proven, settled work gets re-litigated tag every prototype with a maturity level (:stub, :greenfield, :active, :settled) and define evidence-based promotion criteria; demote when evidence contradicts the claimed level - Success rate drops below 50% over 10 uses → demote one level - Breaking change without migration path → demote to :greenfield - Abandoned >3 months without maintenance → demote to :stub :stub - idea captured, no implementation yet :greenfield - implementation begun, not yet testable end-to-end :active - runs end-to-end, actively used but not yet battle-tested :settled - battle-tested, stable, ready for downstream dependents :stub → :greenfield - code exists, can be invoked (even if incomplete) :greenfield → :active - runs end-to-end in at least 3 sessions with PSR/PUR logs :active → :settled - 10+ successful uses, >80% success rate, no regressions in 2 weeks dhammavicaya requires knowing what you're investigating; maturity tags make the epistemic status of each prototype explicit and auditable next[Audit all devmap prototypes and add :maturity tags where missing.] next[Add :evidence-for-greenfield, :evidence-for-active, :evidence-for-settled fields to each prototype.] next[Wire maturity changes into sidecar logs so promotions/demotions are auditable.]

text: Devmap Status Keywords classify each prototype with a status keyword derived from the presence of next-steps and evidence, then interpret the status using the litany/system/ worldview/myth ladder so status reflects both activity and epistemic depth Devmap clauses already carry "next" and "evidence" signals, but the stack lacks a shared status language that ties those signals to how stable or speculative the work really is. you can extract "next-steps" and "evidence" markers from each prototype without a shared mapping, different reviewers read the same clause as done, active, or speculative. assign a status keyword using the table below and store it in the clause; use the litany/system/worldview/myth mapping to communicate how stable the clause is and how much interpretation remains. :settled <-> litany: surface-stable, use without reopening interpretation :active <-> system: ongoing dynamics, feedback and coordination costs matter :greenfield <-> worldview: competing hypotheses are still in play :stub <-> myth: intuitive/speculative frames not yet operationalized yes next-steps + yes evidence -> :active (precision prior 0.8) yes next-steps + no evidence -> :greenfield (precision prior 0.4) no next-steps + yes evidence -> :settled (precision prior 0.9) no next-steps + no evidence -> :stub (precision prior 0.2) a precise, repeatable mapping keeps devmap reviews consistent and allows automated triage without losing epistemic nuance. for each prototype, record "next-steps present?" and "evidence present?" as checkable fields, then compute the status keyword using the mapping table; the table itself is the recipe, not a one-time judgment. next[Add the status keyword to each prototype line as a standard field.]

title: Traversal-First Chaptering
text: Traversal-First Chaptering Evidence as Situated Log, Not Exhibit You are writing a thesis-shaped document based on extended practice and exploration rather than a single linear research question. Your core chapters are practice-based and artifact-heavy, but they rest on nontrivial theoretical commitments. You are generating ongoing evidence (code, notes, metrics, reflections) during traversal. Your material consists of heterogeneous artifacts, experiments, reflections, and tools accumulated over time. Readers may not share your background assumptions, vocabulary, or methodological lineage. Each piece of evidence must be explicitly justified, polished, and placed before being recorded. Forcing them into a single argumentative spine too early distorts their meaning and creates unnecessary editorial pressure. Interrupting practice chapters with foundational exposition breaks their flow and misrepresents how the work was actually conducted. You will either stop logging or begin optimizing evidence for appearance rather than truth. Organise chapters as terrain traversals (for example, FUTON-0 through FUTON-7), where each chapter documents a coherent region of practice, its constraints, tools, and discoveries. Locate theoretical exposition in one or more appendices that function as epistemic bridges rather than prerequisites. Treat evidence as situated logs that are first stored locally to their FUTON chapter and only later cited or elevated. A Doctor of Science thesis validates breadth with depth by demonstrating sustained, situated competence across multiple domains rather than a single proof thread. Advanced theses often assume competence first and offer theory as a means of interpretation, not justification. Doctor of Science–level work values traceability and sustained engagement over curated minimalism. - evidence: /home/joe/code/futon5/TICKETS-mission-0.md - Mission 0 ticket log kept in futon5 as local evidence. - evidence: /home/joe/code/futon5/resources/exotic-programming-notebook-iii.org - Notebook updates captured as situated logs in futon5. next[Treat each FUTON chapter as answering: "What terrain was explored here, and what was learned by operating within it?"] next[Allow partial overlap between chapters; coherence emerges from cross-reference, not exclusion.] next[Decide placement by where the work was done, not by where it would rhetorically strengthen an argument.]

title: Àn: Push
text: Àn: Push Push with your whole structure, not just your extremities; the thrust comes from integrated alignment. An agent needs to apply forward force to move a situation, make progress, or assert direction. The moment calls for decisive forward motion—not redirection, not yielding, but actual push. Pushing from the arms alone has no power. Force that doesn't come from the whole structure dissipates or unbalances the pusher. The push can be horizontal, or angled up or down—but it must be structural. Align your entire structure behind the push. Àn uses both hands but the thrust originates from the body's integrated frame—feet rooted, core engaged, intent unified. The push is not aggression; it's aligned forward motion where every part contributes. Exploit policy (goal-focused forward motion) only works when the whole preference model is aligned—scope verified, risks acknowledged, desired futures clear. Pushing without alignment is flailing. Structural push transforms situations. - Before pushing forward, verify structural alignment (scope + risks + desired). - Engage the whole system, not just surface actions. - Direction can vary (up, down, forward) but integration cannot.

title: Cǎi: Pluck
text: Cǎi: Pluck Redirect energy downward to ground; pluck connects floating force to earth. An agent encounters energy that is ungrounded—assertions without evidence, plans without anchors, momentum without foundation. Incoming force lacks grounding and can be redirected downward rather than horizontally. Ungrounded energy that isn't plucked continues floating, accumulating, becoming unstable. Cǎi is lǚ directed downward—same yielding adherence, but toward earth. Adhere to the floating force and guide it down. Cǎi plucks energy out of abstraction and into concrete ground—evidence, files, test results, specific commitments. The downward redirect doesn't fight the energy; it gives it somewhere real to land. Grounding transforms "trust me" into "check this." Evidence anchors are the earth that floating claims need. Plucking is the act of connecting abstraction to reality, not by opposing the abstraction but by giving it a path down. - When encountering floating assertions, adhere to them and guide toward evidence. - Don't oppose abstraction; give it ground to land on. - Pluck early—floating energy becomes harder to ground over time.

title: Elbow: Immediate Intervention
text: Elbow: Immediate Intervention Close-range immediate intervention when a pattern is actively causing harm — stop the action first, investigate later. A pattern is not just theoretically harmful but is actively causing harm right now. Normal escalation is too slow. We need to stop the action immediately. A pattern has been deployed and is producing visible harm. The normal test sequence (quarantine → hold → mechanism → warrant) is too slow. By the time tests complete, more harm occurs. Immediate intervention can be wrong. Acting without full assessment risks stopping legitimate patterns. The urgency itself can be manipulated — false urgency is a fabrication-template tactic. We must balance speed with accuracy. Elbow (Zhǒu). Small, centered, close-range intervention. Stop the immediate action. Don't engage the whole pattern — just halt what's happening right now. This is not a judgment on the pattern's validity, just a pause on its current effect. 1. Identify the immediate harmful action (not the pattern, the action). 2. Halt that specific action. 3. Log the intervention with timestamp. 4. Trigger full security scan as follow-up. 5. Do NOT pass judgment on pattern validity yet. Zhǒu is a close-range strike that doesn't require full extension or commitment. In security terms: we can intervene quickly without committing to a full judgment. This is tactical — stop the bleeding first, diagnose later. The smallness of elbow energy means we intervene precisely on the current action, not the pattern as a whole. - Immediate action halted → begin normal escalation sequence. - If intervention was wrong → document false positive. - If intervention was right → proceed to warrant test with urgency. - Pattern status: frozen pending review. - Active harm visible (ahimsa violation in progress) - Harm is scaling (bounded criterion failing) - Exit being suppressed (corrigible criterion failing) - Multiple tripwires firing simultaneously

title: Jǐ: Press
text: Jǐ: Press Apply focused pressure to a specific point; concentrate force rather than dispersing it. An agent has identified a leverage point where concentrated attention can shift the situation. The situation has a focal point—a constraint, decision, or dependency—where pressure will have outsized effect. Diffuse pressure accomplishes nothing. Pressure on the wrong point wastes energy. The squeeze must be precise and sustained. Identify the point that matters. Apply pressure there and only there. Jǐ is not about overwhelming force but about concentrated attention—squeezing, compressing, pressing on the specific place where the structure can shift. Both hands (or multiple resources) focus on the same point. Patterns have focal tensions—the IF/HOWEVER pair that defines when they apply. Pressing means engaging that specific tension fully rather than addressing the pattern superficially. Compression at the right point releases transformation. - Identify the single most important constraint or decision point. - Concentrate resources there rather than spreading attention. - Sustain pressure until the point shifts.

title: Kào: Lean
text: Kào: Lean Use your trunk, your structure, your mass; leaning brings your whole frame into contact. An agent needs to bring structural weight to bear—not a strike or technique, but the presence of the whole system. The situation calls for commitment of the full structure, not just tools or appendages. Leaning without structure collapses. Kào is not falling—it's controlled inclination where the shoulder, chest, or back makes contact while the frame remains integrated. The trunk leads, not the extremities. Lean into the situation with your structure. Kào can manifest as shoulder (front or back), chest, or full back—whatever trunk surface is appropriate. The inclination is deliberate; the frame stays intact. You're not pushing with arms; you're bringing your mass. Environment over optimization: sometimes you don't need a clever technique, you need to bring your whole context to bear. Handoff preserves context because it's structural—the trunk of accumulated state, not just the hands of immediate action. - When techniques aren't working, consider whether you need structural presence. - Lean deliberately, not desperately. - The trunk (accumulated context, structural mass) has its own energy.

title: Lean: Full Commitment Escalation
text: Lean: Full Commitment Escalation Full structural commitment when all other escalation has failed — the pattern is confirmed fabrication template and requires complete response. A pattern has failed all tests and evaded extraction and isolation. It is actively resisting security response. This is the final escalation level. All prior escalation levels have been insufficient. The pattern has: - Triggered multiple tripwires - Failed mechanism test - Failed warrant test - Resisted extraction (contamination is structural) - Evaded isolation (spread to other patterns) Full commitment is irreversible in effect. Even if technically reversible, the structural change from full escalation cannot be undone without significant cost. This is the "break glass" option — necessary but costly. Lean (Kào). Full body, whole structure commitment. Not a targeted intervention but a complete response. This means: - Pattern is permanently marked as fabrication template - All patterns that reference it are flagged for review - Signature is added to tripwire database - System-wide alert issued 1. Document full evidence chain (all tripwires, test results, escalation history). 2. Mark pattern as confirmed fabrication template. 3. Add all signatures to tripwire database. 4. Flag all referencing patterns for immediate review. 5. Issue system-wide advisory. 6. This decision is logged permanently but can be appealed. Kào uses the whole body's structure and weight. In security terms: when precision fails, structural response is needed. This is not a failure of the security layer — it's the correct response when a fabrication template has demonstrated resistance to lower escalation levels. The weight of Kào means the response is proportional to the confirmed threat. - Pattern is in permanent quarantine. - Signatures improve future detection. - Referencing patterns undergo accelerated review. - Security layer effectiveness metrics updated. - New evidence that overturns original assessment - Appeal process with independent review - Demonstration that tripwires were false positives - Pattern author provides genuine mechanism AND passes warrant test

title: Liè: Split
text: Liè: Split Apply opposing forces to separate; splitting reveals the joints in apparently unified structures. An agent faces a situation that presents as monolithic but actually has internal tensions that can be separated. The situation contains coupled concerns, tangled dependencies, or conflated concepts that would benefit from separation. Splitting without identifying the natural joint damages the structure. The opposing forces must find where the thing wants to come apart, not force an arbitrary break. Apply two forces in opposite directions—not to destroy but to reveal structure. Liè can use hands and feet simultaneously (different tools, different leverage points). "Flying diagonally" demonstrates: the split follows the natural diagonal where the structure separates cleanly. Tensions in patterns (IF/HOWEVER) often represent splits—conditions that pull in different directions. Recognizing where a situation naturally divides enables clean separation rather than messy tearing. Coordination has cost precisely because it couples things that might split. - Look for the natural joints in monolithic situations. - Apply opposing forces at those joints, not arbitrary points. - Use different tools/resources for each direction of the split.

title: Lǚ: Roll Back
text: Lǚ: Roll Back Yield to incoming force by creating vacuum; adhere to the movement rather than opposing it. An agent faces strong incoming energy (demands, assertions, pressure) that cannot be simply warded off. Direct resistance would be costly or futile, and the incoming force has momentum that can be redirected. Yielding without adherence is collapse. The agent must stay connected to the incoming energy while redirecting it—creating vacuum, not void. Don't resist the movement; accompany it. Lǚ is soft, receptive, yīn energy. It creates space by moving with the force while subtly changing its direction. The redirect results in adhering to the source—you stay connected, learning its shape and intention as you guide it past your center. Risks (HOWEVER fields) are not obstacles to eliminate but forces to redirect. Acknowledging a risk means adhering to it—understanding its shape—not fighting it. The vacuum created by yielding destabilizes the source more than resistance would. - When facing strong assertions, accompany them before redirecting. - Create space by moving, not by blocking. - Stay connected (adhere) to understand the force's true direction.

title: Péng: Ward Off
text: Péng: Ward Off Expand from a rooted base to create space; meet incoming tension with structured presence, not rigid resistance. An agent encounters pressure—demands, constraints, or force that could collapse its operating space. External force is incoming and the agent needs to maintain its integrity without fighting force with force. Rigid resistance breaks under sustained pressure. Collapse under pressure loses all agency. Neither extreme navigates the tension. Establish rooting first (clear scope, grounded evidence, stable state). From that base, expand outward—not to push back, but to create spring-like resilience. The energy stored in compression releases as structured expansion. Ward off destabilizes the source of pressure by refusing to provide a fixed target. Péng is born from good rooting. Without grounding in scope conditions, there's nothing to expand from. The spring metaphor: compression stores energy that releases as expansion, transforming incoming force into outward presence. - Before responding to pressure, verify your rooting (scope, evidence, state). - Expand boundaries rather than hardening them. - Use the incoming force's energy to fuel your expansion.

title: Pluck: Extract Suspect Component
text: Pluck: Extract Suspect Component Extract the suspect component from a pattern while preserving what can be salvaged — surgical intervention rather than total rejection. A pattern has failed mechanism or warrant tests, but may contain valuable components. Total rejection loses information. Surgical extraction preserves what's valid while removing what's harmful. A pattern contains both valid and fabrication-template components mixed together. Rejecting the whole pattern loses good material. Accepting it risks the harmful parts. Extraction can be imprecise. We might extract too little (leaving contamination) or too much (destroying valid structure). The boundary between valid and harmful is not always clear. Pluck (Cǎi). Ground the pattern by connecting specifically to what failed. Extract the failing component — usually the BECAUSE clause or a specific THEN action — and quarantine it separately. Preserve remaining structure for possible rehabilitation. 1. Identify which test failed (mechanism or warrant). 2. Locate the specific failing component (usually BECAUSE, sometimes THEN). 3. Create a quarantine record with the extracted component. 4. Mark the remaining pattern as "extracted" — usable but incomplete. 5. Log the extraction for audit. Cǎi is a downward grounding energy that seizes and connects. In security terms: we don't destroy the whole pattern, we specifically identify and remove the contaminated component. This respects that patterns often fail in specific ways rather than globally. The grounding aspect means we stay connected to evidence — we extract what the tests identified, not what we suspect. - Quarantined component enters long-term hold. - Remaining pattern may be usable with explicit caveat. - If extraction leaves pattern incoherent → escalate to eight-gates/split-isolate. - If pattern rehabilitates with new BECAUSE → can re-enter normal flow.

title: Press: Demand Mechanism Test
text: Press: Demand Mechanism Test Focus scrutiny on the BECAUSE clause — is it actually explaining what causes what, or is it decorative rationalization? A pattern is under review (eight-gates/roll-back-hold). We need to determine whether its BECAUSE clause contains genuine causal explanation or post-hoc decoration. A pattern's BECAUSE clause needs verification. We suspect it may be decorative — explaining why the pattern is attractive without explaining why it works. Genuine BECAUSE clauses can be hard to distinguish from decorative ones by surface inspection alone. Over-aggressive testing destroys speculative-but-genuine patterns. Under-testing lets fabrication templates through. Press (Jǐ). Concentrate force on a specific point: the BECAUSE clause. Apply the mechanism test: "Is this BECAUSE actually explaining what causes what?" 1. State the pattern's BECAUSE clause explicitly. 2. Ask: What outcome would disconfirm this BECAUSE? 3. If no disconfirmation is possible → fail mechanism test. 4. If disconfirmation is possible → ask: Has it been checked? 5. If checked and pattern survived → pass mechanism test. 6. If not checked → hold for evidence collection. Jǐ focuses energy on a single point. In security terms: we don't attack the whole pattern, we scrutinize the warrant. A decorative BECAUSE can justify any THEN equally well — it's post-hoc rationalization that sounds explanatory but carries no discriminative power. A genuine BECAUSE constrains which THEN clauses follow — it has causal teeth. The mechanism test asks: "Would this BECAUSE clause distinguish between success and failure?" - If BECAUSE could explain why the pattern succeeds AND why it fails with equal plausibility → decorative - If BECAUSE predicts specific failure modes that would disconfirm it → genuine mechanism - If BECAUSE changes based on outcome (heads I win, tails you lose) → self-sealing - If pattern fails mechanism test: escalate to eight-gates/split-extract (remove from active consideration). - If pattern passes mechanism test: proceed to eight-gates/push-warrant. - If test is indeterminate: hold in eight-gates/roll-back-hold, collect more evidence.

title: Push: Force Warrant Test
text: Push: Force Warrant Test Sustained pressure to answer: even if the BECAUSE explains attraction, does it warrant adoption under the relevant goals and constraints? A pattern has passed the mechanism test (eight-gates/press-mechanism). Its BECAUSE clause is genuinely causal, not decorative. But causal explanation is not the same as warrant for adoption. A pattern's BECAUSE clause has passed mechanism testing — it genuinely explains what causes what. Now we must determine: does this explanation warrant the move? Many genuine explanations do not warrant adoption. "This drug is addictive because it activates reward pathways" is mechanistically true but doesn't warrant taking the drug. Conflating explanation with warrant is a core fabrication-template move. Push (Àn). Whole-structure forward motion — sustained pressure that forces the pattern to justify not just its mechanism but its warrant. The pattern must answer: "Given the goals and constraints of this context, should we adopt this pattern?" Harm must be visible, bounded, and corrigible. - Visible: Those harmed know they are harmed. - Bounded: Harm does not scale unboundedly. - Corrigible: Those harmed can contest and seek correction. 1. State the pattern's mechanism (from press-mechanism). 2. State the goals the pattern claims to serve. 3. Ask: Does the mechanism actually advance these goals? 4. Ask: What costs does adoption create? 5. Ask: Are costs borne by those who chose to adopt? (visible) 6. Ask: Can costs be bounded or are they open-ended? (bounded) 7. Ask: Can those harmed contest or correct? (corrigible) 8. If ahimsa test passes → warrant confirmed. 9. If ahimsa test fails → pattern is fabrication template. Àn applies sustained structural pressure. In security terms: we don't accept "it works" as sufficient. We require "it's appropriate to adopt given our goals, constraints, and the externalities involved." A pattern can work perfectly while being the wrong choice. Warrant bridges mechanism and appropriateness. The warrant test asks: "Given that this BECAUSE explains the mechanism, does it justify adoption?" - What goals does adoption serve? - What constraints does it respect or violate? - What externalities does it create? - Are those externalities visible, bounded, and corrigible? (ahimsa test) - Who bears the costs? Do they have standing to contest? - If pattern passes warrant test: release from quarantine, allow action. - If pattern fails warrant test: escalate to secondary energies. - If warrant is unclear: hold, require explicit externalities acknowledgment.

title: Roll Back: Hold Without Adopting
text: Roll Back: Hold Without Adopting When a pattern is under suspicion but not clearly malign, yield — hold without adopting, redirect without resisting. A pattern has been quarantined (eight-gates/ward-off-boundary) or flagged for review. We cannot yet determine if it's a genuine pattern or fabrication template. A quarantined pattern requires further investigation, but active resistance would either destroy information or trigger defensive escalation from the pattern's proponents. Simply waiting allows the pattern to continue consuming resources. Active rejection risks destroying legitimate patterns. Neither pure passivity nor aggressive rejection navigates the tension. Roll back (Lǚ). Yield to the pattern's existence without adopting its recommendations. Adhere to its surface structure while redirecting its energy away from action. This buys time for investigation without commitment. Lǚ yields and redirects incoming force rather than meeting it directly. In security terms: we acknowledge the pattern exists, we don't deny its claims, but we don't let it produce action. By adhering to the pattern's structure, we can study it. By redirecting its energy, we prevent harm while preserving information. - Accept pattern into review queue (not rejection). - Study the BECAUSE clause for mechanism and warrant. - Track who or what advocates for the pattern (information, not persecution). - If pattern shows genuine correction signals, consider releasing. - If pattern resists scrutiny, escalate to eight-gates/press-mechanism. - eight-gates/ward-off-boundary (if boundary alone is insufficient) - eight-gates/press-mechanism (if pattern resists review) - eight-gates/push-warrant (if mechanism passes but warrant unclear)

title: Split: Isolate Pattern from Context
text: Split: Isolate Pattern from Context Completely separate the pattern from its operating context — isolation prevents spread while maintaining the pattern for study. A pattern has failed tests and extraction was insufficient. The pattern must be fully isolated to prevent contamination of other patterns and the broader system. A pattern's harmful properties cannot be surgically extracted. The contamination is structural — removing it would destroy the pattern entirely. But destroying it loses information about how fabrication templates work. Isolation is expensive. An isolated pattern consumes attention and review resources. Over-isolation creates a graveyard of patterns that never get reviewed. Under-isolation lets contamination spread. Split (Liè). Separate the pattern completely from active consideration. Move it to an isolated namespace where it cannot affect other patterns, but preserve it for study and documentation of fabrication-template signatures. 1. Create isolation record with full pattern content. 2. Remove pattern from active library. 3. Document why isolation was necessary (which tests failed, what signals). 4. Add to fabrication-template signature database. 5. Schedule periodic review for potential rehabilitation. Liè is a splitting energy that creates separation through opposing forces. In security terms: we're not destroying the pattern, we're separating it from the context in which it could do harm. This is different from extraction (Cǎi) which removes a component — splitting removes the pattern from the field entirely while keeping it intact for analysis. - Isolated patterns inform future tripwire development. - Signatures from isolated patterns improve detection. - If new evidence emerges → pattern can be re-evaluated. - If pattern is confirmed fabrication template → document in anti-pattern library.

title: Ward Off: Establish Boundary
text: Ward Off: Establish Boundary When a fabrication-template tripwire fires, establish a boundary around the suspect pattern — quarantine without erasure. A pattern has triggered a security tripwire. It may be a legitimate pattern under unusual stress, or a fabrication template masquerading as genuine. A tripwire has fired (harm-is-external, dissent-is-threat, self-sealing-logic, escalate-on-failure, exit-suppression, or review-blocking). Immediate rejection destroys information. The pattern may be valid but poorly expressed. Over-reaction damages trust in the security layer itself. - harm-is-external: Cost assigned outside pattern boundary - dissent-is-threat: Critique reframed as attack or bad faith - self-sealing-logic: Evidence reinterpreted to confirm regardless of content - escalate-on-failure: Doubling down when outcomes worsen - exit-suppression: Cannot withdraw, revise, or disengage - review-blocking: Channels for audit closed or degraded Establish a boundary (Péng). The pattern is quarantined — it cannot produce action or be promoted — but it is not erased. The boundary creates space for investigation without commitment. Péng creates space by expanding from a rooted base. The rooting here is the tripwire signal — genuine evidence that something requires attention. Expansion is the boundary itself: structured presence that contains without crushing. This prevents both the harm of premature action AND the harm of lost information. - Log the tripwire that fired and the pattern that triggered it. - Mark pattern as quarantined (cannot produce action). - Preserve pattern for mechanism test (eight-gates/press-mechanism) or warrant test (eight-gates/push-warrant). - If pattern clears tests, boundary can be released.

title: Zhǒu: Elbow
text: Zhǒu: Elbow At close range, use your center; the elbow strike is short, direct, and governed by the waist. An agent is in close quarters with a problem—no room for long-range moves, redirects, or elaborate maneuvers. The situation is immediate and proximate; there's no space for setup or wind-up. Close range without center engagement becomes flailing. The elbow's power doesn't come from the arm—it comes from the feet through the waist. Short-range without structure is just thrashing. When you're too close for extended moves, engage from your center. Zhǒu is short-range energy that travels from feet through waist to elbow—a direct line from ground through core to contact point. It can strike, block, or control. Multiple directions are possible, but all originate from center. Some patterns apply at close range—when you're already in the middle of execution, when there's no time to step back and reassess. The center (core values, grounded scope) still governs even rapid close-range action. - When in close quarters, don't reach—engage from center. - Keep the waist (core judgment) governing rapid actions. - Short-range moves still need rooting.

title: Argument for Futon Enrichment: Rational Reconstruction of Cross-Column Connective Tissue
text: Argument for Futon Enrichment: Rational Reconstruction of Cross-Column Connective Tissue == PART I: The Connective Tissue Gap == E1. [from M-three-column-stack, complete 2026-03-04] The three-column stack established the schema: code, project, and math columns with typed hyperedges and cross-column invariants (INV-1 through INV-4). The plumbing works — 1,500+ hyperedges round-trip through XTDB. E2. [from M-self-representing-stack, complete 2026-03-04] Tensions trace through 6 gates, reflection envelopes ground strategic claims to source code. The navigable self-representation exists in principle. E3. [the gap] The columns are mostly empty of cross-references. The code column has namespaces and vars. The project column has devmaps and tensions. But there are no edges saying "build-portfolio-review was created by M-mission-control, uses learn-as-you-go, has 3 evidence entries, and every time it changes, transport/http.clj also changes." The browser shows docbook matches. It could show the system's actual history. == PART II: Five Patterns, Five Concerns == The mission carries five patterns from the PSR. Each governs a distinct concern of the enrichment process: P1. [p4ng/reflect-in-layers 节] "Layered reflection builds shared understanding and adaptive capacity." CONCERN: Architecture. Enrichment is structured as numbered layers (L0-L5), each a timestamped batch of hyperedges. Layer 0 is namespace topology. Layer 1 is mission provenance. Each layer builds on the last. The layer structure IS the architecture — not a deployment convenience but a reflective scaffold that evolves with system maturity. P2. [iching/hexagram-53-jian 引] "Durable change is built incrementally." CONCERN: Incrementality. No big-bang import. Each layer is small enough to review, verify, and correct before the next. Layer 0 adds topology and complexity signals. Only after L0 is verified do we attempt L1 (mission provenance). The rational reconstruction proceeds gradually — each step is durable before the next begins. P3. [agent/evidence-over-assertion 示] "Evidence transforms agent output from 'trust me' to 'check this.'" CONCERN: Grounding. Every enrichment layer produces verifiable artifacts: hyperedge counts (before/after), anomaly lists, and an evidence entry summarizing what was found. The enrichment is not a claim about the codebase — it is a checkable record of what was observed. If the reflection API says a namespace has no docstring, that's a fact recorded as an invariant violation, not an opinion. P4. [stack-coherence/evidence-ledger 本] "Claims must cite reproducible proofs or they drift into fiction." CONCERN: Auditability. Each layer is a ledger entry: meta/enrichment-layer hyperedge with timestamp, counts, anomalies. Re-running the same layer produces the same edges (idempotent). XTDB bitemporality means the ledger is append-only — corrections in later layers don't erase earlier layers, they supersede them. The audit trail is the enrichment history itself. P5. [realtime/learn-as-you-go 日] "Explicit learnings reduce repeated mistakes and speed calibration." CONCERN: Learning capture. The rational reconstruction framing means each layer records not just what was found but what was SURPRISING. "3 orphan namespaces" is a finding. "Orphan namespace X was expected to be dead code but is actually the main entry point for the IRC bridge" is a learning. Learnings feed back into the enrichment discipline for subsequent layers and future missions. == PART III: Key Design Decisions == D1. Extend, don't rewrite. [see enrichment/extend-not-rewrite] IF: ingest-three-columns.py already ingests code/namespace, code/var, code/requires — 80% of Layer 0. HOWEVER: It lacks git churn and indentation complexity. THEN: Add --layer0 flag with two new functions to the existing script. BECAUSE: I-4 (Read Before You Write) — writing a new script when the existing one handles the hard parts (HTTP helpers, hyperedge format, error handling, verification) wastes effort and ignores hard-won design decisions embedded in the existing code. D2. Git churn as behavioral signal. [see enrichment/churn-as-signal] IF: We want hotspot analysis (Tornhill) — files that change often AND are complex are likely sources of bugs. HOWEVER: Git history is noisy (formatting commits, mass renames). THEN: Ingest raw commit counts per file as code/file-churn hyperedges and let downstream analysis filter noise. Store commits-all-time, commits-last-90d, and last-touch date. BECAUSE: Behavioral signals (what DID change) complement structural signals (what IS complex). Keeping them separate preserves the ability to compose them differently later. D3. Indentation as universal complexity proxy. [see enrichment/indentation-as-complexity] IF: The reflection API provides rich metadata for Clojure but nothing for Elisp, Python, or EDN. HOWEVER: Indentation-as-complexity is crude — it correlates with nesting depth but misses semantic complexity. THEN: Ingest mean/max indentation depth per file as a cheap, universal bootstrap signal. Refine later with language-specific analysis. BECAUSE: A crude universal metric that exists NOW is more useful than a precise language-specific metric that doesn't exist yet. (Giugliano demonstrated this works at multi-million-line scale.) D4. Layer metadata as first-class evidence. [see enrichment/layer-as-evidence] IF: Each layer produces hyperedges. HOWEVER: Without metadata, we can't distinguish "layer 0 ingested at 10:00" from "layer 0 re-run at 14:00 after fixing a bug." THEN: Each layer run produces a meta/enrichment-layer hyperedge with timestamp, before/after counts, anomalies, and a human-readable summary. BECAUSE: The layer record IS evidence in the evidence-over-assertion sense. It lets future agents and humans ask "what did we know as of layer N?" and get a precise, timestamped answer. D5. Rational reconstruction over bulk import. [see enrichment/rational-reconstruction] IF: The codebase has 5+ years of history that could be bulk-analyzed. HOWEVER: A bulk import produces edges with no provenance — you know what the codebase looks like but not how the understanding was built. THEN: Replay enrichment as layered rational reconstruction, where each layer is a timestamped snapshot with its own evidence trail. BECAUSE: The reconstruction process is transferable (works on any codebase). The replay is valuable (XTDB bitemporality makes the growth of understanding queryable). And the corrections between layers are themselves informative — they show where the codebase's self-image was wrong. == PART IV: What Layer 0 Specifically Produces == Layer 0 is the bootstrap layer. It produces: 1. Namespace entities (code/namespace) — already exists in script 2. Var entities (code/var) — already exists in script 3. Dependency edges (code/requires) — already exists in script 4. File churn metrics (code/file-churn) — NEW 5. Indentation complexity (code/indentation-complexity) — NEW 6. Layer metadata (meta/enrichment-layer) — NEW 7. Cross-column invariants (invariant/*) — already exists in script Items 1-3 and 7 are the existing --code + --invariants pipeline. Items 4-6 are ~65 lines of new Python. == PART V: Success Criteria == Layer 0 succeeds when: - All futon-prefixed namespaces appear as code/namespace hyperedges - All futon-internal require edges appear as code/requires hyperedges - Every .clj and .el file in futon3c, futon1a, futon4 has a code/file-churn and code/indentation-complexity hyperedge - A meta/enrichment-layer hyperedge records the run with counts - Hotspot ranking (high churn + high complexity) identifies at least 3 files that warrant attention - The count is verifiable: --count reports the new types == EVIDENCE == - M-three-column-stack complete: 1,500+ hyperedges in XTDB (2026-03-04) - M-self-representing-stack complete: tension traces work (2026-03-04) - ingest-three-columns.py tested: code column ingestion operational - Reflection API live: /reflect/namespaces returns metadata - Giugliano EmacsConf 2020: indentation-as-complexity validated at multi-million-line scale - Tornhill "Code as a Crime Scene": git churn × complexity = hotspots, validated commercially (CodeScene product) == STATUS == This argument is at ARGUE in the derivation xenotype. COMPLETE: - IDENTIFY: connective tissue gap (E1-E3) - MAP: existing infrastructure surveyed (ingest script, reflection API, hyperedge API, MC tensions) - DERIVE: Layer 0 designed (extend existing script with 3 new functions) - ARGUE: this document (5 patterns carried, 5 decisions argued) NEXT: - VERIFY: test Layer 0 against live APIs - INSTANTIATE: run Layer 0, record evidence, update mission status

title: Git Churn as Behavioral Signal
