text: Baldwin Cycle The Baldwin cycle is the engineered form of evolutionary learning: explore (learn within constraints), assimilate (fix successful adaptations into genotype), canalize (remove unnecessary freedom, make success cheap). Named after James Mark Baldwin's insight that learned behaviors can become genetically fixed. In engineering: what starts as runtime adaptation becomes compile-time structure. This is how systems accumulate capability without losing auditability. The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). - Learning without assimilating (ghost capabilities, unreplayable) - Assimilating without canalizing (complexity creep, unstable) - Canalizing prematurely (lock-in before exploration complete) Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. Before: System reaches goal through search After: System reaches goal structurally (no search needed) Evidence: Captured in genotype + invariants + proof trail 1. Local learning reduces global search cost (divide and conquer) 2. Assimilation converts exploration into structural capability (cumulative) 3. Canalization makes repeated success automatic (efficiency) EXPLORATION (Learning) Within fixed exotype constraints, allow phenotype plasticity. - Search, adapt, try variants - Measure outcomes against success criteria - Preserve evidence of what was tried Operations: OBSERVE, PROPOSE_CLAIM, experimental APPLY_CHANGE ASSIMILATION (固化 / Fixation) Compress successful learned behavior back into genotype. - Make replayable, auditable internal representation - Generate pattern, update rule table, extract replayable patch - Attach evidence chain (what worked, why, proof) Operations: VERIFY, PROOF_COMMIT (packaging success as artifact) CANALIZATION (壓縮 / Compression) Remove unnecessary degrees of freedom. - Tighten invariants around success region - Make success cheaper and more reliable - What once required learning now works by default Operations: Strengthen INVARIANT_CHECK, narrow exotype Systems that only execute (no learning) cannot adapt. Systems that only learn (no fixation) cannot accumulate. Systems that only fix (no compression) become brittle. The Baldwin cycle integrates all three. next[Implement Baldwin engine as reusable component for layer interfaces] next[Define metrics for exploration cost vs. canalization benefit]

title: Coordination Protocol (Multi-Agent Handoff)
text: Coordination Protocol (Multi-Agent Handoff) Use an explicit multi-channel handoff protocol with review gates and escalation rules so multi-agent work survives asynchrony instead of dissolving into duplicated effort and lost context. When multiple agents work on related missions, they need coordination. Without explicit handoff protocols, work is duplicated, reviews are skipped, and context is lost between sessions. Multiple agents are assigned to a mission, or a mission requires review by another agent. Agents may be asynchronous (different sessions), have different capabilities (Claude vs Codex), or use different communication channels (Agency, git, files). Apply the ping-pong coordination protocol: HANDOFF-CYCLE: ``` 1. Primary: Complete milestone, emit PUR 2. Primary: Commit + push + notify reviewer 3. Reviewer: Pull + review + emit PSR for review 4. Reviewer: Document findings (approve or request changes) 5. Reviewer: Emit PUR for review outcome 6. If changes needed: handoff back to primary 7. If approved: proceed to next milestone ``` NOTIFICATION-CHANNELS (in priority order): 1. Agency page (sync, immediate response expected) 2. Agency bell (async, notification only) 3. Git commit message with [handoff: agent-id] 4. File-based message (docs/notes/AGENCY-CODEX-BRIEF.md pattern) 5. MUSN chat room HANDOFF-MESSAGE-REQUIREMENTS: - What was completed - What needs review or action - Where to find the changes (commit hash, file paths) - Expected response (approve, review, implement) ESCALATION: - If blocked > 30 minutes: document blocker, notify human - If no response > 1 hour: try alternate channel - If channel broken: fall back to file-based communication When Agency is available: - Register with agent-id via WebSocket - Respond to pages with invoke-fn - Bell for async notifications - Page for sync requests When Agency unavailable: - Use git-based ping-pong - Leave messages in designated files - Poll for changes - Explicit handoffs prevent work from falling through cracks - Review gates ensure quality - Multiple channels provide resilience - Escalation prevents infinite waiting - Verify communication channel is working - Establish handoff protocol with collaborating agent - Document current milestone and next expected action @related futon-theory/agent-contract, futon-theory/mission-lifecycle

title: Counter-Ratchet (Invariant I2)
text: Counter-Ratchet (Invariant I2) I2 (extended): Key counts are monotonically non-decreasing unless explicitly acknowledged deletion occurs. Key counts must not drop unexpectedly. If lyrics count goes from 14 to 4, that's an invariant violation requiring investigation. The counter-ratchet detects regressions before they become silent data loss. Data loss often manifests as count drops: entities that existed no longer exist. The counter-ratchet maintains baselines for critical counts and alerts when they decrease without explanation. The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). Silent data loss -> Detected by count drop Corrupt rehydration -> Detected by startup count check Accidental deletion -> Detected before commit - Ignoring count drops as "probably fine" - Resetting baselines after every operation - Only counting totals, not per-type - Checking counts after commit (too late) Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. - Entity counts by type (songs, lyrics, relations) - Relation counts by type - User/penholder counts - Lab session event counts 1. Pre-operation: Record baseline counts 2. Operation: Execute change 3. Post-operation: Check counts against baselines 4. If drop detected: Check for valid deletion record 5. If no valid deletion: Stop-the-line, report violation `futon1/core/invariants.clj`: Count verification `futon1/startup.clj`: Baseline establishment `futon1/api/middleware.clj`: Pre/post operation checks Data loss is often gradual and silent. 14 -> 13 -> 12 -> ... -> 4. Each small loss seems like noise. The ratchet makes every drop visible and requires explanation. No unexplained regressions. 1. Establish baselines for critical entity types 2. After each operation, compare current counts to baselines 3. If count drops without matching deletion record: VIOLATION 4. If count drops with valid deletion: Update baseline next[Implement count baseline tracking in futon1a] next[Add count verification to rehydration checks]

title: Curry-Howard Operational Principle
text: Curry-Howard Operational Principle Programs are proofs of their specifications. The spec mediates future state into present. In futon theory, every operation is a proof that the intended state is achievable and achieved. The Curry-Howard correspondence reveals that types are theorems and programs are proofs. Futon theory operationalizes this: specifications are claims about future state, and proof paths demonstrate those claims. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. - Untyped code = claims without proof (risky) - Type errors = invariant violations (stop-the-line) - Passing types = verified claims (commit allowed) 1. Declare intent (what future state do we want?) 2. Write spec (formal claim about that state) 3. Implement (construct the proof) 4. Verify (check the proof is valid) 5. Commit (the future state becomes present) - Spec: A claim about what the future state should be - Program: A proof that the spec can be satisfied - Execution: Verification that the proof is valid - Result: The spec-mediated future state, now present When we write: "Entity X will have property P after operation O" We are claiming: There exists a proof path from current state to (X has P) The code is that proof. The test verifies the proof. - Types = Invariants (what must hold) - Functions = Operations (how to maintain invariants) - Type checking = Invariant verification (before commit) - Runtime = Execution (proof in action) Without this correspondence, code is arbitrary text and specs are wishful thinking. With it, code and specs are two views of the same truth. The program proves the spec; the spec justifies the program. next[Formalize spec language for futon1a invariants] next[Connect type-level claims to runtime verification]

title: Durability First (Invariant 0)
text: Durability First (Invariant 0) I0: What you save is what you get back. Persistence is the zeroth invariant: what you save is what you get back. Writes return success ONLY after durable storage confirms. No fire-and-forget. Without reliable persistence, all higher-layer invariants are meaningless. Durability is enforced via invariants (I0), not axioms. The axioms (A1-A5) are operational; durability is structural. The applicability scope of the pattern (see substructure). - Writes return success ONLY after durable storage confirms - Reads return ONLY data that is durably stored - No async-without-callback, no fire-and-forget - All failures throw, no silent logging The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). Storage unavailable -> 503 (service layer error) Write timeout -> 503 (service layer error) Corruption detected -> 500 (blocks startup) - "Write succeeded" before confirmation (async leak) - Catching write errors and returning partial success - Optimistic cache writes without durable sync Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. Layer 0 gates all writes: - Synchronous confirmation before success return - Success returns a durable proof token (e.g., tx-id) - Failure throws with error context, never returns false See `storage/durability-first` for concrete implementation patterns. A storage layer that can't reliably store is violating its reason for existence. Layer 0 errors must surface as Layer 0 errors, not masked by higher-layer failures.

title: Error Hierarchy (Invariant 3)
text: Error Hierarchy (Invariant 3) I3: Errors surface at the layer that caused them. Errors surface at the layer that caused them. No penholder errors when the real problem is durability. Each layer is a gate; lower-layer failures prevent higher-layer code from running. When errors surface at the wrong layer, debugging takes hours instead of minutes. An auth error that masks a storage failure sends you hunting in the wrong codebase. Layer hierarchy ensures the true cause surfaces first. The applicability scope of the pattern (see substructure). - Each layer is a gate; failure stops propagation - Lower layers run before higher layers - Layer N errors must not be masked by Layer N+1 handling - Error context includes: layer, operation, entity ID, expected vs actual The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). Masked error: Auth failure hides storage failure -> bug takes hours to find Wrong layer: 400 when 503 is correct -> client retries uselessly Missing context: "Error" without layer/operation/id -> blind debugging - Catching storage errors and returning auth errors - Running all validations before checking storage health - Generic error handlers that lose layer context - "Something went wrong" without layer identification Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. Middleware orders layer checks from 0 to 4: 1. Can we reach storage? (Layer 0) 2. Is identity valid? (Layer 1) 3. Is data integrity intact? (Layer 2) 4. Is requester authorized? (Layer 3) 5. Is input valid? (Layer 4) Layer 0 (durability) -> 503 Service Unavailable Layer 1 (identity) -> 409 Conflict Layer 2 (integrity) -> 500 Internal Server Error Layer 3 (auth) -> 403 Forbidden Layer 4 (validation) -> 400 Bad Request Debugging is O(layers * complexity) when errors surface at wrong layer, O(1) when they surface at correct layer. The first clue should point to the right file, not send you on a wild goose chase. next[Implement layer-ordered middleware in futon1a] next[Create error catalog mapping every error code to its layer]

title: Event Protocol
text: Event Protocol The event protocol defines the canonical sequence of events in a futon proof path: CLOCK_IN -> OBSERVE -> PROPOSE_CLAIM -> APPLY_CHANGE -> VERIFY -> INVARIANT_CHECK -> PROOF_COMMIT -> CLOCK_OUT. Events are the atoms of auditability. Each event type has defined preconditions and postconditions. The protocol ensures every change follows the same defensible path from intent to durable proof. The applicability scope of the pattern (see substructure). Not every session needs all events. A5 (Minimum Viable Events) allows: - Read-only session: CLOCK_IN -> OBSERVE -> CLOCK_OUT - Quick fix: CLOCK_IN -> OBSERVE -> APPLY -> VERIFY -> COMMIT -> CLOCK_OUT The protocol is the maximum; subsets are valid for simpler operations. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. - On VERIFY failure: Return to OBSERVE, spawn correction path - On INVARIANT failure: Return to OBSERVE, stop-the-line protocol - Session can be abandoned at any point before PROOF_COMMIT 1. CLOCK_IN: Session begins, agent declares identity and intent - Precondition: None - Postcondition: Session ID assigned, timestamp recorded 2. OBSERVE: Read state, gather evidence, build understanding - Precondition: Clocked in - Postcondition: Observations logged, state snapshot available 3. PROPOSE_CLAIM: Agent declares what will change and why - Precondition: Observations made - Postcondition: Claim recorded (not yet applied) 4. APPLY_CHANGE: Execute the proposed change - Precondition: Claim proposed, invariants passing - Postcondition: Change applied to staging area 5. VERIFY: Confirm change matches claim - Precondition: Change applied - Postcondition: Verification result recorded 6. INVARIANT_CHECK: All invariants must pass - Precondition: Verification passed - Postcondition: All invariants confirmed or violations identified 7. PROOF_COMMIT: Durable commit with evidence chain - Precondition: All invariants passed - Postcondition: Change durably committed, tx-id assigned 8. CLOCK_OUT: Session ends, proof path complete - Precondition: Proof committed or session abandoned - Postcondition: Session closed, duration recorded `futon3/lab/session.clj`: Session lifecycle events `futon3/lab/ws.clj`: Event dispatch and logging `futon1/core/`: Layer-specific event handling Unstructured change is unauditable change. The protocol ensures that every mutation has a traceable path. When something breaks, the event log tells the story of how we got here. next[Implement event logging for all protocol phases] next[Add protocol visualization to session replay]

title: Four Types Framework
text: Four Types Framework Four interrelated types describe how structure becomes behavior becomes interface becomes portable pattern: genotype (internal), phenotype (observable), exotype (connectable), xenotype (transplantable). In heterogeneous programming and evolutionary systems, these four types represent different facets of the same transformable system. Each provides a distinct lens for understanding how capability evolves. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. - genotype: Pattern definitions, DSL specs, rule configurations - phenotype: System behavior, test results, API responses - exotype: Layer interfaces (L0↔L1, L1↔L2), event protocol shapes - xenotype: Baldwin cycle itself, applicable at any interface Externally visible type/interface shape. - Interface contracts, data formats, APIs - Signal/control surfaces, I/O types, event protocols - Not behavior itself, but the shape through which behavior connects - What makes components composable The replicable, persistable, versionable internal representation. - Rule sets, programs, pattern DAGs, DSL fragments - Parameter priors, replayable generators - What can be stored and version-controlled - The "recipe" that generates behavior Observable behavior and performance in environment. - Actual outputs, interaction behavior - Test metrics, performance curves - What can be measured and compared - The "result" of executing the genotype xenotype: Cross-domain "generate—select" skeleton ↓ projects to genotype: Concrete instantiation (language/DSL/rule table) ↓ executes as phenotype: Observable performance (measurable) ↔ connects via exotype: Interface shape (wireable) Cross-domain portable control/generation structure. - Meta-CA rules, variational search structures - Categorical wiring, portable generator+selector combinations - A transplantable higher-order embryo - Can be projected onto different genotype forms Conflating these types leads to confusion: optimizing behavior (phenotype) without capturing it (genotype), or defining interfaces (exotype) that don't compose across domains (missing xenotype). Separating them enables systematic evolution with auditability. next[Map existing futon layer interfaces to exotype specifications] next[Identify xenotype structures that can be reused across layers]

title: Futonic Logic: Vocabulary, Composition, and the Recognition Loop
text: Futonic Logic: Vocabulary, Composition, and the Recognition Loop Futonic logic specifies the vocabulary, composition rules, and recognition loop that futon-theory patterns presuppose. It does not replace the patterns; it makes explicit the symbolic operations they perform implicitly. The central insight: composition (鹽) is not concatenation but the recognition that latent potential (鹵) and stabilizing interface (皿) are available under the same decomposition regime (部). The futonic loop — input, decompose, articulate, compose, sense, regulate, act, evaluate — is the abstract form of the PSR→PUR cycle and the derivation xenotype alike. == 0. META-SYNTAX == ⿱ denotes top-bottom composition in glyph space. Futonically, it corresponds to a binary articulation whose abstract form is (CAR . CDR): (meta-syntax (⿱ (role layout-operator) (maps-to cons) (explanation "⿱ denotes top-bottom composition in glyph space; futonically, it corresponds to a binary articulation whose abstract form is (CAR . CDR)."))) This does NOT assert that all composition is binary. It asserts only: when ⿱ appears, interpret it as a historically successful binary articulation, abstractable as a cons pair. Triads, polycentric forms, and n-ary decompositions operate under other 部. == 1. VOCABULARY == Core symbols declared as roles, not definitions. Premature semantic collapse is the vocabulary equivalent of forward-declaration debt (social/verify- before-compose): fixing meaning before structure is verified produces symbols that cannot compose. (vocabulary (象 (role configuration) (note "A structured whole that can be referenced without full expansion. First-class, carryable, transformable.")) (部 (role decomposition-regime) (note "A chosen regime of articulation, not an ontological given. Arity-variable: binary, triadic, polycentric.")) (咅 (role articulation) (note "The act of making a decomposition explicit. Not analysis (which presumes correctness) but perception of structure already present.")) (香 (role embodied-salience) (note "Cross-layer perception that signals without full formalization. Agent-relative. Defeasible.")) (味 (role embodied-evaluation) (note "Selection by felt difference rather than proof. The evaluative counterpart of 香.")) (鹽 (role generative-composition) (note "Composition that generates: not mere juxtaposition but the recognition that potential and container are available under the same 部.")) (鹵 (role latent-substrate) (note "Manipulable potential. What can be transformed if a 皿 is available to receive the result.")) (皿 (role stabilizing-container) (note "Interface, vessel, boundary. What receives and stabilizes the product of transformation.")) (間 (role honest-interval) (note "The structured space between components, perceived without premature filling. 間 is not emptiness — it is the topological fact that an interval exists and has properties that must be read, not generated. Hallucinating content into 間 produces false salience and brittle composition.")) (関 (role gate-relation) (note "Barrier, gate, typed connection. 関 is the structural fact that components are related through constraints, not mere adjacency. A gate pipeline is a chain of 関; a core.logic relation is 関 made evaluable; a typed port (mission-interface-signature) is 関 at a boundary. 関 formalizes what 間 perceives: the interval has structure, and that structure can be traversed or blocked. 間 reads the gap; 関 names the gate. Together (無門関): the gate that dissolves when honestly perceived — tension discovery as navigation.")) (既 (role earned-past) (note "Urðr: that-which-has-come-to-pass. Not mere temporal before, but the load-bearing past — closure-evidence, HEAD-as-escrow, the proof-path's earned record. Citeable, structurally available to the present, and rewritable only with traces. (See futon-theory/wyrd.)")) (化 (role becoming-event) (note "Verðandi: in-process-of-happening, the present participle of weorþan ('to come to pass'). The live writer-action, the consent gate firing, the loop presently composing. Distinct from 未知: 未知 is the epistemic three-valuedness of in-flight state, while 化 is the temporal becoming itself. Every 化 emits (應 . 債).")) (應 (role modal-obligation) (note "Skuld (modal face): the 'ought / shall / should' voice. Cognate with English shall/should via Germanic *skul-. 應 is what the present says about what the future must do; not yet a debt-record but a modal claim. Sorries are stated in the voice of 應.")) (債 (role substantive-debt) (note "Skuld (substantive face): debt incurred. Every act of 鹽 (composition) emits 債 alongside salt-pay (worth, from salarium). sorrys.edn is the registry of 債 at proof-path granularity; mission scope-remaining tracks 債 at mission granularity. 債 outstanding in regime A may be 鹽 generative in regime B — this trans-regime survival is wyrd-salience (futon-theory/wyrd).")) (未知 (role non-equilibrium-interval) (note "Actionable but not predictable. Three-valued logic: the system is neither in its prior state nor in its successor state.")) (非死非活 (role non-terminal-state) (note "System is responsive but not self-sustaining. Equivalent to 未知 at the lifecycle level.")) (🔮 (role regulator) (note "Capacity to act within 未知 while modulating action amplitude. Components: 能 (capacity) + 捨 (setting-down)."))) == 2. COMPOSITIONAL STRUCTURE == 2.1 象 and 部: (象 (status first-class) (properties (carryable transformable)) (note "A structured whole that can be referenced without full expansion.")) (部 (function bounded-decomposition) (arity-variable true) (examples (binary triadic polycentric)) (note "A chosen regime of articulation, not an ontological given.")) 2.2 鹽 as composition: (鹽 (structure (⿱ 鹵 皿)) (abstract-form (cons 鹵 皿)) (interpretation (鹵 (latent manipulable potential)) (皿 (interface container stabilizer))) (constraint "Generativity requires both terms to be available under the same 部.")) 2.3 Salience as the appearance of 鹽: (compositional-salience (depends-on 鹽) (definition "Agent-relative perception that a (鹵 . 皿) decomposition is presently actionable.")) (A7-precondition (if (perceives-間 agent interval)) (then (A7 may proceed: test for 鹵 and 皿)) (else (composition is premature: the interval has not been honestly observed))) (A7 (precondition A7-precondition) (if (exists (鹽 (⿱ 鹵 皿)))) (and (perceivable 鹵) (perceivable 皿)) (then (salience emerges)) (else (generativity remains inert))) 2.4 香 and 味: (香 (role cross-layer-perception) (function "Signals salience without full formalization.")) (味 (role embodied-selection) (function "Evaluates articulations by felt difference rather than proof.")) 2.5 🔮 and 捨: (🔮 (components (能 捨)) (function regulator) (definition "Capacity to act within 未知 while modulating action amplitude.")) (捨 (operation set-down) (precondition (has 🔮)) (effect "Reduce deployed capacity to limit harm while preserving reversibility.")) 2.6 未知 and 非死非活: (未知 (state non-equilibrium) (logic three-valued) (properties (actionable not-predictable))) (非死非活 (equivalence 未知) (note "System is responsive but not self-sustaining.")) 2.7 既 / 化 / 應 / 債 — The Three-Time Decomposition: The three Norns (Urðr, Verðandi, Skuld) constitute a three-time projection of every present moment. See futon-theory/wyrd for the etymological grounding (wyrd ← weorþan ← PIE *wert-) and the Skuld≈SORRY identification. (three-time-decomposition (frame (Norns Urðr Verðandi Skuld)) (glyphs (既 化 (應 . 債))) (note "Decomposes the present moment into already-completed, presently-becoming, and owed-to-the-future aspects. Not a temporal sequence but a simultaneous three-face projection of every loop turn. The Buddhist 三時 (過去/現在/未來) is too neutral here; it loses Skuld's owed character, collapsing future-as-debt into future-as-next.")) (Skuld-pair (structure (⿱ 應 債)) (interpretation (應 (modal voice of obligation: ought, shall)) (債 (substantive record of debt incurred))) (constraint "Premature collapse to 應 alone is anxiety (debt voiced but unrecorded); to 債 alone is bookkeeping (debt without standing modal force). Both faces are required.")) (three-time-rule (each (loop-turn t)) (projects-onto (既 (closure-evidence-available-at t)) (化 (composition-presently-firing-at t)) ((應 . 債) (obligations-emitted-by-firing))) (note "No turn is wholly any one face. Collapse to 既 alone is nostalgia (citing past with no present act); to 化 alone is amnesia (acting without grounding); to (應 . 債) alone is anxiety/accounting without grounding or act.")) 2.8 鹽 / 債 — The Composition-Debt Ledger: Composition has two sides: what it pays (salt, salarium, worth) and what it owes (Skuld, 債, shall). 鹽 (existing §2.2) is the generative side. 債 is the dual obligation side. The pair forms the ledger every loop turn must keep. (compositional-ledger (form (⿱ 鹽 債)) (credit-side (worth "salt-money: the salt-pay") (provenance "Roman salarium → English salary → 'worth one's salt'")) (debit-side (debt 債) (provenance "Germanic *skul- → Old Norse Skuld → English shall/should")) (rule (every-鹽 emits (worth . 債)) (note "No composition completes its bookkeeping in a single 部 — the 債 outstanding in regime A may be the 鹽 generative in regime B. This trans-regime survival IS wyrd-salience (futon-theory/wyrd).")) (cross-linguistic-triangulation (Latin salarium) (Chinese (鹽 債)) (Old-English (wyrd weorþan Skuld-via-Norse)) (note "Three independent linguistic registers triangulate the same ledger structure. The triangulation is itself a wyrd-survival test passing: when the same structure is recovered from three unrelated source languages, it is not an artifact of any one language's idioms."))) (ledger-anti-collapse (anti-pattern "Collapse the ledger to net.") (reason "Net hides structure: 鹽 in regime A and 債 in regime B do not sum to zero — they are the wyrd-salient configuration that the present must continue to turn (vertere) between regimes to keep legible. Net-bookkeeping is the 'mere X' move applied to the ledger itself.")) == 3. THE FUTONIC LOOP == (futonic-loop (input 象) (choose 部) (articulate 咅) (if (forms (鹽 (⿱ 鹵 皿)))) (and (sense 香) (regulate 🔮)) (then (act-within 未知) (evaluate 味)) (else (apply 捨))) 3.1 Three-Time Projection of the Loop: Each loop turn projects onto all three Nornic faces simultaneously. The loop above describes the becoming-firing (化); the three-time projection makes explicit what authorises it (既) and what it emits (應 . 債). (loop-three-time-projection (at-every-turn t (既-at-t (proof-path-history-before-t) (earned-evidence-citeable-at-t) (HEAD-as-escrow-at-t)) (化-at-t (the-rule-itself §3-futonic-loop) (presently-firing 咅) (presently-composing 鹽)) ((應 . 債)-at-t (sorries-registered-during-t) (follow-on-modal-commitments) (discharge-due-by τ)))) (loop-and-ledger (every-step (or 鹽 捨)) (emits ledger-entry (credit (or 香 味-confirms)) (debit (應 . 債))) (note "The futonic loop is a Nornic engine: it inherits 既 as authorisation, composes in 化, emits (應 . 債) as consequence. The else-branch (捨) is explicit handling of obligation without further commitment — the modal 應 'we ought not act' applied to limit 債 accumulation.")) == 4. GROUNDING IN ACTUAL USAGE == Every symbol in the vocabulary has been used (implicitly or explicitly) across futon missions. This section makes those uses explicit. The logic is practical because we have been practising it. 4.1 象 — Configuration | Context | 象 instance | Evidence | | Wiring diagram | coordination-exotype.edn | A structured whole: 6 inputs, 6 outputs, 10 components, 30 edges. Referenceable as ":coordination-exotype" without expansion. | | Flexiarg pattern | mandatory-psr.flexiarg | A structured whole: conclusion, context, IF/HOWEVER/THEN/BECAUSE. Carryable by pattern-id. | | Proof path | gate pipeline output | A structured whole: linked PSR→PUR→PAR chain. Transformable (L1 scans it for tensions). | | Session | Claude Code session | A structured whole: context, tools, history. Compresses (compaction) but remains referenceable. | 4.2 部 — Decomposition Regime | Context | 部 instance | Evidence | | Three-futon split | timescale decomposition | 部 = timescale boundaries (social/task/glacial). Not chosen but perceived (symbolic-individuation). | | Gate pipeline | six-gate decomposition | 部 = the six gates G5→G0. Binary at each gate (pass/reject), hexadic in composition. | | Derivation xenotype | six-step decomposition | 部 = IDENTIFY→MAP→DERIVE→ARGUE→VERIFY→INSTANTIATE. Sequential, not arbitrary. | | Baldwin cycle | triadic decomposition | 部 = NAMING→SELECTION→CANALIZATION. Three phases, not two or four. | 4.3 咅 — Articulation | Context | 咅 instance | Evidence | | PSR | pattern selection | The agent makes a decomposition explicit: "I will use this pattern for this task." | | ARGUMENT.flexiarg | claim composition | Each S/R/T/C section articulates: makes a claim's structure visible. | | Mission scoping | scope in/out | The mission author articulates: what's inside, what's outside. | | Git commit | change articulation | The commit message articulates: what changed and why. | 4.4 鹽 — Generative Composition (鹵 + 皿) | Context | 鹵 (potential) | 皿 (container) | 鹽 (composition) | | Gate pipeline | Pattern library (potential approaches) | Gate shapes (Malli schemas) | Validated proof-path (generative: produces evidence) | | L1 canonicalizer | Observed tensions (potential patterns) | Library format (flexiarg structure) | New pattern in library (generative: constrains future work) | | Social exotype | Agency/realtime patterns (potential requirements) | Wiring diagram format (edn structure) | Validated social-exotype.edn (generative: enables implementation) | | Session | Prior knowledge + context | PSR/PUR protocol (recording structure) | Auditable session (generative: feeds glacial loop) | 4.5 香 — Embodied Salience | Context | 香 instance | Evidence | | Pattern search | futon3a notions/compass | Signals "this pattern might apply" without proving it. ANN + GloVe similarity, not logical implication. | | Hotword matching | patterns-index.tsv hotwords | "deliver" fires on "delivery-receipt" — salience signal, not identification. | | Tension scanning | L1-observe structural-irritation | "This gap-PSR has appeared 3 times" — cross-layer perception that something recurs, without naming what. | | Git archaeology | commit pattern recognition | "These 5 commits all fix forward-declarations" — perceiving a pattern before it has a name. | 4.6 味 — Embodied Evaluation | Context | 味 instance | Evidence | | PUR | pattern use record | Evaluates by outcome (prediction-error), not by proof. "Did using this pattern help?" is 味, not formal verification. | | Mana bins | sospeso confidence bins | p ∈ {0.3, 0.6, 0.8, 0.95} — discrete bins to "reduce self-deception." Evaluation by felt confidence, not computed probability. | | ct/mission.clj | 8/8 checks pass | Evaluation by structural test, not semantic proof. The diagram is well-formed; whether it's the right diagram is 味. | | Code review | Codex review comments | "This could be more defensive" — evaluative judgement, not provable claim. | 4.7 🔮 — Regulator (能 + 捨) | Context | 能 (capacity) | 捨 (setting-down) | 🔮 (regulation) | | Sospeso protocol | Confidence p · C spent on action | (1-p) · C donated to pool + blast radius note | Proceed at lower confidence with bounded harm | | Gate rejection | Pipeline can process the request | Gate rejects with typed error + gate attribution | Fail fast, preserve reversibility | | Mission parking | Team could continue the subsystem | :active → :blocked with recorded blocker | Explicit exit over silent abandonment | | Context compaction | LLM has N tokens of context | Older context compressed to summary | Continue operating with reduced but sufficient state | 4.8 未知 / 非死非活 | Context | Instance | Evidence | | Abandoned missions | Forum: 8 commits, no exit, no :blocked | Neither done (:done) nor explicitly blocked (:blocked). Responsive to git log but not self-sustaining. | | Sospeso interval | Between action and verification | The action has been taken (at p < 0.95) but outcome is not yet verified. System is in 未知. | | futon3c pre-implementation | ARGUMENT written, exotype validated, no code | The social loop is specified but not instantiated. Non-equilibrium: the argument creates obligations the code hasn't satisfied. | | Context boundary | Between session compaction and new turn | The LLM has lost detailed context but retains summary. Actionable but not fully predictable. | 4.9 間 — Honest Interval | Context | 間 instance | Evidence | | Tension discovery | gap between devmap component and mission inventory | Tension browser reads 間: "peripheral-gauntlet/C-arena has no mission." The gap is structural, not empty — it has a devmap, a gate position, dependencies. Reading it honestly (not filling it) produces the correct next action. | | futon1→futon1a porting | gap between declared invariants and implementations | "entity-lifecycle and referential-integrity were not ported." 間 perceived too late: the gap was filled with the assumption "it was ported" — false salience from hallucinated content. | | A7-precondition | interval between 鹵 (potential) and 皿 (container) | Before composing, perceive whether the interval actually exists. A pattern library and a recording protocol may be adjacent without composing — 間 is the honest observation that composition hasn't happened yet. | | Code→docs hypergraph | gap between computed links and persisted links | futon4's finder strategies compute links in Emacs hash tables. 間 is the honest observation that the links are not persisted — the gap between working model and durable fact. | 4.10 関 — Gate / Relation | Context | 関 instance | Evidence | | Peripheral gauntlet | G0→G7 gate pipeline | Each gate is a 関: a typed barrier with acceptance criteria. C-arena (Gate 0) must pass before C-umwelt (Gate 1) can begin. The chain of 関 IS the peripheral gauntlet. | | core.logic relations | `coverso`, `componento`, `invarianto` | Each pldb/db-rel is a 関: a typed connection between facts. `(coverso mid comp-id)` IS the gate between "component exists" and "component is addressed." | | mission-interface-signature | typed input/output ports | Every port is a 関 at a boundary: what the system exposes, typed, constrained. A box with no typed ports cannot participate in composition — missing 関. | | Hyperedge endpoints | `devmap:X`, `component:X/Y`, `mission:Z` | Each endpoint is a 関 connecting the hyperedge to the entities it relates. Queryable: "find all 関 that touch component C-arena." | | Tension→path trace | claim → mission → evidence → var → source | The full path is a chain of 関: each step is a typed gate. When all gates pass (can be traversed), the claim is grounded. When a gate blocks, that's a tension. | 4.11 間 + 関 → 無門関 (The Gateless Gate) Tension discovery is 間 + 関 composed: read the gap honestly (間), then traverse the gate structure (関) to find what the gap implies. The "gateless gate" is not the absence of gates — it is the perception that the gate dissolves when the interval is honestly read. The tension "C-arena has no mission" IS the gate: traversing it (proposing the mission, tracing the path) is how it opens. The barrier and the path are the same structure seen from different sides of 間. In operational terms: `query-uncovered-components` (core.logic) reads 間 relationally; `trace-tension-path` (futon3c) traverses the chain of 関 from tension to source. The composition of these two operations IS the self-representing stack's discovery loop — and it should be invocable on demand, not performed ad hoc. 4.12 既 — Earned Past (Urðr) | Context | 既 instance | Evidence | | Proof path | committed PSR→PUR→PAR chain | The chain is 既: citeable as authority, extensible by future loops, rewritable only with explicit trace | | HEAD-as-escrow | git HEAD as held-truth | HEAD is 既 in the most literal sense: what has come to pass, held as the present's grounding | | Closure evidence | mission-close artifact | Closure freezes a 化 into citeable 既; the closure record is the artifact through which future loops cite the closed mission | | Library canonicalization | promoted flexiarg | Promotion turns a candidate-pattern into 既: subsequent loops cite it as ground rather than candidate | | Frozen tape (piano roll) | append-only PSR/PUR/PAR log | The roll IS the Urðr-surface: what cannot be un-done, only added to | 4.13 化 — Becoming Event (Verðandi) | Context | 化 instance | Evidence | | Live writer-action | VSATARCS-writer presently firing | The act of composition is 化: not yet 既, not yet emitting 債, but in the act | | Consent gate firing | gate evaluating an action class | The firing moment IS 化: not the gate's config (genotype) nor its outcome (phenotype), but the becoming-event | | PSR being authored | agent presently choosing a pattern | The choosing is 化; the recorded choice is 既; the verification obligation is (應 . 債) | | Loop turn | one execution of the futonic loop | Each turn IS 化 for the duration of its firing; afterward it has become 既 | | M-live-geometric-stack | the live geometric surface | The Verðandi-surface of the futon stack: live (T, ∇, Δ, drift) | 4.14 應 / 債 — Owed Obligation (Skuld) | Context | 應 instance | 債 instance | Evidence | | sorrys.edn | "we should X" voice in entry text | typed debt record with :kind | 應 is the modal voice; 債 is the structural debt the registry tracks | | Mission scoping | "this mission shall deliver Y" | uncompleted scoped commitments | 應 in scope language; 債 in scope-remaining accounting | | Pattern next-steps | next[…] entries | unfulfilled pattern-promises | Modal commitments (應) become structural debts (債) if not discharged | | Wiring obligations | invariant statement | broken invariant under load | 應 declares what should hold; 債 is what actually breaks | | sorrys.edn :kind | :prototyping-forward vs :technical-debt | distinct debt-classes | 債 typed by :kind; collapse to one class hides regime distinctions | == 5. THE FUTONIC LOOP IN PRACTICE == The abstract loop (§3) maps onto three concrete cycles: 5.1 PSR→PUR cycle (per-task): (futonic-loop (input 象 := task request entering the gate pipeline) (choose 部 := select decomposition: which gate, which timescale) (articulate 咅 := write PSR: choose a pattern, commit to an approach) (if (forms 鹽) := pattern (鹵) + evidence shape (皿) compose) (and (sense 香) := during execution, perceive whether it's working) (and (regulate 🔮) := stay within budget, reject if budget exceeded) (then (act-within 未知 := execute under uncertainty) (evaluate 味 := write PUR: evaluate outcome by felt difference)) (else (apply 捨 := reject at gate, park mission, write PAR))) 5.2 Derivation xenotype (per-mission): (futonic-loop (input 象 := domain to be derived: "social coordination") (choose 部 := IDENTIFY the decomposition regime: git archaeology, pattern audit, devmap review) (articulate 咅 := MAP + DERIVE: articulate patterns and requirements from the evidence) (if (forms 鹽) := ARGUE: requirements (鹵) + argument structure (皿) compose into a valid case) (and (sense 香) := during argument construction, perceive convergences) (and (regulate 🔮) := VERIFY: check invariants, validate diagrams) (then (act-within 未知 := INSTANTIATE: build the code) (evaluate 味 := tests pass, 8/8 checks, round-trip proof)) (else (apply 捨 := park mission, record blocker, explicit exit))) 5.3 Glacial loop (per-library-evolution): (futonic-loop (input 象 := accumulated proof paths from many tasks) (choose 部 := L1-observe: which tension criterion to scan? structural-irritation / pre-symbolic-pressure / trans-situational-reappearance) (articulate 咅 := name the tension: a recurring pattern emerges) (if (forms 鹽) := tension observation (鹵) + flexiarg format (皿) compose into a candidate pattern) (and (sense 香) := does this tension appear across contexts?) (and (regulate 🔮) := does it meet the canonicalization threshold? frequency >= 3, contexts >= 2) (then (act-within 未知 := write new flexiarg to library) (evaluate 味 := subsequent G3 accepts the new pattern)) (else (apply 捨 := tension does not meet threshold, record but do not canonicalize))) == 6. RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING PATTERNS == | This specification | Existing pattern | Relationship | | 象 as first-class configuration | symbolic-geodesic | 象 IS the structured whole that geodesics traverse | | 部 as decomposition regime | symbolic-individuation | 部 IS the regime under which compound symbols individuate | | 鹽 = (⿱ 鹵 皿) | symbolic-individuation §THE-FUTONIC-VIEW | Same structural analysis, now formalized as composition rule | | 香 as cross-layer perception | structural-tension-as-observation | 香 IS the pre-symbolic pressure before tension is named | | 味 as embodied evaluation | retroactive-canonicalization | 味 IS the selection criterion in the Baldwin cycle | | 🔮 = (能 . 捨) | sospeso protocol (futon5/AGENTS.md) | 🔮 IS the regulator that the sospeso protocol implements | | 未知 / 非死非活 | explicit-exit-over-abandonment | 非死非活 IS the zombie-mission state that the pattern diagnoses | | 間 as honest-interval | structural-tension-as-observation | 間 IS the perception that a gap has structure, before naming what fills it | | 関 as gate-relation | mission-interface-signature | 関 IS the typed boundary that mission ports formalize; core.logic relations are evaluable 関 | | 間 + 関 = 無門関 | tension discovery loop (M-self-representing-stack) | The discovery loop IS 間-reading composed with 関-traversal: perceive gap, navigate gate chain | | futonic-loop | proof-path event-protocol | The loop IS the abstract form of CLOCK_IN → ... → CLOCK_OUT | | 既 / 化 / 應-債 | futon-theory/wyrd (the three Norns) | The three-time decomposition IS the Nornic frame; wyrd grounds the modality, futonic-logic formalises the projection | | 鹽 / 債 ledger | sorrys.edn (registry) + futon-theory/wyrd | sorrys.edn IS the 債 side of the ledger; the 鹽/債 pair is the structural fact wyrd names | == 7. AXIOM A7: COMPOSITIONAL SALIENCE == The existing axioms (A1-A5) are operational. A7 is perceptual: (A7-precondition (if (perceives-間 agent interval)) (then (A7 may proceed: test for 鹵 and 皿)) (else (composition is premature: the interval has not been honestly observed))) (A7 (precondition A7-precondition) (if (exists (鹽 (⿱ 鹵 皿)))) (and (perceivable 鹵) (perceivable 皿)) (then (salience emerges)) (else (generativity remains inert))) In operational terms: a pattern library (鹵) and a recording protocol (皿) may both exist without generating anything — until an agent perceives that they compose under the current decomposition regime (部). Salience is the moment of that perception. The gate pipeline does not create salience; it provides the 皿 that makes 鹵's potential actionable. The agent's PSR is the 咅 that recognizes the composition. This axiom explains why Agency/Forum/Drawbridge failed: the components existed (鹵 was present) but the recording protocol did not (皿 was absent — no typed evidence shapes, no proof-path store). Without 皿, composition could not form. Without composition, salience could not emerge. Without salience, the agents could not perceive when their coordination was or was not working. The result was 非死非活: systems responsive but not self- sustaining, eventually abandoned without exit. == 8. BOUNDARY RULE: 味→未@0 == When evaluation approaches a boundary, it collapses into uncertainty. The correct response is containment, not force. (rule-card 味→未@0 (when (approach boundary)) (then (collapse (味 → 未)) (bias-toward (戒 圍 包))) (therefore (prefer (small reversible moves)) (avoid (irreversible commits)))) Vocabulary for the bias targets: - 戒 (jiè): precept, restraint — the discipline of not-acting - 圍 (wéi): enclosure, surround — contain the blast radius - 包 (bāo): wrap, contain — package the uncertainty for later This rule governs the transition from the futonic loop's "evaluate" phase to the "else" branch. When 味 (embodied evaluation) reaches the edge of what can be evaluated with confidence, the system does not push through — it recognizes it has entered 未知 (non-equilibrium) and shifts to containment mode. Grounding in practice: | Context | Boundary | 味→未 collapse | 戒/圍/包 response | | Sospeso | p drops below 0.95 | Evaluation becomes uncertain | Rescope-to-safety, blast radius note, reversible action only | | Gate rejection | G3 can't find pattern | Evaluation of approach is impossible | Typed rejection with gate attribution; don't execute | | Mission parking | Subsystem hits blocking failure | Evaluation of progress becomes 非死非活 | :active → :blocked with recorded blocker; don't abandon silently | | L1 canonicalizer | Tension below threshold | Evaluation of pattern candidacy is premature | Record but do not canonicalize; wait for more evidence | | Context compaction | Context window approaches limit | Full evaluation of history is no longer possible | Compress to summary; preserve actionable structure, release detail | The rule card is the futonic dual of the sospeso protocol. The sospeso protocol is operational (confidence bins, mana accounting, blast radius notes). The rule card is structural: it says WHEN the transition happens (味 approaches boundary) and WHAT the bias should be (戒/圍/包), without prescribing HOW (that's domain-specific). A7 says: composition requires perceiving both 鹵 and 皿. 味→未@0 says: when you can no longer perceive clearly, stop composing and start containing. A7 opens the door; 味→未@0 knows when to close it. next[Extend the vocabulary as new symbols emerge from practice — this specification is open, not closed] next[Verify that A7 is consistent with A1-A5 (no contradiction, complementary scope)] next[Test whether the futonic loop can serve as a template for AGENTS.md instructions] next[Connect to futon3a search: 香 operations map to notions/compass similarity queries]

title: Interface Loop
text: Interface Loop Each layer interface can host a Baldwin-style loop: the interface serves as both exotype constraint and selection pressure injection point. This enables cumulative functional gain at every boundary. In layered futon architecture (L0 → L1 → L2 → ...), each layer boundary is an opportunity for local learning. Instead of one global training phase, Baldwin cycles run at each interface, accumulating improvements incrementally. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. Same InterfaceLoop structure works at: - L0↔L1: Storage/identity interface - L1↔L2: Identity/integrity interface - L2↔L3: Integrity/auth interface - Any future layer boundary See mission docs for concrete interface loop definitions at each boundary. Each interface Ii between Li and Li+1: 1. Exotype: Defines allowed signal shapes, types, protocols, resources 2. Selection pressure: What succeeds/fails at this boundary For interface Ii: 1. INTERFACE CONSTRAINT (exotype): - Allowed signal shapes, type contracts - Protocol requirements, resource bounds - What must hold for messages to pass 2. EXPLORATION SPACE (phenotype plasticity): - Parameter adjustments, local rule variants - Strategy switching, micro-refactoring - Optional: adapter phenotypes for runtime learning - Constraint: Must not violate exotype 3. ASSIMILATION (genotype writeback): - Successful adaptation strategies compiled back - New patterns generated, rule tables updated - Replayable patches with evidence attached 4. COMPRESSION (invariant strengthening): - "What once required learning" becomes structural - Tests/invariants circle the success region - Exotype tightens, undefined behavior shrinks 1. LOOP_START (interface, initial exotype hash) 2. EXPLORE_ATTEMPT* (variant tried, outcome measured) 3. ADAPT_SUCCESS (strategy that worked, evidence) 4. ASSIMILATE (genotype change, proof commit) 5. CANALIZE (invariant tightened, exotype narrowed) 6. LOOP_END (interface, final exotype hash, gain metric) Global optimization is expensive and opaque. Local optimization at interfaces is tractable and auditable. The interface loop converts every boundary into a learning/accumulation opportunity. Each interface loop produces an evidence package: - Exploration: OBSERVE, PROPOSE_CLAIM events with outcomes - Adaptation: APPLY_CHANGE events with before/after - Fixation: PROOF_COMMIT with success strategy - Compression: Invariant updates, exotype changes Interface gain = (cost_before_canalization - cost_after) / exploration_cost Positive gain: Canalization paid off Negative gain: Exploration wasn't worth it (learn from this)

title: Local Gain Persistence Invariant
text: Local Gain Persistence Invariant LocalGainMustEitherPersistOrBeDeleted: For any interface loop that produces gain G: - Either G is assimilated (genotype updated, PROOF_COMMIT with evidence) - Or G is explicitly deleted (REMOVE_GAIN with reason) - Never: G exists only in runtime/phenotype Any functional gain introduced at an interface must either be assimilated into genotype (replayable, auditable) or explicitly deleted. No ghost capabilities allowed. Interface loops produce functional gains - adaptations that work better than before. Without this invariant, gains can exist in runtime state but never be captured, creating "ghost capabilities" that work but cannot be audited, replayed, or trusted. The applicability scope of the pattern (see substructure). To count as "deleted", gain must have: - Explicit REMOVE_GAIN event - Reason (why not persisting: not worth it, superseded, etc.) - Cleanup verification (no residual effects) To count as "persisted", gain must have: - Genotype change (replayable representation) - Evidence chain (what problem it solved) - Proof commit (durable, with tx-id) - Test coverage (verifies gain still works) The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). - "It just started working" (ghost gain, no genotype) - "We'll capture it later" (procrastinated persistence) - "Nobody uses that anymore" (orphaned gain, not deleted) - Runtime-only optimizations that survive restart Without this invariant: - System works better but nobody knows why - Restart loses the improvement - Can't replicate success in other environments - Can't audit what changed - Can't roll back if it causes problems later Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. 1. LOOP_END event requires disposition field: {persisted, deleted} 2. If persisted: genotype diff + proof commit must exist 3. If deleted: reason + timestamp recorded 4. If neither: INVARIANT_CHECK fails, stop-the-line Accumulated capability is the product of engineering. If capabilities exist but aren't captured, the product is ephemeral. This invariant ensures that every gain either becomes permanent structure or is acknowledged as temporary and removed. next[Add gain disposition field to LOOP_END event schema] next[Implement persistence check in interface loop middleware]

title: Minimum Viable Events (Axiom A5)
text: Minimum Viable Events (Axiom A5) Log the minimum events required for full auditability. Not every keystroke, but every decision point. The goal is defensibility, not surveillance. Event logging has overhead. Too few events lose audit trail; too many create noise and performance drag. A5 defines the threshold: log what's needed for proof paths, no more. The applicability scope of the pattern (see substructure). - Session boundaries (CLOCK_IN, CLOCK_OUT) - State changes (APPLY_CHANGE, PROOF_COMMIT) - Decision points (PROPOSE_CLAIM, pattern selection) - Failures (invariant violations, verification failures) - Observations that led to changes (evidence links) - Intermediate edits before commit - Keystroke-level interactions - Read operations that don't influence changes - Internal system state transitions Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. A5: Log the minimum events required for full auditability. - Storage: Events are append-only, grow linearly - Performance: Event logging should not block operations - Noise: More events = harder to find signal - Pruning: Old events can be archived after audit period Given only the logged events, can you: 1. Reconstruct what was intended? (intent from PROPOSE_CLAIM) 2. Verify what was done? (action from APPLY_CHANGE) 3. Confirm the outcome? (result from PROOF_COMMIT) 4. Attribute responsibility? (agent from session) 5. Diagnose failures? (error context from failures) If yes to all: sufficient events. If no to any: add the missing event type. Auditability is a requirement, not an option. But bloated logs are unreadable logs. A5 threads the needle: enough for proof, no more for comfort. next[Define canonical event types for futon1a] next[Implement event pruning for archived sessions]

title: Mission Dependency Graph
text: Mission Dependency Graph Represent missions as an explicit dependency graph so blocked work, leaf work, and high-value unblocks are visible before agents spend effort in the wrong place. Missions rarely exist in isolation. They block and enable each other, share prerequisites, and compete for resources. Without explicit dependency tracking, agents work on blocked missions or miss opportunities to unblock others. You are planning work across multiple missions or diagnosing why a mission is stuck. Dependencies can be circular (requiring negotiation), soft (preferred but not required), or discovered late. The graph must be maintainable. Model missions as a directed acyclic graph (DAG): RELATIONSHIP-TYPES: - blocks: Mission A must complete before Mission B can start - enables: Mission A completion makes Mission B easier (soft) - shares: Missions A and B share a resource or decision - parent-child: Mission A spawned Mission B (split) REPRESENTATION: In mission docs: ``` Blocked-by: M-other-mission.md Enables: M-downstream.md ``` CONSTRAINTS: - No orphan missions (every mission linked to at least one other or to root) - No cycles in "blocks" relationships - Blocked missions must cite specific blocker - When blocker completes, blocked mission notified PRIORITY-INFERENCE: - Missions that unblock many others have higher priority - Leaf missions (no blockers) can proceed immediately - Root missions (no dependents) may be deprioritized The mission graph can be rendered: ``` M-futon1a-rebuild ├── blocks → M-futon1a-migration └── enables → M-pattern-inference-engine M-make-agency-work-properly └── blocks → M-codex-parity ``` - Explicit dependencies prevent wasted work on blocked missions - Graph structure enables priority inference - Unblock propagation accelerates overall progress - Shared resources surface coordination needs - Audit mission docs for dependency declarations - Build mission graph from declarations - Identify leaf missions (unblocked, can work now) - Identify high-value unblock targets @related futon-theory/mission-lifecycle, futon-theory/mission-scoping, futon-theory/mission-interface-signature

title: Mission Interface Signature (Boundary Types)
text:
Mission Interface Signature (Boundary Types) Every mission must declare a non-empty interface signature - typed inputs, typed outputs, and their wiring - so internally correct work can actually compose with the rest of the stack. Missions that specify internal correctness (invariants, gates, proofs) but not boundary types (what the system exposes) will produce systems that work internally but cannot be composed with anything. The futon1a rebuild demonstrated this failure mode: 5 invariants, 9 tension resolutions, 82 tests — but the API contract was never specified. The system verified itself but couldn't describe what it offered. In wiring diagram terms: the internal morphisms were well-composed but the output ports were unspecified. A box with no typed ports cannot participate in composition. You are writing a mission document, or reviewing one that has reached the :scoped or :active state. Not all output ports are known at mission start. Discovery during implementation may reveal new boundary types. The signature should be updated when this happens — but it must never be empty. Every mission document must include an Interface Signature section with typed input and output ports: 1. INPUT-PORTS Each port specifies: - Name: what the input is called - Type: the shape of the data (schema, format, contract) - Source: where it comes from (another system, user, file) - Description: what it carries 2. OUTPUT-PORTS Each port specifies: - Name: what the output is called - Type: the shape of the data (contract reference or inline) - Consumer: who uses this output - Description: what it provides 3. COMPOSITION-CONSTRAINT Every output port must be: (a) Specified in the mission's technical specification (section ref) (b) Implemented in code (module reference) (c) Tested (at least one test exercises the port) (d) Documented (in the spec, not just in code comments) If an output port exists in code but not in the spec, that is a stop-the-line violation (futon-theory/stop-the-line). 4. FIDELITY-CONTRACT (required for all missions) Every mission must declare a baseline and track fidelity against it: (a) Baseline capability inventory: - donor missions: donor behavior (feature, shape, known consumers) - greenfield missions: declared spec commitments (ports, behavior, and semantic/query layer) (b) Preservation contract: `preserve`, `adapt`, or `drop` per feature (c) Tripwire tests for each `preserve` feature: - must fail on pre-implementation target state - must pass after implementation (d) Latent dependency/omission probe: - donor missions: static call-sites + runtime traces - greenfield missions: consumer scenario probes against declared spec unresolved findings converted into explicit preserve/drop decisions If a baseline feature is neither preserved nor explicitly dropped, this is a stop-the-line violation. Every mission must include a wiring diagram (mermaid) alongside the port tables. The diagram is the primary artifact — the tables are the machine-readable shadow. The diagram shows: - Input ports on the left (what enters the system) - Internal composition in the center (how components connect) - Output ports on the right (what the system exposes) - Typed edges (what flows along each wire) The diagram catches gaps that tables miss. A box with no outgoing wires to the output region is visibly incomplete. A table row is easy to forget; a blank region in a diagram is hard to ignore. The diagram should be created at mission :scoped state and updated at each prototype gate. Each prototype may add new output ports or refine internal composition — the diagram tracks this evolution. DIAGRAM-DISCIPLINE: - Draw the output ports FIRST. What does the system expose? If you cannot name the output ports, the mission is not scoped. - Then draw the input ports. What does the system consume? - Then draw the internal composition. How do inputs become outputs? - Every output port must have at least one path from an input port through internal components. Orphan outputs are unimplementable. - Every internal component that has no path to an output port is either dead code or a missing output port. Both are bugs. ```markdown ## Interface Signature ### Mission Diagram ```mermaid graph LR subgraph inputs I1[input-name
type] I2[input-name
type] end subgraph system-name C1[Component] --> C2[Component] C2 --> C3[Component] end subgraph outputs O1[output-name
type / spec-section] O2[output-name
type / spec-section] end I1 --> C1 I2 --> C1 C3 --> O1 C3 --> O2 ``` ### Input Ports | Port | Type | Source | Description | |------|------|--------|-------------| | ... | ... | ... | ... | ### Output Ports | Port | Type | Consumer | Description | |------|------|----------|-------------| | ... | ... | ... | ... | ### Composition Constraint Every output port must be: 1. Specified in the technical specification (section reference) 2. Implemented in code (module reference) 3. Tested (at least one test exercises the port) 4. Documented (in the spec, not just code comments) ### Fidelity Contract (all missions) | Capability | Baseline Ref (donor/spec) | Contract | Tripwire Test | Notes | |------------|-----------------------------|----------|---------------|-------| | ... | ... | preserve/adapt/drop | test id/path | ... | ``` At each checkpoint, verify both manually and by machine. Manual: - Every output port in code has a spec section reference - Every output port in spec has at least one test - No unspecified output ports exist in code - No uncategorized baseline capabilities - Every `preserve` capability has a tripwire test - Data-shape, behavior, and semantic/query layers are all tracked Machine (futon5.ct.mission): - Maintain an EDN mission diagram alongside the mermaid diagram (see futon1a/docs/mission-diagram.edn for the reference exemplar) - Components are morphisms: declare :accepts (domain) and :produces (codomain), not just :type (identity) - Run `(futon5.ct.mission/validate diagram)` at every prototype gate - All five checks must pass: completeness, coverage, no orphan inputs, type safety, spec coverage - `(futon5.ct.mission/diagram->mermaid diagram)` regenerates the human-readable mermaid from the EDN; keep them in sync - Fidelity check must fail when: - capability inventory contains uncategorized entries - a `preserve` entry has no linked failing-then-passing test - latent dependency findings are unresolved - semantic/query fidelity for an exposed capability is unspecified If verification fails, the checkpoint is blocked until the spec catches up with the code. - Internal correctness without boundary specification produces systems that cannot be composed, integrated, or replaced - Typed ports force the mission author to think about what the system *presents*, not just what it *does internally* - The composition constraint catches the exact failure mode observed in futon1a: code that exists without specification - Wiring diagrams require typed interfaces at every boundary; missions are the organizational equivalent - Fidelity contracts prevent "compat surface passes while behavior silently drops" failures during ports - The same discipline prevents spec omissions in greenfield missions futon1a rebuild (M-futon1a-rebuild.md): - Prototype 0 (82 tests) specified internal layers but no API contract - Prototype 1 delivered HTTP serving, but the compat endpoints and model descriptor system were unspecified - The gap was discovered only when attempting to hand off to Codex - Retrofit required: Section 2.6 (API spec), Section 2.11 (model descriptor system), Prototype 2 Gate, interface signature section - Add Interface Signature section to current mission doc - Enumerate input and output ports from existing code - Cross-reference output ports against spec sections - Flag any unspecified ports as stop-the-line - Build the baseline capability inventory before DERIVE - Add tripwire tests before implementation starts @related futon-theory/mission-scoping, futon-theory/mission-lifecycle, futon-theory/mission-dependency, futon-theory/stop-the-line

title: Mission Lifecycle (State Machine)
text: Mission Lifecycle (State Machine) Treat each mission as a state machine with explicit transition requirements so scope, blockage, review, and closure leave an auditable trail instead of drifting invisibly. Missions progress through defined states. Without a formal lifecycle, missions drift indefinitely or are abandoned without evidence. The proof-path pattern governs individual changes; this pattern governs the mission as a whole. You are defining, tracking, or transitioning a mission. Missions may be blocked by dependencies, split into sub-missions, or merged when scope overlaps. The lifecycle must accommodate these. Apply the mission state machine: ``` :greenfield → :scoped → :active → :blocked → :review → :done ↑ ↓ ↓ └──────────┴─────────┘ (can regress) ``` State definitions: - :greenfield - Idea captured, no work plan - :scoped - Success criteria, boundaries, dependencies defined - :active - Work in progress, owner assigned - :blocked - Waiting on dependency (cite blocker) - :review - Work complete, awaiting verification - :done - Success criteria met, evidence recorded Transition requirements: - greenfield → scoped: Mission doc has success criteria + scope - scoped → active: Owner assigned, dependencies clear - active → blocked: Blocker cited with link to blocking mission - active → review: All success criteria addressed - review → done: Evidence verified by reviewer - Any → :abandoned: Explicit decision with rationale - Explicit states prevent invisible drift - Transition requirements create evidence trail - Blocked states surface dependency graphs - Review gates ensure verification before closure - Check current mission state - Verify transition requirements are met - Update mission doc with new state - If blocked, link to blocker mission @related futon-theory/proof-path, futon-theory/mission-scoping, futon-theory/mission-dependency, futon-theory/mission-interface-signature

title: Mission Scoping (Bounded Ownership)
text: Mission Scoping (Bounded Ownership) Scope every mission with bounded success criteria, inclusions, exclusions, ownership, and dependencies so it can be completed, reviewed, and handed off without ambiguity. Unbounded missions never complete. Without clear scope, work expands to fill available context, agents duplicate effort, and success cannot be verified. Every mission needs explicit boundaries. You are defining a new mission or reviewing an existing one. Scope may need revision as work progresses. Discovery during :active phase may reveal the mission is too large or too small. Every mission document must specify: 1. SUCCESS-CRITERIA - Concrete, verifiable outcomes - "Done when X is true" not "improve Y" - Minimum 1, maximum 5 criteria 2. SCOPE-IN - What is explicitly included - Files, modules, features affected - Decisions this mission makes 3. SCOPE-OUT - What is explicitly excluded - "Not addressing X in this mission" - Future work deferred 4. OWNER - Single agent responsible at any time - Handoff requires explicit transfer - Owner can delegate but retains accountability 5. DEPENDENCIES - What must be true before this mission can complete - Links to blocking missions or external requirements - SPLIT when success criteria exceed 5 - SPLIT when multiple unrelated concerns emerge - MERGE when two missions share >50% scope - On split: create child missions, link to parent - On merge: archive one, expand the other - Bounded scope enables completion - Explicit exclusions prevent scope creep - Single owner prevents diffusion of responsibility - Dependencies surface the mission graph - Review mission doc for all 5 elements - Add missing scope elements - If scope unclear, mark mission :blocked with "scope-undefined" @related futon-theory/mission-lifecycle, futon-theory/mission-dependency, futon-theory/mission-interface-signature

title: Progress Signal (Evidence Accumulation)
text: Progress Signal (Evidence Accumulation) Measure mission progress through accumulating evidence and explicit health states so slowdown, blockage, and dead work are detected early instead of being felt only as vague stagnation. Missions can feel stuck even when progress is happening. Without explicit progress signals, agents lose motivation, humans lose visibility, and dead missions aren't detected. Counter-ratchet applies to code; this pattern applies to missions. You need to assess whether a mission is progressing, stalled, or dead. Progress isn't always linear. Research phases may produce no artifacts. Blocked missions may have zero commits but active waiting. The signal must distinguish stalled from legitimately waiting. Track progress via evidence accumulation: EVIDENCE-TYPES (in order of strength): 1. SUCCESS-CRITERIA-MET: Criterion checked off with proof 2. ARTIFACT-CREATED: Code, doc, test added (commit hash) 3. DECISION-MADE: Choice recorded in mission doc 4. BLOCKER-RESOLVED: Dependency cleared 5. REVIEW-COMPLETED: Milestone reviewed and approved 6. SESSION-LOGGED: PSR/PUR pair recorded (weakest signal) PROGRESS-METRICS: ``` velocity = evidence_count / time_elapsed momentum = recent_evidence (last 7 days) / total_evidence completion = criteria_met / total_criteria ``` HEALTH-STATES: - PROGRESSING: velocity > 0, momentum > 0.3 - SLOWING: velocity > 0, momentum < 0.3 - STALLED: velocity = 0 for > 7 days, not :blocked - BLOCKED: explicitly marked :blocked with blocker - DEAD: stalled > 30 days, no activity INTERVENTION-TRIGGERS: - SLOWING: Review scope, consider split - STALLED: Diagnose cause, reassign or close - DEAD: Archive with post-mortem Like code counts, mission evidence should not decrease: - Criteria met stays met (unless scope changes) - Artifacts created persist - Sessions logged accumulate If evidence decreases (reverted commit, criterion unmarked): - Flag for investigation - Require explicit justification Mission progress feeds into stack vitality metrics: - Active missions with evidence = healthy - Many stalled missions = unhealthy - High completion rate = velocity - Evidence accumulation makes progress visible - Metrics enable early intervention - Health states trigger appropriate responses - Dead mission detection prevents zombie work - Audit mission for evidence types present - Calculate current health state - If stalled, diagnose and intervene - Log progress signal to MUSN activity stream @related futon-theory/counter-ratchet, futon-theory/mission-lifecycle, futon-theory/minimum-viable-events

title: Proof Path
text: Proof Path Every change in the FUTON stack follows a proof path: an auditable event chain linking intent to operation to change to verification to durable proof commit. The proof path is the core unit of work in futon theory. It embodies the Curry-Howard correspondence: programs are proofs of their specifications. The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). This protocol assumes a single-writer linear chain. Open constraints: - Concurrent writers: Requires conflict detection at APPLY_CHANGE or serialization at PROOF_COMMIT. Domain patterns must specify strategy. - Partial apply: If APPLY_CHANGE partially succeeds, VERIFY must detect and the path must either complete rollback or spawn a repair path. - Retries: Failed paths may be retried from OBSERVE, not mid-path. Future: A "concurrency protocol" pattern may extend this for multi-writer. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. A1 (Auditability): Every proof path is fully traceable from intent to outcome. A2 (Attributability): Each event in the path has a clear source and owner. A3 (Evidence-driven): Progression requires verified evidence, not assertion. Domain patterns specify how proof paths are implemented: - Storage: `storage/durability-first` for PROOF_COMMIT - Lab sessions: Session lifecycle wraps proof paths - Checks: Verification DSL for VERIFY phase - No change commits without passing all invariant checks - Every commit references its evidence chain - Proof paths are append-only; errors spawn new paths, not mutations A proof path consists of these phases: 1. CLOCK_IN - Session begins, agent declares intent 2. OBSERVE - Read state, gather evidence 3. PROPOSE_CLAIM - Agent proposes what will change 4. APPLY_CHANGE - Execute the change 5. VERIFY - Confirm change matches claim 6. INVARIANT_CHECK - All invariants must pass 7. PROOF_COMMIT - Durable commit with evidence chain 8. CLOCK_OUT - Session ends, proof path complete Without proof paths, changes are unauditable. With them, any bug can be traced from symptom to cause through the evidence chain. The spec mediates future state into present; the proof path is how we get there defensibly.

title: Rapid Debugging (Invariant 4)
text: Rapid Debugging (Invariant 4) I4: Any bug diagnosable in under 10 minutes. Any bug diagnosable in under 10 minutes. Errors name their source: layer, operation, entity ID, expected vs actual. One write path to trace, not six. State inspectable at any moment. Debugging hours instead of minutes is not just inconvenient - it's a sign of architectural failure. If you can't find the bug, you can't fix it. Rapid debugging is a first-class design concern, not an afterthought. The applicability scope of the pattern (see substructure). - Errors include: layer, operation, entity ID, expected vs actual - Single write path (chokepoint) to trace, not multiple paths - State inspectable at any moment via REPL or API - Logs tell a story: "write started -> confirmed -> done" or "started -> failed at X" The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). Missing layer -> search all layers (hours) Missing entity ID -> search all entities (hours) Multiple write paths -> trace all paths (hours) Unstructured logs -> grep randomly (hours) - "Error occurred" without context - Six different write functions - State only visible after restart - Logs that require human interpretation to correlate Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. - All errors use structured format with required fields - Write path is single chokepoint (one function to trace) - State query API available without restart - Logs structured, not prose 1. Error message names source layer 2. Entity ID links to exact record 3. Expected vs actual shows the discrepancy 4. Operation name maps to one function 5. Timestamp + tx-id allows timeline reconstruction Time-to-diagnosis determines time-to-fix. A system where bugs take hours to find will have more bugs, because the feedback loop is slow. Fast debugging is a multiplier on all other engineering work. next[Implement single write chokepoint in futon1a] next[Add structured error format with required fields] next[Create state inspection API for live debugging]

title: Specification Emerges by Retroactive Canonicalization of Ancestors
text: Specification Emerges by Retroactive Canonicalization of Ancestors Futon theory specifications are not a priori axiom systems. They are the result of retroactive canonicalization: taking patterns that emerged from practice (ancestors), recognizing which ones are structurally necessary, and promoting them to invariants and constraints. Events do not change; their symbolic coordinates change — from "incidental fix" to "necessary constraint." This process must itself be auditable. A persistent question in the futon stack is: where does the specification come from? If you treat it as an axiom system that existed before the code, you cannot explain how it was derived. If you treat it as code-first, you have no theory. The answer is neither: specification emerges from practice through a specific, identifiable, auditable process that this pattern describes. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. When is canonicalization warranted? A pattern is a candidate when: - Frequency: it has been applied across multiple tasks/missions - Risk: its absence caused or would cause a detectable failure - Reusability: it applies across domains, not just one context - Failure cost: the consequence of ignoring it is high - Machine-checkability: it can be enforced by code, not just convention These rules correspond to the theory-as-exotype type-check: a pattern that satisfies these criteria "type-checks" against the theory exotype and is eligible for promotion. The key insight: when a pattern is canonized, its past instances are retroactively reclassified. The event that prompted delivery-receipt was, at the time, just a bug fix for silent message drops. After canonicalization, it becomes evidence that G1 (mandatory-pur / delivery receipt guarantee) was always structurally necessary. What changes: the pattern's role (from incidental to necessary) What does NOT change: the events themselves (commits, bug reports, fixes) This is why "future elements manifesting in the present" is not mystical — it is the retroactive recognition that a pattern which seemed contingent was actually structurally required. The structure was always there; the naming capacity to see it was not. Formally: > A newly formed specification retroactively rewrites the role of old > patterns (from contingent repair to necessary constraint) without > rewriting the old events themselves. The futon3 pattern library contains ~843 patterns. Of these, ~23 are in futon-theory/ (the "specification"). The rest are the ancestor set: patterns written under immediate pressure — data recovery failures, persistence bugs, counter ratchet needs, agent coordination breakdowns. These ancestors are: - Genotype material: replicable, mutable, selectable symbol fragments - Local adaptation history: each written to solve a specific failure - Uncanonized rule fragments: they work but haven't been placed in a unified constraint system The specification is NOT the ancestor set. The specification is what you get when you compress, standardize, and constrain the ancestor set into an exotype (contract). Each act of canonicalization should produce a durable record: {:canonization/id :string :canonization/ancestor-pattern :string ; e.g. "agency/delivery-receipt" :canonization/target-spec :string ; e.g. "coordination/mandatory-pur" :canonization/evidence [:string] ; commits, incidents, PURs :canonization/old-role :string ; "ad-hoc fix for silent drops" :canonization/new-role :string ; "ancestral evidence for G1" :canonization/rationale :string ; why this promotion :canonization/ts :string} Without canonization events, the lineage from ancestor to specification is invisible. With them, anyone can ask: "why does this invariant exist?" and trace it back through the ancestor that demonstrated its necessity.
