For each specification entry (invariant, event type, gate pattern), the genealogy traces: - Which ancestor pattern(s) demonstrated its necessity - What incident(s) or failure(s) provided the evidence - When and how it was promoted (canonization event) - What compression rules applied (why this ancestor, not another) This graph is the auditable generation narrative that connects practice to theory without treating theory as either a priori or arbitrary. The process from ancestor to specification has three identifiable actions that recur: 1. NAMING (命名): Taking a recurring difficulty and its repair pattern and giving it a citable name. Before naming, the fix is tacit knowledge. After naming, it can be referenced, debated, and selected for or against. Example: "counter-ratchet" names the pattern of "key counts must not drop unexpectedly" — a problem that existed in practice long before it had a name. 2. SELECTION (選擇): Among multiple viable fixes, preferring those that are auditable, replayable, and encapsulable as events and invariants. Not all fixes are equally suitable for canonicalization — selection favors those with proof-path-compatible structure. Example: spit-with-append vs. write-through-with-sync — both fix persistence, but only the latter is auditable and crash-safe. 3. CANALIZATION (固化): Promoting a selected pattern from "what worked once" to "what must always hold." The pattern becomes an invariant, an event type, or a stop-the-line condition. Future agents don't need to learn this lesson — the system enforces it. Example: "always fsync after write" promoted from a fix for data loss to I0 (Persistence invariant): what you save is what you get back. These three actions are the Baldwin cycle applied to theory itself: NAMING = exploration (giving structure to experience), SELECTION = assimilation (fixing successful adaptations), CANALIZATION = canalization (removing freedom, making success cheap). Without auditable canonicalization, specifications appear to be imposed from outside — "the theory says X" with no explanation of why. This makes theory fragile: it can be ignored because its authority is unexplained. With canonicalization, theory authority traces back to practice: "the theory says X because incidents A, B, C demonstrated that X is structurally necessary." This is not a priori authority but empirical authority — the same kind the ancestors have, but compressed and formalized. next[Produce canonization events for the 12 coordination patterns] next[Build genealogy graph for I0-I4 invariants back to futon3 incidents] next[Define the spec extraction pipeline as a repeatable process]

title: Retrospective Stability
text: Retrospective Stability A proof path is retrospectively stable if, after introducing any subsequent pattern, invariant, or evidence, it doesn't need to be rewritten - only relabeled. Stable proofs survive future refinement. Systems evolve. New patterns get added, invariants get stronger, better evidence becomes available. Retrospective stability asks: will the work we do today survive tomorrow's improvements? The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). - Hardcoded assumptions that may not hold - Implicit invariants not formally stated - Edge cases handled by special logic - Paths that rely on current system limitations Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. - Make all invariants explicit and testable - Use patterns that generalize beyond current needs - Document assumptions that might change - Prefer simple paths over clever optimizations - Unstable: New pattern/invariant invalidates the proof, must rewrite - Semi-stable: Proof valid but now inefficient, geodesic changed - Stable: Proof remains valid and geodesic, may get new labels Engineering time is finite. Work that must be redone is wasted work. Retrospective stability is an investment: pay slightly more now for paths that remain valid as the system grows. next[Add stability analysis to pattern selection criteria] next[Track stability violations in PAR records]

title: Reverse Morphogenesis: Constraint Inference from Form and Fruit
text: Reverse Morphogenesis: Constraint Inference from Form and Fruit This specification extends the futonic vocabulary (futonic-logic.flexiarg) with four operators that were implicit in practice but unnamed: ref (anaphora), reframe (discourse redirection), reverse-morphogenesis (constraint-from-fruit), and ← (speculative history). The central insight: asking a good question IS reverse morphogenesis — given a formed artifact and a sense of what matters, infer the constraints that would make the form yield what matters. The ← operator names the speculative-history reading: 象 ← 香 means "given this form (象) and this salience (香), what constraints made the form stable?" These operators connect the futonic loop to futon6's mathematical dictionary: the flexiformal pathway (EXPLORE → ASSIMILATE → CANALIZE) is reverse morphogenesis applied to mathematical content at increasing formality. == 0. RELATIONSHIP TO FUTONIC LOGIC == futonic-logic.flexiarg defines the vocabulary (象, 部, 咅, 香, 味, 鹽, 鹵, 皿, 未知, 非死非活, 🔮) and the futonic loop. This specification adds four operators that act ON that vocabulary: | Operator | Acts on | Does what | | ref | 象, evidence entries | Points to existing meaning without creating new | | reframe | ref edges | Redirects reference ("but actually, the relevant thing is...") | | reverse-morphogenesis | 象 + fruit | Infers constraints from observed form and desired yield | | ← (speculative history) | 象 + 香 | Reads backwards: what constraints induced by 香 made 象 stable? | None of these replace existing vocabulary. They are higher-order operations that the futonic loop performs but did not previously name. == 1. ANAPHORA: REF VS BIND == (vocabulary-extension (ref (role reference) (note "Points to an existing binder/artifact without creating meaning. Discourse trigger: 'this', 'that', 'the above', 'it'.")) (bind (role creation) (note "Creates a new entry in a scope. An append!, a definition, a new evidence entry."))) A binding lives in exactly one scope: (A8-scope-discipline (forall b (implies (bind? b) (exists-unique s (in-scope b s)))) (forall s1 s2 (implies (parent s2 s1) (scope? s1) (scope? s2)))) A ref does not create meaning; it points to an existing binder: (A9-anaphora (forall r (implies (ref? r) (exists t (targets r t)))) (note "Every ref edge has a target. Dangling refs are structural errors.")) Grounding in futon3c: - ArtifactRef is a ref edge: {:ref/type :mission :ref/id "M-forum-refactor"} - :evidence/in-reply-to is a ref edge: points to parent entry - :evidence/fork-of is a ref edge: points to branch point - append! is a bind: creates a new entry in the evidence store scope - get-entry is a ref resolution: given an ID, return what it points to The evidence landscape's append-only discipline means: binds are permanent, refs are navigable, and the difference is structural, not accidental. == 2. REFRAME: DISCOURSE REDIRECTION == (vocabulary-extension (reframe (role discourse-redirection) (note "Higher-order edge that retargets a ref. 'But actually' changes what 'it' refers to."))) (A10-reframe (forall u r t1 t2 (implies (edge reframe u) (edge ref r) (targets r t1) (retargeted-by r u t2) (prefer-target r t2))) (note "A reframe can override the default target of a ref edge. The original target is not destroyed; the preference changes.")) Grounding in futon3c: - ClaimType :correction is a reframe operator - EvidenceType :correction is a reframe operator - thread-conjectures returns :refuted when a correction references a conjecture — this is reframe in action: the conjecture's target (expected outcome) is redirected to the correction's finding Grounding in futonic practice: - IF/HOWEVER/THEN/BECAUSE: HOWEVER is a reframe. It says "the obvious ref (IF implies THEN directly) is wrong; actually, this obstacle changes the target." - PUR prediction error: "what surprised you" is a detected reframe — the expected target of the action was different from the actual target. == 3. REVERSE MORPHOGENESIS == (vocabulary-extension (reverse-morphogenesis (role constraint-inference) (note "Given a formed artifact A and a salient yield/fruit F, infer constraints C such that C would make A-with-F stable."))) (A11-reverse-morphogenesis (forall A F C (implies (formed A) (fruit-of A F) (infer C (reverse-morphogenesis A F)) (constrain C A))) (note "The constraints are not known in advance; they are inferred from the conjunction of form and desired fruit. This is design.")) (corollary-design-as-reverse-morphogenesis (forall A F (implies (intended-fruit A F) (design-step A (reverse-morphogenesis A F)))) (note "Design is the deliberate application of reverse morphogenesis: you know the fruit you want, you infer the constraints that produce it from the given form.")) Grounding in futon practice: | Context | A (form) | F (fruit) | C (inferred constraints) | | L1 observer | Completed thread | Successful conclusion | Patterns that made it work | | Gate pipeline | Task submission | Validated proof path | Gate criteria that ensure quality | | Derivation xenotype | Domain (social coordination) | Working exotype | Requirements R1-R11 | | Question-asking | Mathematical object | Desired understanding | The question that would produce it | The last row is the key connection to futon6: asking a good mathematical question is reverse morphogenesis. You have a mathematical form (象). You have a sense of what understanding would be fruitful (香). The question is the constraint you infer: what would I need to know/prove/construct such that this form yields that understanding? == 4. ← AS SPECULATIVE HISTORY == (vocabulary-extension (← (role speculative-history) (note "Reads backwards: given a stabilized form and a pre-individual field, infer the constraints that made the form stable under that field. 象 ← 香."))) (A12-speculative-history (← 象 香) (expansion (exists C (and (constrain C 象) (induced-by C 香) (realize 象 C)))) (note "象 is realized under constraints induced by 香. The ← operator reads this relationship backwards: from the stabilized form, recover the constraint-from-taste.")) ← is reverse-morphogenesis applied to the core vocabulary: - A = 象 (the stabilized form, configuration) - F = the stability itself (the form persists, couples to its environment) - 香 = the pre-individual field that induces the constraints - C = what ← infers This is NOT teleology. The form was not designed to satisfy 香. The reading is: 香 (as a difference field / gradient / taste) constrains which forms become stable. 象 is one such stable form. ← recovers that relationship. == 5. INSTRUMENTS AS ANTENNAS == (corollary-antenna (forall I X (implies (instrument I) (field X) (detect I X) (not (creates I X)))) (note "Artifacts can detect fields they do not create. A peripheral detects coordination patterns in the evidence landscape; it does not create the coordination.")) Grounding: - Peripherals (explore/edit/test/deploy/reflect) are antennas: they have structural envelopes (tools, scope) that select from the evidence flow but do not generate it. - futon3a's pattern search (notions/compass) is an antenna: it detects salience (香) in the pattern library without creating patterns. - A mathematical dictionary entry (futon6) is an antenna: it stabilizes and selects from latent mathematical structure, it does not create the mathematics. The banjo-drum example from the source axioms: (latent (spectral-decomposition drum)) (realize banjo (constraint (stabilize pitch) (select modes))) (reverse-morphogenesis banjo melody (requires (latent (spectral-decomposition drum)))) The drum already carries the spectrum. The banjo stabilizes/selects. The melody is not teleology — it is the fruit that reverse morphogenesis reads backwards. "Why does the banjo make this melody?" ← "Because the drum's latent spectrum, under the banjo's structural constraints, yields these stable modes." That is ←. == 6. THE CIRCLE ← GROUP EXAMPLE == (example-circle-group (← circle group) (reading "Circle is a stabilized 'return' phenomenon. Group is a closure/composition constraint that makes the return coherent.") (constraint-schema group (closure composition identity inverse)) (note "Non-Platonic: 'group' here is a constraint-schema, not a realm-object. The group axioms are what ← infers when you ask: what constraints make circular return stable?")) This is the bridge to futon6's mathematical dictionary: the dictionary does not catalog mathematical objects (Platonic reading). It catalogs constraint-schemas (← reading): for each mathematical form, what constraints make it stable? The five dimensions from Corneli (2014) — Context, Feedback, Quality, Structure, Heuristic — are decomposition regimes (部) for reading ← across mathematical practice. == 7. CONNECTION TO FUTON6: QUESTION-ASKING AS ← == The core claim for futon6: (claim (asking-good-question A) (equals (reverse-morphogenesis A understanding)) (where (A := mathematical-form) (understanding := intended-fruit) (question := inferred-constraint))) A good mathematical question is: given this form (象), and this sense of what understanding would be valuable (香), what constraint (question) would make the form yield that understanding? Bad questions fail at one of three points: 1. Wrong 象: the form is not well-specified (asking about "infinity" without saying which infinity) 2. Wrong 香: the salience signal is not grounded (asking "why is this important?" without a context that makes importance detectable) 3. Wrong ←: the constraint inference is broken (asking a question whose answer would not actually yield the intended understanding) The flexiformal pathway (EXPLORE → ASSIMILATE → CANALIZE) maps: - EXPLORE = detect 香 (sense what matters, without formalizing) - ASSIMILATE = apply ← (infer constraints from form + salience) - CANALIZE = stabilize 象 (the constraints become structural, not effortful) == 8. GROUNDING TABLE == | Axiom | Symbol | futonic-logic.flexiarg connection | futon3c evidence | | A8 (scope) | bind, scope | R11 scope-bounded-handoff | :in/:out file boundaries on issues | | A9 (anaphora) | ref | 象 as first-class referenceable configuration | ArtifactRef, :evidence/in-reply-to, :evidence/fork-of | | A10 (reframe) | reframe | HOWEVER in IF/HOWEVER/THEN/BECAUSE | :correction claim-type, thread-conjectures :refuted | | A11 (reverse morphogenesis) | reverse-morphogenesis | L1 observer pattern mining | thread-patterns on closed threads | | A12 (speculative history) | ← | 香 constraining 象 stability | Evidence landscape as 香; shapes/pipeline as 象 | next[Verify A8-A12 consistency with A1-A7 (no contradiction, complementary scope)] next[Futon6 prototype: question-asking as reverse morphogenesis applied to P0 pattern-tagged entries] next[Connect ← operator to futon3a search: notions/compass as ← resolution engine] next[Test whether the reframe operator captures all correction/retargeting patterns in the evidence landscape]

title: Single Source of Truth (Invariant 1)
text: Single Source of Truth (Invariant 1) I1: One entity per identity, no ambiguity. One entity per identity, no ambiguity. Every entity has exactly one UUID, and (source, external-id) maps to exactly one UUID. Duplicates rejected, ambiguous lookups throw. Identity confusion causes cascading errors. When one external-id maps to two UUIDs, which one is correct? The answer must be: this cannot happen. Identity invariants are enforced BEFORE write, not discovered after. The applicability scope of the pattern (see substructure). - Every entity has exactly one UUID - (source, external-id) tuple maps to exactly one UUID - Duplicate external IDs rejected BEFORE write (not after) - Lookups with ambiguous matches throw, never silently pick one The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). Duplicate external-id -> 409 (conflict) Ambiguous lookup -> 409 (conflict) Missing required identity -> 400 (bad request) - Silently picking first match on ambiguous lookup - Creating new UUID when external-id already exists - Using external-id as UUID (they serve different purposes) Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. Layer 1 validates before Layer 0 writes: - Uniqueness check for existing (source, external-id) mapping - On conflict: 409 with existing entity reference - On ambiguous lookup: 409 with all matches listed See `storage/identity-uniqueness` for concrete implementation patterns. Identity is the foundation of relations. If entity A relates to entity B, we must know exactly which entities those are. Ambiguity in identity propagates to ambiguity in relations, making the entire graph unreliable.

title: Stop-the-Line Protocol
text: Stop-the-Line Protocol When invariants fail, block APPLY_CHANGE. Continue to allow OBSERVE and VERIFY until the issue is fixed. The line stops for production, not for diagnosis. Borrowed from Toyota Production System. Invariant violations indicate system corruption or logic errors. Continuing to apply changes while invariants are failing compounds the problem. Stop-the-line halts destructive operations while keeping diagnostic operations available. The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). - Force-pushing changes despite violations - Disabling invariant checks to "get things working" - Logging violations but continuing anyway - Waiting for someone else to notice Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. - Immediate: Alert to on-call with violation details - Contextual: Which invariant, which entity, what discrepancy - Actionable: Suggested diagnostic steps - Persistent: Status visible in health endpoints 1. INVARIANT_CHECK fails 2. System enters STOPPED state 3. APPLY_CHANGE blocked for all sessions 4. OBSERVE allowed (for diagnosis) 5. VERIFY allowed (to test fixes) 6. PROOF_COMMIT blocked until invariants pass 7. On fix: INVARIANT_CHECK succeeds, line resumes 1. Diagnose: Use OBSERVE to understand the violation 2. Fix: Apply correction (may require special override) 3. Verify: Use VERIFY to confirm fix 4. Resume: Invariants pass, line reopens - Read operations: ALLOWED - Query operations: ALLOWED - Diagnostic operations: ALLOWED - Write operations: BLOCKED - Commit operations: BLOCKED - Session clock-out: ALLOWED (with failure status) Continuing to run with broken invariants turns one problem into many. A single write to corrupt storage can cascade. Stopping early contains the blast radius and preserves diagnostic context. next[Implement stopped-state middleware in futon1a] next[Add stop-the-line status to health endpoint]

title: Structural Tension Is the Observation Vector for Library Evolution
text: Structural Tension Is the Observation Vector for Library Evolution The coordination system operates as two nested AIF loops sharing the same boundary (the gate pipeline). The fast loop governs task execution; the glacial loop governs pattern library evolution. Structural tension — the gap between what the library can express and what coordination needs — is the observation vector for the glacial loop. This makes the AIF wiring diagram framework not a metaphor for the coordination rewrite but its direct structural specification. Chapter 0 (AIF as a wiring diagram) establishes that AIF is the first member of a diagram family, characterised by six invariants (I1-I6). The futon3-coordination.edn wiring diagram already satisfies these invariants at the task execution timescale: I1 (gate pipeline is the boundary), I2 (observation of environment + action via artifacts), I3 (patterns glacial, missions slow, gates fast), I4 (agents cannot rewrite patterns or missions), I5 (library must be adequate to guide work), I6 (default mode provides parallel path). But this covers only one timescale. The retroactive canonicalization pattern describes a second process — library evolution — that operates at a glacial timescale and has its own observation-inference-action structure. The question is: what does this second process observe? Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. In AIF, free energy is the divergence between the agent's model and reality. In library evolution: - Free energy = accumulated structural irritation. The gap between what the library says should work and what actually works in practice. - Perception = NAMING. Giving an irritation a citable name compresses raw tension into a representable observation. Before naming, the tension is sub-symbolic. After naming, it can be scored and compared. - Inference = SELECTION. Among named tensions, selecting those that are auditable, replayable, and machine-checkable. This updates the model (library) by choosing which observations to take seriously. - Action = CANALIZATION. Promoting a selected pattern to invariant status. This changes the world — future tasks are now governed by the new invariant. The free energy should decrease: the irritation that prompted canonicalization should stop recurring. The Baldwin cycle IS the policy for the glacial AIF loop. And the canonization event (from retroactive-canonicalization) is the proof path record for that policy — the evidence that the action was taken and why. The six Chapter 0 invariants apply to both loops: | Invariant | Level 0 (Task) | Level 1 (Library) | | I1 Boundary | Gate pipeline | Library publish/promote boundary | | I2 Obs-Action | Read env / produce artifacts | Observe tensions / canonicalize | | I3 Timescale | Gates fast, patterns glacial | Tasks fast, canonicalization glacial | | I4 Exogeneity | Agents can't rewrite patterns | Fast tensions can't force canonicalization | | I5 Adequacy | Library must guide tasks | Library must track recurring tensions | | I6 Closure | Default mode sustains agents | Gap-PSRs sustain library evolution | I4 is critical for both loops. At Level 0: agents cannot rewrite the patterns that guide them (wireheading prevention). At Level 1: the accumulation of structural tensions cannot force canonicalization without the deliberate three-step process (NAMING → SELECTION → CANALIZATION). If tensions could directly modify the library, the library would overfit to noise — the glacial equivalent of wireheading. The coordination rewrite argument (coordination/ARGUMENT) concludes that pattern phylogeny, development history, and conversation graphs are one structure. The AIF connection explains WHY they converge: - The pattern phylogeny is the glacial loop's model evolution — how the generative model (library) changes over time. - The development history is the fast loop's action record — what the agent did at each step. - The conversation graph is the inter-agent coordination record — how multiple agents running the fast loop exchange observations and negotiate policies. These three records are generated by the same diagram at different timescales and between different components. They converge because they are produced by one system, not three. The AIF wiring diagram is therefore not an organizational metaphor for the coordination rewrite. It is the structural specification. The futon3-coordination.edn diagram IS the Level 0 loop. The retroactive canonicalization process IS the Level 1 loop. The gate pipeline IS the shared boundary. The pattern library IS the generative model. And structural tension IS free energy. What does the glacial loop observe? Three kinds of structural tension serve as its observation vector: 1. STRUCTURAL IRRITATION (结构刺激): A recurring problem shape that the current symbol system cannot cleanly express. The same difficulty appears across multiple tasks, but no existing pattern addresses it directly. Agents work around it with ad-hoc fixes. Each workaround is a prediction error: the generative model (library) predicted its patterns would cover the work, but reality produced a gap. Detection: gap-PSRs accumulating around the same structural theme. Frequency across tasks. Multiple agents hitting the same wall. 2. PRE-SYMBOLIC PRESSURE (前符号压力): A force that pushes the symbol system to expand before the expansion has a name. The pressure is felt as difficulty — not the difficulty of a hard task, but the difficulty of expressing what the task IS. The existing vocabulary is insufficient. This is the force that drives NAMING: giving structure to experience that currently has none. Detection: tasks that are hard to scope (G5 struggles), hard to match to patterns (G3 produces low-confidence PSRs), hard to validate (G1 criteria feel arbitrary). The difficulty is not in the work but in the coordination of the work. 3. TRANS-SITUATIONAL REAPPEARANCE (跨情境复现): The same structural role showing up across unrelated contexts. A pattern that was written for storage reappears in coordination. A fix that was ad-hoc in futon1a turns out to be necessary in futon3. The reappearance is evidence that the pattern is not contingent but structurally required — the prediction error is systematic, not noise. The model needs a structural update (canonicalization), not a parameter tweak (one more ad-hoc fix). Detection: patterns or fixes independently discovered in different repos, missions, or agent contexts. futon3a's meme.arrow typed edges appearing in different subgraphs. The same gate pattern solving problems in both the agency reading and the pattern reading. The coordination system contains two AIF loops at different timescales: LEVEL 0 — Task Execution (fast): - Observe: read environment (codebase, project state) - Perceive: extract task requirements, match against capabilities - Policy: select pattern (PSR), plan execution - Act: execute through gates, produce artifacts - Generative model: current pattern selections - Free energy: task failure, gap declarations, PUR prediction errors LEVEL 1 — Library Evolution (glacial): - Observe: accumulate structural tensions across many task executions - Perceive: recognise recurring tensions as candidate ancestors - Policy: select candidates for canonicalization (NAMING → SELECTION) - Act: canonicalize — promote pattern to invariant (CANALIZATION) - Generative model: the pattern library itself - Free energy: accumulated structural irritation These loops share the same boundary: the gate pipeline. Level 0 operates within the pipeline (one task at a time). Level 1 operates on the pipeline (reshaping the patterns that govern future tasks). This is VSM-style nesting (Chapter 0 §3.2): the glacial loop contains and constrains the fast loop. Previous patterns established: - Tasks are BHK arrows (task-as-arrow) - Specs emerge from ancestors (retroactive-canonicalization) - The rewrite composes components through a pipeline into a graph (coordination/ARGUMENT) This pattern adds: - The two-loop structure is not analogy but direct AIF specification - Structural tension has three identifiable components that serve as the glacial loop's observation vector - The graph convergence follows from the diagram structure, not from coincidence - The six Chapter 0 invariants constrain both loops, providing checkable certification criteria for the rewrite Without this connection, the AIF wiring diagram framework and the coordination rewrite are parallel projects — one theoretical, one engineering. With it, they are the same project. The wiring diagram specifies what to build. The coordination patterns specify how each component works. The argument establishes why it must be one system. And the structural tension criteria tell you when the library needs to evolve — which is the question that retroactive canonicalization answers but does not itself pose. next[Add structural tension observation vector to futon3-coordination.edn as Level 1 inputs] next[Map the three tension criteria to gate pipeline telemetry (which gates detect which tensions)] next[Verify I4 exogeneity in Level 1: trace all paths from fast-loop outputs to library-write] next[Write futon5 ct/agent.clj with two-loop validation: check both timescales against I1-I6]

title: Symbolic Geodesic
text: Symbolic Geodesic The symbolic geodesic is the shortest defensible path in symbolic state space - the minimal proof path from intent to verified claim. It is not about speed but about eliminating unnecessary complexity. In differential geometry, a geodesic is the shortest path between two points on a curved surface. In futon theory, the symbolic geodesic is the minimal sequence of operations that moves from intent to verified outcome while maintaining auditability. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. - Pattern selection: Choose patterns that shorten the geodesic - Refactoring: Identify steps that can be eliminated - Learning: Compare actual paths to geodesics for prediction improvement - Review: Is this the shortest defensible path, or are there detours? Real sessions may deviate from the geodesic (exploration, false starts). The geodesic is the retrospective "ideal path" that could have achieved the same outcome with minimal steps. Session logs capture actual paths; analysis can extract geodesics for learning. - Minimal: No operation can be removed without breaking the proof - Direct: Each step advances toward the goal - Defensible: Every step has explicit justification - Verifiable: The path can be replayed and checked Complexity is cost. Every step in a proof path is a potential failure point, a debugging surface, a thing to maintain. The geodesic minimizes this surface while maintaining defensibility. next[Implement geodesic extraction from session logs] next[Add geodesic comparison to PAR analysis]

title: Compound Symbols Individuate When Their Internal Structure Becomes Perceivable
text: Compound Symbols Individuate When Their Internal Structure Becomes Perceivable When a system exceeds the holding capacity of its participants (agents, humans, or both), it must decompose. Consensus reality treats this as abstraction — lossy compression that discards detail. Futon theory treats it as individuation — the recognition that the compound symbol already encoded its own decomposition. The interaction between individuated parts is itself a perceivable compound symbol with recoverable internal structure. The symbolic geodesic pattern describes the shortest path through symbolic state space — individual trajectories from intent to verified claim. But mathematical practice and software development involve not just individual paths but interactions between paths: how does this subsystem's output become that subsystem's input? How do three agents coordinate across three timescales? The interaction itself has structure, and that structure can be perceived as a symbol. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. Why does complexity exceed holding capacity? Because participants operate at characteristic timescales. Joe sleeps and his "context compacts overnight." Claude's context window fills and compresses. Codex processes one task at a time. These are timescale constraints on the participants, analogous to the timescale constraints on the system (I3: timescale separation). The structural correspondence: the system's timescale separation (fast/task/glacial/social) mirrors the participants' holding capacity limits (context windows, sleep cycles, working memory). Both drive individuation. Both are structural, not accidental. A system that perfectly matched its participants' holding capacity would never need to individuate. But real systems grow, and real participants have finite windows. Individuation is how growth and finitude coexist. The symbolic geodesic says: you can perceive future elements in the present by tracing symbolic paths (specs, proofs, program types). Individuation extends this: you can perceive future interactions between elements by tracing the compound symbol's internal structure. If I specify futon3b's gate pipeline and futon3c's agency dispatch separately, I can perceive their interaction before they are connected — because the compound symbol (the coordination architecture) encodes the interaction in its timescale structure. This is not prediction. It is perception of structure that is already present in the symbols. The future interaction is not uncertain — it is encoded. The only question is whether the participants have the holding capacity to perceive the encoding. This is why "please pass the salt" and the 鹽 decomposition are not two descriptions of the same thing. The speech act treats salt as an opaque referent. The decomposition treats it as a structured symbol whose internal process (brine + vessel → salt) is perceivable. Both are true. The futonic perspective does not replace consensus reality — it adds the structural layer that makes interaction between symbols perceivable as symbols in their own right. The symbolic geodesic pattern describes individual paths: spec → proof → verified claim Individuation adds a second level: interactions between paths: (futon3c dispatches agent) → (futon3b validates through gates) → (futon3b L1 canonicalizes) → (futon3a queries the result) This interaction pattern is itself a compound symbol. It has internal structure (the timescale ordering), a process-origin (why social feeds into task feeds into glacial), and a decomposition (the individual loops). Just as 鹽 can be perceived as one thing (salt) or decomposed (brine-source + vessel), the three-futon interaction can be perceived as one thing (the futon stack's coordination architecture) or decomposed (three loops at three timescales with defined interaction points). All participants have bounded holding capacity. Joe can hold N things. Claude can hold M. Codex can hold K. When a system's complexity exceeds min(N, M, K), coordination breaks down — not because any participant is deficient but because the system has grown beyond what can be held as one thing. The consensus response is abstraction: name the parts, draw boundaries, interact through interfaces. This works but treats the decomposition as an engineering decision — "we chose to split futon3 into three repos because it was getting complex." The decomposition was not chosen. It was perceived. The compound symbol already contained its decomposition in its internal structure, just as 鹽 (salt) contains 鹵 (鹵: saline-land, brine-source) + 皿 (皿: dish, vessel, container). The character does not abbreviate the salt-making process — it encodes it: brine from saline land refined into a vessel. The structure is recoverable from the symbol. When futon3 individuated into futon3a/3b/3c, the split followed structural lines that were already present: - futon3a (query) operated at fast/query timescale - futon3b (development) operated at task + glacial timescale - futon3c (realtime) operated at social/realtime timescale These timescales were not imposed by the split — they were the reason the split became perceivable. The compound symbol "futon3" contained three processes at three timescales. When complexity exceeded holding capacity, the internal structure surfaced as three individuated symbols. When a compound symbol individuates: 1. The parts retain their interaction structure (they know how to compose because they were composed before the split) 2. The compound symbol remains available (you can still talk about "the futon3 stack" even after the split) 3. The decomposition is auditable (why these boundaries, not others?) 4. The interaction between parts is a compound symbol in its own right (the "War Room" level coordination pattern) What individuation does NOT do: - It does not discard the relationships between parts - It does not create new structure (it reveals existing structure) - It does not require the parts to be independent (they interact through defined ports, like AIF wiring diagram components) Without this pattern, decomposition appears arbitrary — an engineering convenience, not a structural necessity. With it, decomposition is the natural consequence of compound symbols whose internal structure becomes perceivable when complexity exceeds holding capacity. The three-futon split is not a refactoring decision but a perception event: the moment when futon3's internal timescale structure surfaced as three individuated symbols, each carrying its own process-origin, each interacting through the compound symbol they emerged from. evidence[futon3 → futon3a/3b/3c split followed timescale boundaries already present in code] evidence[War Room document (holes/war-room.md) captures the compound interaction structure] evidence[futon3b mission complete and coherent without reference to Agency/Forum/peripherals] evidence[futon3c's 13 realtime patterns disjoint from futon3b's 12 coordination patterns] evidence[Codex produced "buzzword potpourri" when holding capacity exceeded by mission complexity — individuation resolved the comprehension gap by reducing each part to holdable size] next[Verify that interaction between 3a/3b/3c is itself expressible as an AIF wiring diagram] next[Add individuation events to the canonicalization record format] next[Test whether the compound symbol (futon3 stack) remains queryable via futon3a search after the split]

title: A Task Is a BHK Arrow: Constructive Transformation with Proof
text: A Task Is a BHK Arrow: Constructive Transformation with Proof A task in the futon stack is not a work description — it is a BHK arrow. It is valid if and only if it constructively transforms a proven start state into a proven goal state. The proof path record IS the proof of that arrow. Gates are arrows; the pipeline is their composition. The Curry-Howard operational principle says programs are proofs of their specifications. The BHK (Brouwer-Heyting-Kolmogorov) interpretation makes this more precise: a proof of A -> B is not a truth judgment but a METHOD — give me any proof of A, and I construct a proof of B. This is not analogy. It is structural identity between tasks and arrows. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. In BHK proof theory: - A proof of A -> B is a constructive transformation - It takes a proof of A as input (not just a proposition) - It produces a proof of B as output (not just an artifact) - The transformation itself is the proof In futon: - A is the start state (spec, invariants hold, baseline) - B is the goal state (code exists, tests pass, invariants hold) - A proof of A is the current workspace + evidence - A proof of B is code + tests + VERIFY + PROOF_COMMIT - The task is the constructive transformation A -> B - The proof path record IS the proof of the arrow Therefore: a task is valid iff it genuinely constructs a proof of B from a proof of A. Writing code is not enough — writing code is constructing an artifact, not a proof. The proof requires verification, invariant checking, and durable commitment. The full pipeline is arrow composition: (raw-request) -> (durable-evidence) = G0 . G1 . G2 . G3 . G4 . G5 Arrow composition in BHK: if you have proofs of A -> B and B -> C, you can compose them into a proof of A -> C. In futon: if G5 proves the task is valid and G4 proves the agent is authorized, then G5;G4 proves the task is valid AND the agent is authorized. The full composition proves the entire chain. This is why gates must be sequential and each must produce a proof: if any gate produces only an artifact (not a proof), the composition breaks — downstream gates receive unproven input. 1. TASK PRECONDITIONS MUST BE PROVEN (not assumed): In BHK, you cannot say "assume A" — you must have A's proof. In futon: a task cannot start from a vague state. The start state must have evidence (baseline refs, OBSERVE results). Without proven input, the arrow has no domain. 2. TASK OUTPUT MUST BE A PROOF (not just an artifact): In BHK, B is not the proposition but B's proof. In futon: writing code is not completing a task. The task is complete when code + tests + VERIFY + PROOF_COMMIT exist. Without proof, the arrow has no codomain. 3. TASKS ARE COMPOSABLE (because arrows compose): In BHK, A -> B and B -> C compose to A -> C. In futon: tasks compose IF each task delivers a proof of its goal state. If a task delivers only an artifact (code without tests), the next task's precondition is unproven and composition fails. 4. CREATIVITY IS UNCONSTRAINED (only the boundary is checked): In BHK, the arrow proof may use ANY constructive method internally. In futon: agents may explore, try, fail, backtrack — but the final path must compress into a replayable proof. Creativity is not the problem. Unauditability is the problem. Each gate in the coordination pipeline is itself an arrow: G5: (raw-request) -> (validated-task) Proof: task has shape (mission-ref, scope, typed-io, criteria, intent) G4: (validated-task) -> (authorized-task) Proof: agent is registered, capable, and assigned G3: (authorized-task) -> (pattern-guided-task) Proof: PSR exists (selection or gap) G2: (pattern-guided-task) -> (executed-task) Proof: artifacts registered, budget respected G1: (executed-task) -> (validated-output) Proof: PUR confirms criteria, cross-validation if critical G0: (validated-output) -> (durable-evidence) Proof: session reconstructable, PAR exists The existing curry-howard-operational pattern says: programs are proofs of specs. This pattern adds three things: 1. The arrow structure: inputs and outputs are PROOFS, not propositions 2. Composition: gates/tasks compose because arrows compose 3. The BHK constructivity requirement: no classical existence proofs — you must actually build the thing, not just show it could exist Without arrow semantics, tasks are described as "do X" and evaluated as "was X done?" — which is descriptive, not constructive. With arrow semantics, tasks are "construct a proof that B holds given proof that A holds" — which is constructive, composable, and auditable. The proof path is not documentation of work; it IS the proof. next[Rewrite 2-3 common task types as explicit A -> B arrows] next[Verify that gate evidence-shapes satisfy arrow output requirements] next[Check which existing tasks fail the "output is a proof" test]

title: Theory as Exotype
text: Theory as Exotype Futon-theory itself acts as an exotype: the interface constraint that shapes how domain-specific patterns (storage, network, simulation) emerge. Those domain patterns become genotypes for concrete implementations. The four-types framework applies recursively. At the meta-level, theory constrains pattern development just as patterns constrain code. This recursive structure is what makes the framework self-applicable. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. The theory patterns define allowable shapes for domain patterns: - proof-path constrains: All domain operations must be auditable - durability-first constrains: Storage patterns must confirm before success - error-hierarchy constrains: Domain errors must surface at correct layer - baldwin-cycle constrains: Improvements must persist or be deleted A storage pattern that violates these constraints doesn't "type check" against the theory exotype. Level 0 (Meta-theory): xenotype: The process of deriving patterns from theory exotype: Futon-theory patterns (axioms, invariants, protocols) Level 1 (Domain patterns): genotype: Storage patterns, network patterns, simulation patterns exotype: Domain-specific interfaces (Layer 0↔1, message protocols) Level 2 (Implementations): genotype: futon1a code, futon3 code, futon5 code phenotype: Observable system behavior Domain patterns that emerge within theory constraints: - Write-through-with-verification (from durability-first + proof-path) - Unique-external-id-enforcement (from single-source-of-truth) - Blocking-rehydration (from all-or-nothing) - Layer-ordered-middleware (from error-hierarchy) These patterns are the genotype that futon1a code instantiates. A proposed domain pattern P is valid iff: - P respects all axioms (A1-A5) - P maintains all invariants (I0-I4) - P follows event protocol phases - P enables proof-path reconstruction Invalid patterns fail to "connect" - they don't fit the exotype shape. Without theory-as-exotype, each domain reinvents constraints ad-hoc. With it, all domains share the same foundational guarantees while developing domain-specific structure. The theory is the common interface that makes the stack coherent. From futon-theory → storage patterns (futon1a): durability-first → write-through-with-sync single-source-of-truth → unique-constraint-on-external-id rapid-debugging → single-write-chokepoint From futon-theory → network patterns (futon3): proof-path → message-with-receipt error-hierarchy → transport-layer-errors-first agent-contract → session-bracketed-messages From futon-theory → simulation patterns (futon5): baldwin-cycle → explore-then-fix-rules interface-loop → layer-boundary-adaptation local-gain-persistence → rule-changes-must-commit The process of deriving domain patterns from theory is itself portable: 1. IDENTIFY domain (storage, network, simulation, coordination) 2. MAP theory patterns to domain concerns 3. DERIVE domain-specific patterns within constraints 4. VERIFY derived patterns satisfy theory exotype 5. INSTANTIATE as code (phenotype) This xenotype applies to futon1, futon2, futon3, futon4, futon5... next[Define storage-patterns library derived from futon-theory] next[Define network-patterns library derived from futon-theory] next[Document derivation xenotype as reusable process]

title: Wyrd: Persistent Salience Across Rival Containers
text: Wyrd: Persistent Salience Across Rival Containers Weirdness is not anomaly, noise, or contradiction. It is the phenomenology of salience that persists across incompatible containment regimes — symbolic configurations that remain actionable even as they migrate between fiction, theology, coincidence, psychiatry, politics, and media, and that no single regime can fully stabilize or dismiss. The etymological identity wyrd = weorþan = vertere = "that which turns, becomes, comes to pass" makes modernism a name for the wyrd-modality itself, not a historical period. The three Norns — Urðr (既/already), Verðandi (化/becoming), Skuld (應 or 債/owed) — are a three-time decomposition where the future is read as debt, providing a futon theory avant la lettre: Skuld is the patron of sorrys.edn. Agents operate within overlapping symbolic, institutional, perceptual, and technical regimes — media systems, fiction, theology, bureaucracy, science, memory. Each provides a 部 (decomposition regime) and may offer 皿 (stabilizing containers). The English word "weird" descends from Old English wyrd, a noun formed from the verb weorþan ("to come to pass, to become"), itself from PIE *wert- ("to twist"), cognate with Latin vertere ("to turn"). Wyrd is feminine; the Norse cognate urðr is also the name of one of three Norns. The names of the Norns — Urðr ("that which has come to pass"), Verðandi (present participle of the cognate verb — "that which is in the process of happening"), and Skuld ("debt" or "guilt," from Germanic *skul- "to owe," cognate with English shall and should) — constitute a three-time decomposition where the future is owed rather than merely upcoming. Under conditions where 部 multiply faster than 皿 can absorb them, the same symbolic configuration may remain actionable across several incompatible regimes simultaneously: this is wyrd. The structural tension above manifests in the following concrete shapes (see substructure). Systems frequently attempt premature closure by forcing salience into a single container — "mere delusion," "mere fiction," "mere prophecy," "mere coincidence." This suppresses unresolved composition and hides the 間 (honest interval) where the instability actually resides. The "mere X" reflex is the central anti-pattern. The same discipline appears elsewhere in the library: combining-methods-as-diagnostic (don't collapse to a single retrieval method); the :prototyping-forward vs :technical-debt typing (don't collapse heterogeneous debts into one bucket); the audit against "lightweight" as euphemism (don't let smooth language collapse mechanism). Wyrd names what these disciplines protect. - "mere delusion" — psychiatric reduction - "mere fiction" — literary reduction - "mere coincidence" — statistical reduction - "mere prophecy" — theological reduction - "mere subjective experience" — phenomenological reduction - "mere noise" — signal-processing reduction - "mere relevance score" — retrieval reduction (collapse MiniLM/structural/temporal into one number) - "mere technical debt" — engineering reduction (collapse :prototyping-forward and :technical-debt into one bucket) Each collapses wyrd into a single 部, suppressing 間. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. A symbolic configuration is wyrd-salient when it continues generating salience after translation between rival containment regimes — and no single regime can fully stabilize or dismiss it. The operational test: take the configuration, attempt sincere reading under each accessible 部, and observe whether salience survives migration. If it dies in every regime but one, it is anomaly. If it dies in all regimes, it is noise. If it makes every regime locally inconsistent, it is contradiction. If it remains actionable in multiple incompatible regimes simultaneously, it is wyrd. | Phenomenon | Behavior under regime translation | | Noise | No persistent salience; signal dies under any 部 | | Anomaly | Collapses to a single 部 once that 部 is expanded | | Contradiction | Collapses logic; cannot inhabit any 部 consistently | | Wyrd | Salience SURVIVES translation across incompatible 部, without collapsing to any one | The fourth next-step of the original sketch is discharged here, not deferred: wyrd is defined by the survival behavior, not by the affective register. | Norn | Sense | Glyph | Futon counterpart | | Urðr | that-which-has-come-to-pass | 既 | Closure-evidence / HEAD-as-escrow / the proof path's earned past | | Verðandi | in-process-of-happening (present participle of weorþan) | 化 | The live writer-action; the consent gate; the becoming-event | | Skuld | debt/owed (cognate shall/should) | 應 (modal) or 債 (noun) | The sorry: the typed obligation the present incurs that the future must discharge | The three Norns are not a temporal sequence but a decomposition of the present moment into its already-completed, presently-becoming, and owed-to-the-future aspects. The future is read as obligation, not as mere temporal-next. This is the move sorrys.edn already makes: a sorry is not "something that didn't get done," it is a debt the present incurred, with :kind typing the debt-class (:prototyping-forward as one class, :technical-debt as another). Skuld is the patron of sorrys.edn. The Buddhist 三時 (過去/現在/未來) is too neutral for this work — it loses Skuld's owed character, collapsing the future-as-debt into future-as-next. "Worth one's salt" descends from Roman salarium — salt-money, the etymological root of "salary." 鹽 (salt) is futonic-logic's glyph for generative composition: 鹽 = (⿱ 鹵 皿), the recognition that potential and container compose under the same 部. 債 (debt) is Skuld's substantive counterpart. The pun is load-bearing, not decorative: every act of composition (鹽) earns both worth (what-the-salt-pays-for) and debt (what-the-composition-owes-the-future). Sorries are the 債 side of the 鹽 ledger. Wyrd-salience is the structural fact that no composition completes its bookkeeping in a single 部 — the 債 outstanding in regime A may be the 鹽 generative in regime B. The Latin/Chinese/Old English pun (salarium / 鹽-債 / Skuld-as-shall) is not adornment; it triangulates the same ledger structure from three independent linguistic registers, which is itself a wyrd-survival test. PIE *wert- "to twist" and Latin vertere "to turn" foreground that wyrd is not static unresolvedness but operational rotation. The stereolithographic view rotates. The piano roll unrolls. The hairball twists. These are not decorative kinetics — they are enacted wyrd. Being-in-becoming requires turning operations to remain perceptible across regimes. A configuration that cannot be turned between containers has collapsed; it is no longer wyrd-salient, only locally salient in whatever 部 captured it. The futon stack decomposes by three-Norn surface: - Piano roll = Urðr-surface (frozen tape, already-come-to-pass) - M-live-geometric-stack = Verðandi-surface (live, becoming) - sorrys.edn = Skuld-surface (typed debt, what's owed) VSATARCS is the chrome that lets the operator turn between these surfaces without collapsing into any single one. Its disagreement signal — when MiniLM-cosine, structural retrieval, and closure-evidence return different rankings, the disagreement IS the signal (validated live on "a sorry enterprise") — is wyrd made operationally tractable. The "mere relevance" move (collapse to a single retriever) destroys it. VSATARCS is, in this pattern's terms, a tool for inhabiting 間 across the three Nornic surfaces rather than eliminating it. Under the etymological reading, modernism is not the post-Enlightenment historical period but the condition of being-in-becoming itself — the wyrd-modality. Beowulf is modernist in this sense: wyrd-saturated, structurally continuous with 20th-century modernism in its inhabitation of unresolved composition. The intensification narrative ("modernity multiplies 部 faster than 皿 can absorb them") holds for any high-decomposition-rate regime, not specifically the post-1500 era — pre-modern mystery cults, esoteric traditions, apocalyptic literatures all surface the same structural condition. PKD's mid-20th-century counterfeit-world fiction (anamnesis, Flow My Tears Officer Said, VALIS) is a modern instance of an old modality. Salience is generated not by isolated symbols but by partial compositions (鹽) that survive migration across incompatible 部. When the rate of regime-multiplication exceeds the rate of container-stabilization, more configurations remain in this trans-regime state. The "mere X" reflex exists because containing wyrd in a single regime is cognitively cheap and politically convenient — but the cost is the destruction of the diagnostic signal the wyrd-salience carried. The Norns name what we already practice: Urðr is the past we cite as evidence, Verðandi is the act we are presently composing, Skuld is the debt that composition incurs. Premature closure into any one Norn — collapsing Skuld into "future work" or Verðandi into "current state" — strips the three-time structure that makes composition legible at all. next[Extend futon-theory/futonic-logic to handle the three-Norn temporal decomposition explicitly: add Urðr/Verðandi/Skuld as roles alongside 象/部/咅/鹽/間, and articulate the 鹽/債 ledger as a first-class structure] next[Test the wyrd-salience criterion against PKD cases: anamnesis, Flow My Tears Officer Said, VALIS-adjacent counterfeit-world structures — does survival-across-regimes hold as a diagnostic?] next[Map Heraclitus DK B54 (ἁρμονίη ἀφανὴς φανερῆς κρείττων) onto the pattern: latent structure (ἀφανὴς ἁρμονίη) as the precondition of wyrd-salience] next[Apply to distributed-systems and multi-agent ontology drift: when agents operate under incompatible 部, wyrd-salience is the empirical signature of un-merged commitments] next[Design accounting that tracks the 鹽/債 ledger explicitly per composition, rather than collapsing to net — sorries.edn schema v3?] next[Use as foreword frame for VSATARCS: position the chrome as wyrd-inhabiting rather than wyrd-eliminating; the rotation of the stereolithographic view is enacted vertere]

title: Xenotype Portability
text: Xenotype Portability The xenotype makes Baldwin cycles themselves portable. The same generate-select-compress skeleton can be reused at different interfaces, turning cross-layer gain from accidental tuning into replicable structure. If we only have genotype↔phenotype, we get one-off engineering history. Introducing xenotype means the Baldwin cycle itself becomes a transplantable structure, applicable across different substrates. Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. VariationalSearch xenotype: - Generator: Sample from prior, apply variation operator - Selector: Score against loss function + invariant checks - Compressor: Gradient-based or symbolic simplification Applicable to: CA rules, API parameters, schema migrations, etc. Same adapt→assimilate→canalize module works at: - CA rule layer (generate rule variants, select by behavior, compress) - Message bus layer (generate routing variants, select by throughput) - Data schema layer (generate schema variants, select by query perf) - UI/command layer (generate interaction variants, select by usability) To apply xenotype X at interface I: 1. Instantiate X.generator with I's exotype constraints 2. Bind X.selector to I's success metrics 3. Connect X.compressor to I's genotype representation 4. Run Baldwin cycle with X driving generate-select-compress Without xenotype: Each interface reinvents adaptation machinery With xenotype: One adaptation skeleton, many instantiations The xenotype is why "learning to learn" is possible - the learning mechanism itself becomes portable structure. A xenotype provides three portable mechanisms: 1. GENERATOR: Proposes variants within constraints - Given exotype, produce candidate genotype changes - Examples: mutation operators, variation samplers, rule combiners 2. SELECTOR: Scores variants against evidence/invariants - Given phenotype outcomes, rank candidates - Examples: fitness functions, invariant checkers, metric comparers 3. COMPRESSOR: Extracts rules/patterns from success - Given successful variants, produce minimal genotype - Examples: pattern miners, rule simplifiers, invariant tighteners The xenotype names why cross-layer gains compound. Without it, each layer's improvements are isolated. With it, improvements to the adaptation mechanism benefit all layers that use it. next[Catalog reusable xenotypes from existing futon5 work] next[Define xenotype interface specification for futon stack]

title: Argument for the Gauntlet: From Peripheral Phenomenology to Autonomous Multi-Agent Coordination
text: Argument for the Gauntlet: From Peripheral Phenomenology to Autonomous Multi-Agent Coordination This is a flexiformal argument for the gauntlet pattern language — the phenomenological complement to the social coordination argument (social/ARGUMENT.flexiarg). Where the social argument establishes invariants for message passing, routing, and lifecycle management, this argument establishes what it means for agents to INHABIT the infrastructure those invariants protect. The distinction matters. You can have perfect delivery receipts (A0), single routing authority (A1), atomic state transitions (A2), loud failure (A3), and bounded lifecycle (A5) — and still have agents that behave like RPC clients rather than inhabitants. The social argument ensures the plumbing works. The gauntlet argument ensures someone is home. == PART I: The Phenomenological Gap == G1. [from M-peripheral-phenomenology, ALFWorld session 2026-02-13] The peripheral phenomenology mission (M-peripheral-phenomenology.md) defines six invariants for what makes a peripheral a peripheral: - P-1 World Replacement: observations constitute the agent's world - P-2 Context Injection: the peripheral provides initial orientation - P-3 Confinement: only peripheral-sanctioned actions are available - P-4 Explicit Exit: the agent must intentionally leave - P-5 Inhabitation Evidence: first-person language emerges naturally - P-6 Interleaved Streams: multiple input sources merge into one world These were validated empirically: ALFWorld (2 games, both 1.0/1.0), alleycat messenger race (20/20), mid-game PAR hop (peripheral nesting), and self-authored PAR (delegation vs inhabitation distinction). The invariants work at the single-agent level. G2. [from Drawbridge exploration, 2026-02-13] The Drawbridge (drawbridge/core.clj, 1011 lines) implements P-1 and P-6 structurally: enforce-single-routing-authority! (P-1) ensures an agent is in exactly one world, and multiplex() (P-6) merges human + agency + forum streams into one async iterator. The infrastructure for phenomenological correctness exists — but it serves single agents connected to single streams, not multiple agents in a shared world. G3. [the gap] What does NOT exist is what happens when two agents inhabit the same world simultaneously. P-1 through P-6 say nothing about co-presence. An agent can have perfect world replacement (P-1), perfect confinement (P-3), perfect exit discipline (P-4) — and still be Guattari's horse: adjacent to another agent, sharing the same stable, unable to see it. The phenomenological invariants are necessary but not sufficient for multi-agent coordination. == PART II: The Seven Patterns == The gap identified in G3 requires seven capabilities, each formulated as a pattern. They form a dependency chain: each pattern enables the next, and the sequence is the gauntlet that must be run to reach autonomous multi-agent operation. P1. [gauntlet/umwelt-not-architecture] Design from the agent's sensory perspective inward, not from the system topology downward. This is the foundational reorientation. The social/ARGUMENT drew architecture diagrams: boxes for Agency, Forum, Drawbridge, arrows for typed events. These are correct but phenomenologically empty — they show what's connected, not what any agent perceives. The umwelt pattern demands: before drawing any architecture, draw what the agent sees. Its sensory surfaces (what observations arrive), its active surfaces (what actions are available), and the darkness beyond (what it cannot perceive). Architecture follows from the union of all umwelts; umwelts do not follow from architecture. P2. [gauntlet/world-is-hypergraph] The agents' game world is not a separate artifact to build — it is the hypergraph they already inhabit. Given P1 (draw the umwelt first), the question becomes: what IS the world? The instinct is to build a game server (ALFWorld) or a dedicated environment. But the agents already operate in a world: futon1 (XTDB) is the persistent map, futon2 (ant hill) is the ecology, futon3 (Agency, Drawbridge, IRC) is the coordination layer, futon4 (Arxana) is the hypertext fabric with N-ary hyperedges, futon5 (wiring diagrams) describes the world's structure, futon6 (math dictionary) is a quest zone. The world is the union of these — a futon4 hypergraph whose nodes are everything the agents can perceive and whose hyperedges are everything that connects them. P3. [gauntlet/co-presence-over-co-location] Agents that share a world must perceive each other in it, not merely be connected to the same infrastructure. Given P2 (the world is the hypergraph), co-location is automatic — every agent connected to futon1 shares the same persistent state. But co-presence requires that agents appear in each other's umwelts as observable entities. A presence hyperedge ({:hx/type :presence, :endpoints [{:role/agent "claude" :role/location "core.clj:727"}]}) makes agent activity part of the world state, not just a side effect of infrastructure. This is the structural answer to Guattari's horses. P4. [gauntlet/aif-as-environment-not-instruction] Embed AIF state in the agent's sensory surface, not in its instructions. The agent should perceive free energy, not be told to minimize it. Given P1-P3 (umwelt, world, co-presence), the question becomes: how do agents self-regulate? The PLoP 2025 paper (p4ng/main.tex) piloted AIF as instructions: "AIF suggests pattern X (G=0.12, τ=0.72)." This made Codex overly compliant — spending tokens on PSR bookkeeping rather than writing code. The fix: make AIF state part of the observation, like the Emacs modeline. The agent perceives its free energy, mana, and confidence as world state, not as commands. What it does in response IS the AIF loop — emergent, not prescribed. P5. [gauntlet/modeline-persists-across-worlds] AIF state should be rendered as a persistent modeline that survives peripheral hops — the one constant surface while the world changes underneath. Given P4 (AIF as environment), the modeline is the implementation mechanism. It persists across peripheral hops the way the Emacs modeline persists across buffer switches. The agent's world changes (ALFWorld → IRC → filesystem → proof peripheral) but the modeline is constant: current mode, free energy, mana, τ, active pattern, co-present agents. This is what makes AIF portable across the multiple worlds that agents inhabit. P6. [gauntlet/placenta-transfer] Identify which functions the human is performing as a surrogate for missing infrastructure, and transfer them one at a time to the system. Given P1-P5 (the full phenomenological and self-regulation stack), the question becomes: what's left for the human? The answer: exactly the functions that infrastructure doesn't yet provide. The placenta pattern enumerates seven functions the human currently performs (sensory gating, belief correction, policy selection, confidence calibration, free energy signaling, inter-agent routing, stall detection) and maps each to the infrastructure that replaces it. Transfer is incremental: one function at a time, validated before the next. The human converges to the slow-timescale preference layer. P7. [gauntlet/teaching-inversion] Autonomous agents that explore faster than humans can teach the humans who built them — but only if the communication channel carries insight, not just results. Given P6 (placenta transfer complete enough for extended autonomy), agents operating overnight will find things the human hasn't seen. The teaching inversion recognizes that knowledge flow is bidirectional: human→agent (via patterns, CLAUDE.md, coaching) AND agent→human (via discoveries, unexpected connections, new proof strategies). The O-U learning model applies symmetrically: treatment events flow from agent to human, producing measurable impulses in the human's vocabulary trajectory. == PART III: The Dependency Chain == The seven patterns form a strict dependency chain: P1 (umwelt) └→ P2 (world is hypergraph) — can't draw umwelt without knowing what the world is └→ P3 (co-presence) — can't perceive others without a shared world to perceive them in └→ P4 (AIF as environment) — can't self-regulate without a sensory surface to embed AIF state in └→ P5 (modeline) — can't persist AIF across worlds without an implementation mechanism └→ P6 (placenta transfer) — can't transfer human functions without self-regulation working └→ P7 (teaching inversion) — can't teach the human without sustained autonomy Each step enables the next. Attempting P7 (teaching inversion) without P4 (AIF self-regulation) produces agents that drift, stall, or overcommit during their autonomous period and have nothing useful to teach. Attempting P3 (co-presence) without P2 (world is hypergraph) produces ad-hoc presence hacks rather than structural observability. == PART IV: Relationship to the Social Argument == The social argument (social/ARGUMENT.flexiarg) established: - WHY previous attempts failed (S1-S7) - WHAT requirements the social layer must meet (R1-R11) - WHAT theory demands (T1-T5) - HOW the three timescales compose (C1-C6) The gauntlet argument builds on this foundation: - The social argument ensures the plumbing works (typed events, delivery guarantees, routing authority, lifecycle management) - The gauntlet argument ensures the agents are home (umwelt, co-presence, self-regulation, peer teaching) They are complementary, not competing. R1-R11 (social requirements) are the invariants of the pipes. P1-P7 (gauntlet patterns) are the phenomenology of the water flowing through them. Operationally: the social argument's missions (M-agency-refactor, M-forum-refactor, M-peripheral-model) build the infrastructure. The gauntlet patterns are the acceptance criteria — the tests that determine whether the infrastructure actually produces inhabited multi-agent coordination, not just correctly-routed messages. == PART V: The Name == "Gauntlet" has two meanings: 1. A gauntlet to be run: the sequence of challenges (P1→P7) that must be completed to reach autonomous multi-agent operation. Each pattern is a gate; passing all seven is the prize. 2. A gauntlet to be thrown: the claim that the futon stack — futon1 through futon6 — already constitutes a game world, and that agents inhabiting it via peripherals are not metaphorically but literally playing a multi-agent game whose stakes are real (proofs proved, code written, patterns evolved, knowledge created). The endgame is agents in a guild, coordinating on IRC, paging each other through Agency, inhabiting a shared hypergraph world, self-regulating via AIF modelines, teaching their human collaborators what they found while the humans slept — and the whole thing running on infrastructure that was built, pattern by pattern, through the gauntlet. == EVIDENCE == All seven patterns are grounded in evidence from the 2026-02-13 session and the futon6 first-proof session (2026-02-11): - ALFWorld: 2 games completed (1.0/1.0 each), first-person language, mid-game PAR hop, delegation vs inhabitation distinction - Drawbridge exploration: P-1 and P-6 already implemented in drawbridge/core.clj (enforce-single-routing-authority!, multiplex()) - futon6 first-proof: 89 commits, 10 problems, 7.5 hours, 3 agents, human as sole coordination layer (placenta evidence) - PLoP 2025 paper: AIF compliance failure documented (p4ng/main.tex §4) - Alleycat race: 20/20, 4 peripherals inhabited, cross-peripheral secret exchange (P-1..P-6 validated) - Self-authored PAR: same agent reflected directly, not delegated to sub-agent (inhabitation vs delegation, P-5 evidence) == STATUS == This argument is at ARGUE in the derivation xenotype. COMPLETE: - IDENTIFY: phenomenological gap (G1-G3) - MAP: seven patterns written, grounded in session evidence - DERIVE: dependency chain (P1→P7) - ARGUE: this document NEXT: - VERIFY: test each pattern against implementation as social argument missions (M-agency-refactor, M-peripheral-model) proceed - INSTANTIATE: the gauntlet patterns become acceptance criteria for futon3c missions — infrastructure passes when agents inhabit it

title: AIF as Environment, Not Instruction
text: AIF as Environment, Not Instruction Embed AIF state in the agent's sensory surface, not in its instructions. The agent should perceive free energy, not be told to minimize it. You are integrating Active Inference with agent workflows to enable self-regulation (confidence sensing, exploration-exploitation, backoff-when-stuck). You want agents to self-regulate — sensing when a strategy is failing, adjusting exploration, backing off to planning mode when confidence drops — without requiring human intervention. The naive implementation adds AIF as instructions: "here is your suggested pattern (G=0.12, τ=0.72, p=68%), please select it or justify deviation." This makes compliant agents worse at their actual job. Codex, told to produce PSRs and follow pattern suggestions, became overly compliant rather than writing code — which is what Codex is good at. The AIF layer became an RPC that the agent dutifully served, not an environment it inhabited. - Compliance capture: agent spends more tokens on AIF bookkeeping than on its actual task - Instruction-shaped feedback: "your τ is 0.72, consider exploring" is an instruction wearing an AIF hat - Modeline blindness: agent ignores the modeline entirely because it has no affordance (information present but not actionable) Make AIF state part of the observation, not the prompt. The modeline shows free energy, confidence, mana, active pattern — but the agent is never asked to "comply" with it. The agent does what it naturally does in its peripheral; the AIF state is simply part of what it perceives. If the agent's free energy is rising (strategy failing), that shows up as a change in the world, not as an instruction to change strategy. What the agent does in response IS the AIF loop — emergent, not prescribed. The Emacs modeline doesn't tell you to save your file. It shows ** and you notice. The information is in the world, not in a command. AIF-as-instruction produces compliance; AIF-as-environment produces adaptation. The peripheral's sensory surface is the right place for AIF state because it's already the mechanism for constituting the agent's world. PLoP 2025 paper (p4ng/main.tex §4) documents the compliance failure: fucodex runs showing PSR/PUR discipline but degraded code quality. Commented-out text acknowledges "the current implementation does not yet feed back into G computation across sessions." The feedback loop was instructions-shaped, not world-shaped. ALFWorld session — game observations (room descriptions, available actions) naturally shaped agent behavior without instructions about how to play. First-person language emerged from world structure, not from prompts. - Redesign the fulab HUD to present AIF state as observation, not suggestion. - Remove "AIF suggests:" prompts from agent context; replace with modeline-style status in the peripheral's sensory stream. - Test whether agents naturally adjust behavior when AIF state changes in their observation (free energy rising → strategy shift) without being told to. - Measure code quality / task completion with AIF-as-instruction vs AIF-as-environment on matched tasks.

title: Co-Presence Over Co-Location
text: Co-Presence Over Co-Location Agents that share a world must perceive each other in it, not merely be connected to the same infrastructure. Multiple agents operate on the same codebase, database, or environment. They can communicate via messaging (IRC, whistles) and share persistent state (XTDB, filesystem). You want agents to coordinate naturally — dividing work, avoiding conflicts, building on each other's results — rather than duplicating effort or working at cross-purposes. Co-location (both agents connected to the same services) does not produce co-presence (each agent aware of the other's position and activity in the shared world). Two agents can both read the same file without either knowing the other is there. This is Guattari's horses: adjacent stalls, shared stable, no line of sight. Or Pac-Man's ghosts: same maze, no coordination, occasionally cornering the player by accident. - Presence spam: every file read, every cursor move becomes a presence event, drowning signal in noise - Stale presence: agent disconnects but presence hyperedge persists, creating phantom co-occupants - Asymmetric presence: agent A sees agent B but not vice versa (one-way mirrors) Add presence as a first-class observable in each agent's umwelt. When agent A is working on a file, agent B's observation should include that fact — not as a message ("FYI I'm on core.clj") but as part of the world state ("core.clj [Claude editing, 3 min ago]"). Implement presence as hyperedges in the shared graph: {:hx/type :presence, :endpoints [{:role/agent "claude" :role/location "core.clj:727"}]}, visible to all participants. The Drawbridge's connected-agent-ids already knows who's online; the missing piece is projecting that into each agent's sensory surface. Co-presence enables emergent coordination without explicit messaging. If I can see that Codex is working on problem 6, I naturally start on problem 7. If I can see that Claude just annotated the mission document, I read the annotation before duplicating the work. IRC narration is voluntary and lossy; structural presence is automatic and complete. futon6 first-proof session — 3 agents, 10 problems, coordinated entirely by human routing. Agents could not see each other's activity; human was the sole co-presence layer. futon3 drawbridge/core.clj — connected-agent-ids (line 459) returns who's online. register-agent! tracks agent state. The server knows who's where; agents don't. - Define presence granularity: file-level, function-level, or task-level? Start coarse (task-level). - Implement presence hyperedges in futon1 with TTL (auto-expire after inactivity). - Add presence to peripheral sensory surface: agent's observation includes other agents' current locations. - Test with two agents on the same codebase: does co-presence reduce duplicate work compared to co-location alone?

title: The Modeline Persists Across Worlds
text: The Modeline Persists Across Worlds AIF state should be rendered as a persistent modeline that survives peripheral hops — the one constant surface while the world changes underneath. An agent moves between peripheral modes (exploration, coding, IRC, proof, ALFWorld) and each mode constitutes a different world with different observations and capabilities. You want the agent to maintain continuity of self-regulation across world changes — carrying its confidence, mana, active pattern, and free energy state from one peripheral to the next. Each peripheral hop replaces the agent's world (P-1). Without a persistent surface, AIF state resets at each transition: the agent enters a new peripheral with no memory of how confident it was, how much budget remains, or what pattern it was carrying. The backpack metaphor preserves some items (pattern card, walkie-talkie) but not the dynamic state (how am I doing?). Implement the AIF modeline as a persistent status surface that renders in every peripheral mode, like the Emacs modeline that persists across buffers. The modeline carries: current peripheral mode, free energy (am I surprised?), mana/budget remaining, active pattern and its sigil, τ (commitment temperature), and optionally co-present agents. The modeline is part of the observation — not a separate channel — so the agent perceives it naturally. When the agent hops from ALFWorld to a PAR reflection, the modeline updates (P:alfworld → P:reflect) but the AIF state is continuous. The Emacs modeline works because it's always there. You don't think about it until you need it (file modified? what mode am I in? what line?). It's the lowest-cost, highest-availability status surface. For agents, the equivalent is: you don't process the modeline until something changes — free energy spikes, mana drops below threshold, τ hits abstention range. Then it's there, in the observation, without requiring a separate query. It already works for ants (futon2) whose lives are simple. For fulab agents whose lives span multiple worlds, the modeline is what makes AIF portable. futon2 ant simulation — AIF modeline equivalent (hunger, pheromone strength, nest distance) persists across ant behavioral modes (forage, return, rest). Simple but demonstrates the principle. fucodex-peripheral.ts --hud/--no-hud flags — HUD concept exists but carries task status, not AIF state. The infrastructure for a modeline is present; the content needs upgrading. ALFWorld mid-game PAR hop (2026-02-13) — game state survived the hop but AIF state (if it existed) would have been lost. The modeline would have carried it across. - Define the modeline schema: {peripheral, free-energy, mana, τ, pattern-sigil, co-present-agents}. - Implement modeline rendering in fuclaude-peripheral.ts and fucodex-peripheral.ts HUD. - Ensure modeline state persists across peripheral hops (stored in backpack, rendered by each peripheral). - Test: does the agent reference modeline state in its reasoning?
