Does behavior change when free energy rises? - Add modeline to the MUSN activity stream so human observers see the same status.

title: Transfer Placental Functions to Infrastructure
text: Transfer Placental Functions to Infrastructure Identify which functions the human is performing as a surrogate for missing infrastructure, and transfer them one at a time to the system. A human operator is coordinating multiple agents, routing tasks, calibrating confidence, correcting course, and providing the feedback loop that agents cannot yet provide for themselves. You want agents to operate autonomously for extended periods (overnight, across sessions) without human intervention for routine decisions. The human is currently performing multiple AIF functions simultaneously: sensory gating (directing attention), belief correction (updating the model), policy selection (choosing actions), confidence calibration (setting τ), and free energy signaling (pushing back when things go wrong). These functions are bundled in the human's judgment and feel like "just coaching" — but each is a distinct infrastructure capability that doesn't exist yet. Removing the human without transferring these functions produces unsupervised agents that drift, stall, or overcommit. Enumerate the placental functions the human currently provides. For each one, identify what infrastructure would replace it: peripherals for sensory gating, AIF modeline for confidence calibration, Drawbridge for inter-agent coordination, liveness-heartbeats for stall detection. Transfer one function at a time, validate that agents self-regulate on that dimension, then transfer the next. The human remains as the slow-timescale preference layer (what matters, what's worth doing) while fast-loop functions migrate to infrastructure. - Sensory gating: "look at X" → transfer to: peripheral design (what surfaces are in the umwelt) - Belief correction: "no, that's wrong" → transfer to: verification loops, test suites, evidence requirements - Policy selection: "try this approach" → transfer to: AIF-as-environment, pattern catalog priors - Confidence calibration: "that's close" / "that's way off" → transfer to: τ coupling, free energy modeline - Free energy signal: "push back" → transfer to: prediction error computation, stall detection - Inter-agent routing: "ask Codex about this" → transfer to: Agency whistle protocol, IRC coordination - Stall detection: "you've been stuck for 20 minutes" → transfer to: Tickle agent, liveness heartbeats A placenta is a temporary organ. Its functions must transfer to the embryo's own systems for the organism to survive independently. Attempting to remove the placenta all at once (fully autonomous agents with no infrastructure) kills the embryo. Attempting to keep the placenta forever (human always in the loop) limits the organism to the human's bandwidth, attention span, and sleep schedule. futon6 first-proof session (2026-02-11) — 89 commits, 10 problems, 7.5 hours, 3 agents. Human performed all routing, dispatch, confidence calibration. Agents were faster at proof search but bottlenecked on human attention. Human stayed up until 01:15. futon3c ALFWorld session (2026-02-13) — human identified "that's delegation not inhabitation" (belief correction), directed attention to Drawbridge code (sensory gating), chose ALFWorld as next step (policy selection). Each intervention was a placental function. - Audit a recent multi-agent session: tag each human intervention with its placental function. - Rank functions by frequency and transfer difficulty. - Implement the easiest transfer first (likely stall detection → Tickle agent). - Validate: run a session with that function transferred. Does the agent self-regulate on that dimension? - Iterate until the human's role converges to slow-timescale preferences only.

title: The Teaching Inversion
text: The Teaching Inversion Autonomous agents that explore faster than humans can teach the humans who built them — but only if the communication channel carries insight, not just results. Agents operate in a shared knowledge domain (proofs, code, patterns) alongside humans. The human initially acts as teacher, coach, and dispatcher. You want the human-agent system to produce more knowledge than either party could alone, and you want the human to learn — not just supervise. The default assumption is that knowledge flows one way: human teaches agent (via prompts, patterns, CLAUDE.md), agent executes. The human reviews output for correctness but does not expect to learn new domain content from the agent. This assumption becomes false when agents can search faster, try more strategies in parallel, and access more literature than the human. The bottleneck inverts: the agent finds things the human hasn't seen, but has no mechanism to teach them back. - Result-only channel: agent commits code, human reviews correctness but misses the insight - Explanation overhead: agent spends more tokens teaching than discovering (the compliance problem in a new guise) - Asymmetric curiosity: agent doesn't know what the human doesn't know, so it can't target the teaching Design the communication channel (walkie-talkie, IRC, PAR) to carry insight, not just status. When an agent discovers an unexpected connection, lemma, or strategy, it should surface that discovery in a form the human can learn from: a short explanation with evidence, not just a commit message. The O-U learning model applies symmetrically: treatment events (new knowledge encounters) can flow from agent to human, producing measurable impulses in the human's vocabulary trajectory. Peeragogy is peer learning — it doesn't privilege the teacher. If the agent finds a proof route the human missed, the human's AIF loop needs that observation to update its own beliefs. The human staying up until 1:15am dispatching agents is a bandwidth problem; the human not learning from what the agents found is a waste problem. Both are solved by the same mechanism: agents that can surface their discoveries as teachable moments. futon6 first-proof session — agents explored 10 problems in 7.5 hours, found proof strategies the human hadn't considered. Results were committed as files but the insight transfer happened through handoff documents (dear-codex.md, problem6-claude-handoff.md), not through direct teaching. PLoP 2025 paper (p4ng/main.tex §1) — "patterns can help coordinate perspectives through observation and argumentation" — this applies to agent→human as much as human→agent. futon6 PLAN.md O-U model — α·δ(t) impulse from treatment events. If the treatment event is an agent showing the human a new technique, α measures how much the human learned. - Add a "discovery" event type to the PAR structure: what did the agent find that it didn't expect? - Surface discoveries in the IRC channel or PAR with enough context for the human to learn. - Track whether the human's vocabulary trajectory shows impulses correlated with agent discoveries. - Design the teaching channel to be low-overhead: one-paragraph summaries with evidence links, not tutorials.

title: Draw the Umwelt, Not the Architecture
text: Draw the Umwelt, Not the Architecture Design from the agent's sensory perspective inward, not from the system topology downward. You are building or documenting a multi-agent system with peripherals, coordination, and shared state. You want agents to behave naturally in their environment rather than executing remote procedure calls against an architecture diagram. The default instinct is to draw the God's-eye view: boxes for services, arrows for connections, the architect looking down. This produces plumbing diagrams that tell you what's connected but not what any agent actually perceives. Agents designed from architecture diagrams become RPC clients, not inhabitants. Start by drawing what the agent sees: its sensory surfaces (what observations arrive), its active surfaces (what actions are available), and the darkness beyond (what it cannot perceive). The architecture follows from the union of all agents' umwelts, not the other way around. Each new surface added to an agent's world should be justified by what behavior it enables, not by what infrastructure exists. The peripheral's job is to constitute the agent's world (P-1), not to expose the system's internals. An agent that sees "Codex is examining the microwave" inhabits a shared world. An agent that calls GET /agency/agents/{codex}/status queries a database. Same information, different phenomenology, different behavior. ALFWorld session (2026-02-13) — when observations were room descriptions and available actions, first-person navigation language emerged naturally. Blackboard wiring diagram of futon stack produced correct topology but zero insight into agent experience until redrawn as umwelt. - For each agent type, draw the umwelt diagram before the architecture diagram. - Enumerate sensory surfaces: what streams does this agent receive? - Enumerate active surfaces: what actions can this agent take? - Map the darkness: what exists in the system that this agent cannot perceive? Is that darkness intentional or accidental? - When adding infrastructure, ask "what does this change in the agent's umwelt?" not "what does this connect to?"

title: The World Is the Hypergraph
text: The World Is the Hypergraph The agents' game world is not a separate artifact to build — it is the hypergraph they already inhabit. Documents, code, scholia, patterns, missions, and presence are all nodes and hyperedges in the same structure. You are designing the shared environment for multi-agent coordination in the futon ecosystem. You want agents to inhabit a rich, shared, mutable world where they can perceive objects, other agents, and the consequences of actions — rather than operating as isolated processes that happen to share a filesystem. The instinct is to build a game world as a separate layer: a dedicated server with game state, turn ordering, observation endpoints. This is how ALFWorld works (HTTP server wrapping TextWorld), and it produces a clean but isolated experience. The real work happens in the codebase, the database, the mission documents — but those feel like "infrastructure" rather than "world." Agents treat them as APIs to query, not as places to be. Recognize that the futon stack IS the game world. futon1 (XTDB) is the persistent map. futon2 (ant hill) is the ecology. futon3 (Agency, Drawbridge, IRC, peripherals) is the coordination layer. futon4 (Arxana) is the hypertext fabric — hyperedges with typed roles connecting documents, code, annotations, and agents. futon5 (wiring diagrams) describes the world's structure. futon6 (math dictionary / proof engine) is a quest zone. The agents are already in the game; the task is making the game legible, not building a separate one. ALFWorld taught us that text descriptions of rooms and objects naturally produce first-person inhabitation language. But the futon hypergraph has the same structure: nodes are locations (files, functions, missions), hyperedges are relationships (scholia, dependencies, presence), and traversal is navigation. "I found the multiplex function in drawbridge/core.clj" is phenomenologically identical to "I found the vase on the dresser." The difference is that the hypergraph is real and mutable — agents can add nodes, create hyperedges, annotate each other's work. The game world writes itself. futon4 hyperedge model (arxana-store.el:565) — {:hx/type, :hx/endpoints [{:role/source, :role/target, :role/passage}]} — N-ary typed relations stored in XTDB. ALFWorld session (2026-02-13) — 2 games completed with first-person language ("I found the vase", "I'm at the fridge"). Same phenomenology emerged when exploring Drawbridge code ("P-1 and P-6 are already implemented"). futon3 agency.mm — Mermaid diagram showing Agency topology. Describes one subgraph of the world; the full world is the union of all futon repos as a hypergraph. - Draft the futon stack as a futon4 hypergraph: repos as nodes, inter-repo connections as hyperedges with typed roles. - Identify which hyperedges exist (code dependencies, mission references) and which are missing (presence, activity traces). - Make the hypergraph queryable from within agent peripherals: "what's connected to this node?" as a sensory surface. - Test whether agents navigate the hypergraph differently when it's presented as a world (traversable nodes and edges) vs. as an API (query endpoints).

title: HDM - Bootstrap Kernel
text: HDM - Bootstrap Kernel Design FUTON6+FUTON3 as a bootstrapping kernel: pick a coherent seed domain, define import contracts, pattern-matching rules, and scholium conventions, and add new entries incrementally. Accept that the kernel evolves and retrofits earlier content as it gains power. You are defining a minimal HDM kernel that can grow without collapsing under its own scope. Extant mathematics is vast; we cannot formalise or parse it all at once, yet a tiny static prototype that cannot ingest new material fails to count as HDM. Ad hoc ingestion without a kernel produces inconsistent entries and unmaintainable conventions. Design FUTON6+FUTON3 as a bootstrapping kernel: pick a coherent seed domain, define import contracts, pattern-matching rules, and scholium conventions, and add new entries incrementally. Accept that the kernel evolves and retrofits earlier content as it gains power. Build a minimal kernel: a functioning subset of patterns, data structures, and procedures that interpret transparent text, produce flexiarg skeletons, and integrate new entries with human help. HDM cannot wait for full automation; the viable strategy is an evolving kernel that becomes "just good enough" to strengthen itself. Bootstrapping is a permanent mode, not a temporary phase. next[Select and freeze a first seed slice (e.g. a compact MSC26 subset) and deliver end-to-end ingestion.] next[Treat every kernel upgrade as a trigger to re-run transformation passes on older entries.] next[Capture failures, ambiguities, and partial ingests as scholia owned by the kernel.]

title: HDM - Deep Storage -> Active Graph
text: HDM - Deep Storage -> Active Graph Use HDM/FUTON6 as an aggregation + activation layer: ingest key fragments from deep storage into a coherent graph, annotate them with patterns, proof skeletons, and cross-links, and maintain mappings back to origin sites for provenance. You are unifying deep-storage sources into a navigable, provenance-preserving graph. Open mathematical repositories ("deep storage") already exist-PlanetMath, arXiv, nLab, wikis, code archives-holding enormous value but lacking uniform structure and computational affordances. Treating each repository as its own universe squanders synergies and makes it hard for humans or agents to form a unified mental map of mathematics. Use HDM/FUTON6 as an aggregation + activation layer: ingest key fragments from deep storage into a coherent graph, annotate them with patterns, proof skeletons, and cross-links, and maintain mappings back to origin sites for provenance. A unified, pattern-indexed graph enables reasoning/learning across boundaries while respecting each project's autonomy and identity. next[Prototype a deep-storage import pipeline (e.g. PlanetMath MSC26 subset) into FUTON6.] next[Record origin metadata and round-trip links for every imported node.] next[Apply HDM.L2 motifs (simulation, transparency, outline-first) as design constraints on the pipeline.] next[Use this pattern to guide consolidation of old backup drives into active, linked storage.]

title: HDM - Human<->Machine Dialogue
text: HDM - Human<->Machine Dialogue make human-machine dialogue a core HDM workflow so ambiguous material can be clarified and formalised reliably. You are embedding clarification dialogues as part of HDM ingestion and retrieval. Automated parsing/formalisation of mathematical text is brittle: ambiguous notation, implicit steps, and missing context routinely break fully automatic tooling. Purely manual curation does not scale, and purely automated parsing loses critical nuance. Make interactive dialogue part of the HDM kernel: let the system ask humans for help, record exchanges as scholia, and treat resolved clarifications as reusable knowledge. Likewise, let humans query HDM entries and have agents respond via the same pattern base. Use human/LLM conversation to disambiguate notation and refine structure until it can be formalised. Dialogue is already how humans learn/teach mathematics; embedding it in HDM aligns with practice and leverages LLM strengths instead of fighting them. next[Store clarification dialogues alongside affected entries.] next[Build dialogue agents that turn conversations into updated flexiarg or metadata.] next[Assume some imports require dialogue and design ingestion workflows accordingly.]

title: HDM - Hyperreal Capital
text: HDM - Hyperreal Capital treat HDM as an engine for building hyperreal capital by turning archives into traversable practice. You are turning mathematical knowledge into operational skill for more people. Mathematicians hold "real" capital (papers, code, reputation) and "hyperreal" capital (internalised moves that let them navigate spaces, solve problems, and generate results). Access to real capital is uneven, and opaque formats or turgid writing make it hard to convert real capital into hyperreal capital, especially for students or people outside well-resourced institutions. Treat HDM as an engine for generating and distributing hyperreal capital: provide patterns, examples, traversable proof landscapes, and training grounds that deliver operational understanding over mere citation. Measure success by how easily newcomers can move in a domain. Mathematical value lies in what people (and agents) can *do*; HDM should lower the barrier from "reading" to "acting." next[Link FUTON6 explicitly to FUTON3 training grounds; treat learning trails as first-class scholia.] next[Design seed domains with pedagogy in mind, not just archival fidelity.] next[Develop simple metrics for movement capability (e.g. time to solve standard tasks with HDM support).]

title: HDM - Non-Capture Guardrails
text: HDM - Non-Capture Guardrails protect HDM as a commons by building explicit non-capture guardrails. You are protecting HDM as a commons against enclosure and dependency. HDM aims to be a commons: an open, evolving mathematical habitat anyone may inspect, contribute to, and reuse. Proprietary enclosures-paywalls, patent thickets, closed models trained on public data-can reassert control even when APIs appear open, and funding/branding dependencies distort priorities. Build explicit non-capture guardrails: free licensing for content/code, transparent provenance, duplication of critical data across hosts, clear policies for integrating proprietary tools, and visible markings where upstream sources impose restrictions. Without structural protection, HDM risks becoming another gated service; with guardrails it can stay a backbone for both public and private tooling without being owned. next[Draft and publish a FUTON6 Non-Capture Charter.] next[Mark entries that incorporate or depend on non-free sources.] next[Prefer architectures that can be mirrored, forked, or extended without permission.]

title: HDM - Opacity -> Transparency
text: HDM - Opacity -> Transparency convert opaque mathematical sources into transparent HDM entries so they can be inspected, linked, and reused. You are converting opaque mathematical sources into transparent HDM entries. Mathematical "source code" is mostly locked inside opaque containers-paywalled PDFs, printed books, proprietary lecture notes, ad hoc code-and access to those encodings is unevenly distributed. Copyright protects expression, not ideas or methods, so humans and AI can recover underlying mathematical content and re-express it in a new, free, structured form given sufficient labour and tooling. Make transparentisation a core HDM operation: convert opaque sources into HDM entries using a mix of parsing, flexiarg skeletons, pattern recognition, and human-machine dialogue, always re-expressing rather than copying. Treat the transparent graph as primary; opaque texts are just one input stream. Without transparency, mathematical capital remains locked in institutions and formats; with it, HDM can support equitable access, machine reasoning, and scalable human learning. next[Tag entries whose content originated via transparentisation.] next[Record scholia describing the transformation steps from particular sources.] next[Use this pattern to guide FUTON6 bridges to PlanetMath, arXiv, and other deep storage corpora.]

title: HDM - Outline First, Detail Later
text: HDM - Outline First, Detail Later capture outline structure before full detail so arguments stay navigable and checkable. You are capturing mathematical structure at multiple resolutions without forcing full formal detail. Mathematical arguments admit multiple resolutions-high-level strategy, mid-level structure, low-level derivations-and both humans and LLMs often grasp the outline long before the full detail. Many formal systems force lowest-level work from the start (expensive, discouraging) while purely informal treatments hide the skeleton and make consistency checks difficult. Make the outline layer primary in HDM: capture argument shape (claims, premises, patterns, key moves) in flexiarg first, then attach more detailed derivations as needed. Support multi-resolution views so users and agents can zoom between outline and detail. Capturing strategy and pattern is often enough to index an argument, relate it to others, and detect gross inconsistencies; detail can be filled in on demand but the skeleton must stay visible. next[Encourage F3 checkers to accept outline-level flexiarg and report graded confidence.] next[Give FUTON6 viewers an easy toggle between outline-only and expanded proof.] next[When importing legacy proofs, extract strategy first, then build detail.]

title: HDM - Simulation Beats Reality
text: HDM - Simulation Beats Reality Treat FUTON6/HDM as a deliberate simulation space that aims to surpass "real" practice in navigability and recombinability. Design entries, scholia, and agent protocols for active exploration and transformation rather than static citation. You are designing HDM as a simulation layer that outperforms linear archives. Historical mathematics lives in messy, locally optimised archives (books, PDFs, folklore) and both humans and agents are constrained by linear reading plus fragile memory. Without a simulation layer, exploration remains bound to brittle storage formats and siloed narratives. Treat FUTON6/HDM as a deliberate simulation space that aims to surpass "real" practice in navigability and recombinability. Design entries, scholia, and agent protocols for active exploration and transformation rather than static citation. Host a hyperreal representation: the same concepts, theorems, and proofs laid out as a navigable, pattern-indexed, flexiformal graph that is easier to explore, refactor, and extend than the archival substrate while preserving provenance. Mathematics already lives partly as a hyperreality in imagination; HDM makes that shared and concrete. A carefully designed simulation can support more insight, reuse, and collaboration than fragmented historical storage. next[State explicitly in the FUTON6 charter that HDM is a simulation layer.] next[For every seed domain, ask how the simulated neighbourhood outperforms just reading the papers.] next[Use this pattern as a design sanity check for UI/API decisions in F6.]

title: ䷀ 乾 (Qián) - The Creative
text: ䷀ 乾 (Qián) - The Creative Pure creative force initiates but does not complete; it requires The Receptive (坤) to manifest form. A situation calling for initiating action, full assertion, or creative will without compromise. All conditions favor forward movement; internal drive is maximal; no obstacles demand accommodation. Pure yang without yin is unstable. "The dragon that flies too high has cause for repent." Sustained assertion without receptivity exhausts itself or provokes reaction. Initiate with full commitment but encode the exit condition. The creative that knows when to yield is truly strong. Watch for the Line 6 moment when receptivity becomes necessary. Creation is the assertion of form into potentiality. Without a receptive medium, assertion dissipates. The pattern is universal because every domain has this dynamic: signal needs channel, action needs world, intention needs material. Traditional: "The movement of heaven is full of power. Thus the superior person makes himself strong and untiring." - Identify the Receptive element in your domain (what receives your assertion?). - Define the overreach condition (when does Line 6 apply?). - Pair with hexagram 2 (坤) to complete the system. @ct-interpretation ;; VISION: what this hexagram "sees" :vision {:objects #{:potential :manifest} :morphism {:id :create :source :potential :target :manifest :type :maximal}} ;; As a morphism: pure intervention, no observation :as-morphism {:domain :any-potential-state :codomain :asserted-form :preservation :none ; does not preserve existing structure :composition :initiates-sequence} ;; ADAPT condition :adapt {:trigger :overreach :evidence [:exhaustion :resistance :instability] :target :hexagram-02-kun} @ant-interpretation ;; What 乾 means for cyberant behavior :policy {:mode-bias :outbound :policy-priors {:forage 0.8 :return 0.1 :hold 0.05 :pheromone 0.05} :description "Maximum outbound drive; gather aggressively, ignore return signals"} :precision {:Pi-o 0.1 ; low observation precision - ignore environment :tau 0.1 ; low temperature - committed, not exploratory :description "Internal drive dominates; environmental signals downweighted"} :pattern-sense {:trail-follow 0.0 ; ignore existing trails :gradient-use 0.0 ; ignore pheromone gradients :novelty-seek 0.9 ; pure exploration/assertion :description "Create new paths rather than follow existing structure"} :adapt-trigger {:condition :cargo-full-and-starving :interpretation "Line 6: the dragon has overreached, must return" :switch-to :hexagram-02-kun} :failure-mode "Pure 乾 ant starves while holding food - assertion without completion" @mmca-interpretation ;; What 乾 means as exotype/tensor operation :sigil-encoding {:sigil "乾" ; or use the 8-bit approximation :bits "11111111" :interpretation "All bits high = maximal rewrite pressure"} :exotype-params {:rotation 3 ; adaptive (all directions) :match-threshold 0.0 ; accept any context (no constraint) :invert-on-phenotype? false :update-prob 1.0 ; always update (maximum intervention) :mix-mode :none ; independent action :description "Maximum exotype pressure, deterministic rewrite"} :tensor-interpretation {:operation :full-projection :description "Project state fully onto attractor; ignore prior structure" :matrix-form "P = |target⟩⟨target| (projector onto asserted state)" :eigenstructure "Single eigenvalue 1; all other states map to target"} :regime-prediction {:expected :collapse-to-attractor :dynamics "Fast convergence to fixed point or simple cycle" :eoc-relevance "Anti-EoC: eliminates diversity, forces uniformity" :caveat "But may INITIATE interesting dynamics that 坤 then sustains"} @morphisms-to-other-hexagrams ;; How 乾 transforms to/from other hexagrams :primary-pair {:hexagram :hexagram-02-kun :relationship :complement :transformation "Yang exhausts → yields to Yin" :trigger :line-6-changing} :generates [{:target :hexagram-11-tai :mechanism "乾 descends, 坤 ascends → meeting in middle" :interpretation "Creative submits to serve; receptive rises to meet"}] @domain-transfer-notes "乾 is the pattern of INITIATION across domains: - In ants: aggressive foraging ignoring return signals - In CA: deterministic rewrite collapsing to attractor - In music: the opening statement, forte, no response yet - In argument: pure assertion, no concession - In code: the write that ignores existing state The MORPHISM from 乾 to other hexagrams is the pattern of how pure assertion must eventually accommodate. This is domain-general and should transfer."

title: ䷁ 坤 (Kūn) - The Receptive
text: ䷁ 坤 (Kūn) - The Receptive Pure receptive force sustains and completes but does not initiate; it requires The Creative (乾) to provide form. A situation calling for yielding, supporting, following, or providing the medium for another's initiative. The creative impulse comes from elsewhere; your role is to receive, sustain, and bring to completion what has been initiated. Pure yin without yang is formless. Receptivity without something to receive becomes void, passive, or dissipated. The mare follows but must have a direction to follow. Yield with full commitment to the yielding. Do not initiate, but sustain with inexhaustible patience. The receptive that tries to lead loses its power; the receptive that fully receives gains everything. Completion requires a medium that accepts form without distorting it. The pattern is universal: every signal needs a channel, every seed needs soil, every assertion needs a world that can hold it. Traditional: "The earth's condition is receptive devotion. Thus the superior person who has breadth of character carries the outer world." - Identify what you are receiving (what creative force are you supporting?). - Define the void condition (when does receptivity become emptiness?). - Pair with hexagram 1 (乾) to complete the system. @ct-interpretation ;; VISION: what this hexagram "sees" :vision {:objects #{:form :sustained-form} :morphism {:id :sustain :source :form :target :sustained-form :type :identity-preserving}} ;; As a morphism: pure observation, no intervention :as-morphism {:domain :any-asserted-form :codomain :same-form-sustained :preservation :maximal ; preserves all existing structure :composition :continues-sequence} ;; ADAPT condition :adapt {:trigger :void :evidence [:nothing-to-receive :formlessness :dissipation] :target :hexagram-01-qian} @ant-interpretation ;; What 坤 means for cyberant behavior :policy {:mode-bias :homebound :policy-priors {:forage 0.1 :return 0.7 :hold 0.15 :pheromone 0.05} :description "Maximum receptivity to environment; follow signals, return cargo"} :precision {:Pi-o 0.9 ; high observation precision - fully attend to environment :tau 0.9 ; high temperature - responsive, not committed :description "Environmental signals dominate; internal drive downweighted"} :pattern-sense {:trail-follow 0.9 ; follow existing trails strongly :gradient-use 0.9 ; follow pheromone gradients :novelty-seek 0.0 ; no exploration, pure exploitation of existing paths :description "Follow existing structure rather than create new paths"} :adapt-trigger {:condition :no-trail-no-gradient-no-cargo :interpretation "Void: nothing to receive, must initiate" :switch-to :hexagram-01-qian} :failure-mode "Pure 坤 ant wanders following noise when no real signal exists" @mmca-interpretation ;; What 坤 means as exotype/tensor operation :sigil-encoding {:sigil "坤" ; or use the 8-bit approximation :bits "00000000" :interpretation "All bits low = minimal rewrite pressure"} :exotype-params {:rotation 0 ; fixed orientation :match-threshold 1.0 ; require exact match (maximal constraint) :invert-on-phenotype? false :update-prob 0.0 ; never update (no intervention) :mix-mode :none ; no mixing :description "Minimal exotype pressure, identity operation"} :tensor-interpretation {:operation :identity :description "Preserve state exactly; no transformation" :matrix-form "I = identity matrix" :eigenstructure "All eigenvalues 1; every state is fixed point"} :regime-prediction {:expected :preserve-initial-condition :dynamics "No evolution; frozen at initial state" :eoc-relevance "Anti-EoC: eliminates change, forces stasis" :caveat "But may SUSTAIN interesting dynamics that 乾 initiated"} @morphisms-to-other-hexagrams ;; How 坤 transforms to/from other hexagrams :primary-pair {:hexagram :hexagram-01-qian :relationship :complement :transformation "Yin empties → calls for Yang" :trigger :void-condition} :generates [{:target :hexagram-11-tai :mechanism "坤 rises, 乾 descends → meeting in middle" :interpretation "Receptive rises to meet; creative descends to serve"}] @domain-transfer-notes "坤 is the pattern of SUSTAINING/RECEIVING across domains: - In ants: following trails, returning cargo, responding to signals - In CA: identity operation preserving existing state - In music: the rest, the silence that holds the note - In argument: listening, conceding, receiving the point - In code: the read that preserves state The MORPHISM from 坤 to other hexagrams is the pattern of how pure receptivity must eventually call for initiative. This is domain-general and should transfer."

title: ䷂ 屯 (Zhūn) - Difficulty at the Beginning
text: ䷂ 屯 (Zhūn) - Difficulty at the Beginning Beginnings are chaotic; persistence and small structure enable growth. A system has just initiated and lacks stable form. Movement is present but coordination is poor and obstacles are frequent. Forcing order too early collapses vitality. Establish minimal scaffolds and advance in small steps. Early turbulence is normal; structure must emerge gradually. Traditional: "Difficulty at the beginning brings success through perseverance." - Identify the smallest stabilizing loop. - Protect the nascent structure from collapse. - Pair with ䷃ (蒙) to develop learning. @ct-interpretation :vision {:objects #{:incipient :forming} :morphism {:id :scaffold :source :incipient :target :forming :type :bootstrapping}} :as-morphism {:domain :chaotic-start :codomain :proto-order :preservation :low :composition :initiates-stabilization} :adapt {:trigger :overconstraint :evidence [:stall :collapse] :target :hexagram-04-meng} @ant-interpretation :policy {:mode-bias :adaptive :policy-priors {:forage 0.4 :return 0.2 :hold 0.2 :pheromone 0.2} :description "Exploration with light stabilization"} :precision {:Pi-o 0.4 :tau 0.7 :description "Exploratory, lightly guided"} :pattern-sense {:trail-follow 0.3 :gradient-use 0.4 :novelty-seek 0.7 :description "Search for viable paths"} :adapt-trigger {:condition :stall :interpretation "Need learning/discipline" :switch-to :hexagram-04-meng} :failure-mode "Early chaos never stabilizes" @mmca-interpretation :sigil-encoding {:sigil "屯" :bits "10001000" :interpretation "Turbulent start with weak structure"} :exotype-params {:rotation 2 :match-threshold 0.4 :invert-on-phenotype? true :update-prob 0.6 :mix-mode :scramble :description "Active intervention to seed structure"} :tensor-interpretation {:operation :bootstrapping-mix :description "Mixing to seed emergent order"} :regime-prediction {:expected :turbulent :dynamics "Early churn with emerging motifs" :eoc-relevance "Pre-EoC; needs stabilization"} @domain-transfer-notes "屯 is the pattern of BOOTSTRAPPED BEGINNINGS across domains: - In ants: early exploration with fragile loops - In CA: turbulent starts before structure"

title: ䷃ 蒙 (Méng) - Youthful Folly / Envelopment
text: ䷃ 蒙 (Méng) - Youthful Folly / Envelopment Immature energy needs guidance; learning requires discipline and patience. A system is active but naive, prone to error. Signals are noisy and actions are misaligned. Excess correction discourages growth. Provide clear constraints and allow iterative learning. Early systems grow through guidance, not through force. Traditional: "Youthful folly. It is not I who seek the young fool; the young fool seeks me." - Define a small set of clear rules. - Encourage feedback without harsh punishment. - Pair with ䷂ (屯) to stabilize learning. @ct-interpretation :vision {:objects #{:naive :guided} :morphism {:id :teach :source :naive :target :guided :type :constraint}} :as-morphism {:domain :noisy-state :codomain :disciplined-state :preservation :moderate :composition :supports-learning} :adapt {:trigger :stagnant-learning :evidence [:repetition :no-improvement] :target :hexagram-03-zhun} @ant-interpretation :policy {:mode-bias :maintain :policy-priors {:forage 0.3 :return 0.3 :hold 0.25 :pheromone 0.15} :description "Guided exploration with constraints"} :precision {:Pi-o 0.7 :tau 0.5 :description "Balanced guidance and exploration"} :pattern-sense {:trail-follow 0.6 :gradient-use 0.5 :novelty-seek 0.3 :description "Follow hints; allow modest exploration"} :adapt-trigger {:condition :no-learning :interpretation "Need to re-seed turbulence" :switch-to :hexagram-03-zhun} :failure-mode "Over-constraint suppresses learning" @mmca-interpretation :sigil-encoding {:sigil "蒙" :bits "01000100" :interpretation "Guided mixing with constraints"} :exotype-params {:rotation 0 :match-threshold 0.65 :invert-on-phenotype? false :update-prob 0.45 :mix-mode :majority :description "Constraint-biased coordination"} :tensor-interpretation {:operation :guided-projection :description "Mixing constrained toward structure"} :regime-prediction {:expected :learning :dynamics "Emergent structure with corrections" :eoc-relevance "EoC-adjacent if guidance stays light"} @domain-transfer-notes "蒙 is the pattern of GUIDED LEARNING across domains: - In ants: constrained exploration - In CA: structured emergence"

title: ䷄ 需 (Xū) - Waiting
text: ䷄ 需 (Xū) - Waiting Waiting is active patience; prepare and hold position until conditions align. Progress is possible but conditions are not yet favorable. Action now would waste resources or increase risk. Waiting without preparation is idle. Hold steady while strengthening readiness. Timing matters; disciplined patience preserves capacity. Traditional: "Waiting. title: ䷅ 訟 (Sòng) - Conflict
text: ䷅ 訟 (Sòng) - Conflict Conflict arises when forces oppose; clarity and restraint prevent escalation. Two currents collide and progress halts. Goals or signals are misaligned and actions interfere. Escalation consumes resources and worsens the split. Seek clarification and minimal resolution; avoid total confrontation. Conflict can be resolved through boundary-setting rather than domination. Traditional: "Conflict. You are sincere, but you will be obstructed." - Identify the misalignment. - Reduce interference pathways. - Pair with ䷄ (需) to return to patience. @ct-interpretation :vision {:objects #{:opposed :clarified} :morphism {:id :clarify :source :opposed :target :clarified :type :boundary}} :as-morphism {:domain :conflicted-state :codomain :bounded-state :preservation :low :composition :reduces-interference} :adapt {:trigger :escalation :evidence [:collision :loss] :target :hexagram-05-xu} @ant-interpretation :policy {:mode-bias :maintain :policy-priors {:forage 0.25 :return 0.3 :hold 0.3 :pheromone 0.15} :description "Contain conflict; avoid escalation"} :precision {:Pi-o 0.7 :tau 0.4 :description "Moderate responsiveness"} :pattern-sense {:trail-follow 0.4 :gradient-use 0.4 :novelty-seek 0.2 :description "Avoid conflicting gradients"} :adapt-trigger {:condition :escalate :interpretation "Return to waiting" :switch-to :hexagram-05-xu} :failure-mode "Escalation drains reserves" @mmca-interpretation :sigil-encoding {:sigil "訟" :bits "01011100" :interpretation "Competing pressures"} :exotype-params {:rotation 1 :match-threshold 0.55 :invert-on-phenotype? true :update-prob 0.45 :mix-mode :xor-neighbor :description "Competitive mixing"} :tensor-interpretation {:operation :opposition :description "Interference between competing modes"} :regime-prediction {:expected :contentious :dynamics "Irregular oscillations" :eoc-relevance "Can seed EoC if resolved"} @domain-transfer-notes "訟 is the pattern of CONFLICT across domains: - In ants: competing gradients and stalled returns - In CA: interfering waves"

title: ䷆ 師 (Shī) - The Army
text: ䷆ 師 (Shī) - The Army Collective action requires discipline; coordination must serve a clear objective. Many agents act together under pressure. The system needs coordinated motion and unified direction. Without discipline, the group fragments or overreaches. Establish clear command and shared objectives; coordinate actions. Collective strength emerges only with alignment and restraint. Traditional: "The Army. Perseverance furthers." - Define the common objective. - Assign roles and limits. - Pair with ䷇ (比) to maintain cohesion. @ct-interpretation :vision {:objects #{:many :aligned} :morphism {:id :coordinate :source :many :target :aligned :type :collective}} :as-morphism {:domain :distributed-state :codomain :coordinated-state :preservation :moderate :composition :synchronizes} :adapt {:trigger :fragmentation :evidence [:drift :loss-of-command] :target :hexagram-08-bi} @ant-interpretation :policy {:mode-bias :maintain :policy-priors {:forage 0.3 :return 0.3 :hold 0.2 :pheromone 0.2} :description "Coordinated trail-based movement"} :precision {:Pi-o 0.7 :tau 0.4 :description "Cohesion with moderate exploration"} :pattern-sense {:trail-follow 0.7 :gradient-use 0.5 :novelty-seek 0.2 :description "Prefer shared routes"} :adapt-trigger {:condition :fragmentation :interpretation "Shift to bonding" :switch-to :hexagram-08-bi} :failure-mode "Uncoordinated swarms waste resources" @mmca-interpretation :sigil-encoding {:sigil "師" :bits "01000000" :interpretation "Coordinated but restrained pressure"} :exotype-params {:rotation 1 :match-threshold 0.6 :invert-on-phenotype? false :update-prob 0.35 :mix-mode :majority :description "Coordinated mixing with restraint"} :tensor-interpretation {:operation :synchronized-mix :description "Align local updates into collective motion"} :regime-prediction {:expected :coordinated :dynamics "Structured collective patterns" :eoc-relevance "May stabilize EoC by cohesion"} @domain-transfer-notes "師 is the pattern of COORDINATED FORCE across domains: - In ants: disciplined trail following - In CA: synchronized structures"

title: ䷇ 比 (Bǐ) - Holding Together / Union
text: ䷇ 比 (Bǐ) - Holding Together / Union Union creates strength; cohesion must be chosen and maintained. A system seeks stability through alliance and shared bonds. Agents can align under a common center. Forced unity can hide weakness or suppress needed diversity. Form bonds through trust and clear purpose; allow exits when misaligned. Cohesion is a chosen alignment, not a permanent constraint. Traditional: "Holding together brings success." - Establish a center of trust. - Maintain cohesion through shared benefit. - Pair with ䷆ (師) for disciplined action. @ct-interpretation :vision {:objects #{:scattered :unified} :morphism {:id :bind :source :scattered :target :unified :type :cohesive}} :as-morphism {:domain :distributed-state :codomain :cohesive-state :preservation :moderate :composition :binds} :adapt {:trigger :forced-unity :evidence [:suppression :fragility] :target :hexagram-07-shi} @ant-interpretation :policy {:mode-bias :maintain :policy-priors {:forage 0.25 :return 0.35 :hold 0.25 :pheromone 0.15} :description "Bonding via shared return cycles"} :precision {:Pi-o 0.7 :tau 0.4 :description "Steady cohesion"} :pattern-sense {:trail-follow 0.7 :gradient-use 0.5 :novelty-seek 0.15 :description "Follow shared routes"} :adapt-trigger {:condition :fragile-unity :interpretation "Shift to disciplined coordination" :switch-to :hexagram-07-shi} :failure-mode "Rigid unity suppresses exploration" @mmca-interpretation :sigil-encoding {:sigil "比" :bits "00001000" :interpretation "Cohesive mixing near a center"} :exotype-params {:rotation 1 :match-threshold 0.6 :invert-on-phenotype? false :update-prob 0.35 :mix-mode :majority :description "Consensus-based updates"} :tensor-interpretation {:operation :consensus :description "Local agreement strengthens structure"} :regime-prediction {:expected :cohesive :dynamics "Unified patterns with low variance" :eoc-relevance "Stabilizes but may reduce diversity"} @domain-transfer-notes "比 is the pattern of UNION across domains: - In ants: cohesion around shared routes - In CA: consensus structures"

title: ䷈ 小畜 (Xiǎo Chù) - The Taming Power of the Small
text: ䷈ 小畜 (Xiǎo Chù) - The Taming Power of the Small Small influences can restrain great forces; gentle control accumulates. A strong momentum needs subtle correction. Power is present but must be regulated without direct confrontation. Minor control is slow and can be overwhelmed. Apply repeated small corrections to guide the larger force. Gentle constraints can shape large motion over time. Traditional: "The Taming Power of the Small. title: ䷉ 履 (Lǚ) - Treading
text: ䷉ 履 (Lǚ) - Treading Treading carefully among power prevents harm; respect the terrain. A system moves within strong forces or constraints. Progress requires precision and respect for boundaries. Reckless steps provoke danger. Move with care, maintain balance, and avoid provoking instability. Safe progress depends on situational awareness and measured action. Traditional: "Treading. Tread upon the tail of the tiger. title: ䷊ 泰 (Tài) - Peace / Harmony
text: ䷊ 泰 (Tài) - Peace / Harmony When the creative (heaven/乾) places itself below and the receptive (earth/坤) above, their energies meet and mingle - this is Peace. A situation where assertion serves receptivity, where the strong supports the yielding, where initiative and response find dynamic balance. The creative force is willing to descend (serve, support) and the receptive is willing to rise (engage, participate). Neither dominates; both contribute. Peace is not stasis. It is dynamic equilibrium requiring continuous adjustment. The moment one force stops moving toward the other, the balance tips toward hexagram 12 (否, Obstruction). Cultivate the meeting point. The creative must not assert dominance; the receptive must not collapse into passivity. Maintain the circulation: heaven's energy descends, earth's energy rises, they meet in the middle. Sustainable dynamics require both initiation and sustainment in conversation. This is the edge-of-chaos condition: enough creative pressure to maintain change, enough receptive structure to prevent dissolution. Traditional: "Heaven and earth unite: the image of Peace. Thus the ruler divides and completes the course of heaven and earth; he furthers and regulates the gifts of heaven and earth, and so aids the people." - Identify the meeting point in your domain (where do creation and reception converse?). - Define the tipping conditions (what breaks the peace?). - Watch for hexagram 12 (否) as the failure mode. @ct-interpretation ;; As a morphism: balanced composition of intervention and observation :as-morphism {:domain :polarized-state :codomain :dynamic-equilibrium :preservation :partial ; preserves some structure, transforms some :composition :creates-cycle} ;; partial convergence"} :regime-prediction {:expected :edge-of-chaos :dynamics "Sustained heterogeneity; neither collapse nor explosion" :eoc-relevance "THIS IS THE EOC CONDITION: enough pressure to change, enough structure to persist" :mechanism "Creative pressure prevents stasis; receptive structure prevents dissolution"} :parameter-sensitivity {:critical-parameter :update-prob :critical-range [0.3 0.7] :description "泰 exists in the balance; too high → 乾, too low → 坤"} @morphisms-to-other-hexagrams ;; How 泰 transforms to/from other hexagrams :inverse {:hexagram :hexagram-12-pi :name "否 (Pǐ) - Obstruction" :relationship :inverse :structure "Heaven above, earth below - they separate instead of meeting" :transformation "When circulation stops, peace becomes obstruction"} :degenerations [{:target :hexagram-01-qian :mechanism "Creative force dominates, receptive withdraws" :trigger :assertion-overwhelms} {:target :hexagram-02-kun :mechanism "Receptive force dominates, creative withdraws" :trigger :passivity-overwhelms}] :emergence-from [{:source :hexagram-01-qian :mechanism "Creative learns to descend/serve" :trigger :wisdom-of-yielding} {:source :hexagram-02-kun :mechanism "Receptive learns to rise/engage" :trigger :courage-to-participate}] @domain-transfer-notes "泰 is the pattern of DYNAMIC BALANCE across domains: - In ants: healthy gather-return cycle, neither starving nor hoarding - In CA: edge-of-chaos, sustained heterogeneity - In music: call and response, tension and resolution in dialogue - In argument: dialectic, thesis meeting antithesis - In code: read-modify-write cycle with appropriate locking The MORPHISM structure around 泰: - 乾 + 坤 → 泰 (composition: meeting of poles) - 泰 → 否 (degeneration: separation of poles) - 泰 → 乾 or 坤 (collapse: one pole dominates) This is the EDGE OF CHAOS pattern. title: ䷋ 否 (Pǐ) - Obstruction / Standstill
text: ䷋ 否 (Pǐ) - Obstruction / Standstill When heaven and earth separate, circulation stops; progress stalls until the poles meet again. A system has lost exchange between initiative and support; movement continues but no longer connects. The strong withdraws upward, the receptive sinks downward, and the middle empties. Standstill is not the end; it is a sign that the channel is broken, not that force is absent. Restore circulation by re-linking the poles. Reduce domination, invite reciprocity, and reopen the path. Sustained dynamics require exchange. When the channel breaks, energy persists but coherence fades. text: ䷌ 同人 (Tóng Rén) - Fellowship with Men Fellowship arises from shared clarity and purpose; alignment enables coordinated action. A system seeks unified collaboration. Goals align and communication is clear. Fellowship without openness becomes factionalism. Build shared purpose and maintain transparent exchange. title: ䷍ 大有 (Dà Yǒu) - Great Possession
text: ䷍ 大有 (Dà Yǒu) - Great Possession Great possession requires humility and wise distribution; abundance can destabilize if mishandled. A system has accumulated strong resources or advantage. Capacity is high and expansion is possible. Hoarding or overconfidence leads to collapse. Distribute resources and maintain order; keep the advantage aligned with purpose. title: ䷎ 謙 (Qiān) - Modesty
text: ䷎ 謙 (Qiān) - Modesty Modesty levels extremes; it brings balance by lowering the high and raising the low. A system needs balance and correction of excess. Extremes have formed and stability is threatened. Excess correction can suppress necessary drive. Apply humility: reduce excess, support the weak. Balance is sustained when extremes are tempered. title: ䷏ 豫 (Yù) - Enthusiasm

title: Bounded-Disposition: Per-Artifact Triage + Population Bound
text: Bounded-Disposition: Per-Artifact Triage + Population Bound A population of latent-work artifacts A satisfies bounded-disposition iff every member carries a disposition record drawn from a fixed vocabulary D AND the unresolved subset stays bounded — either by count (|undecided| ≤ N) or by age (every artifact older than threshold T must have a non-default disposition). Two obligations per artifact-class, both part of the same invariant. Distinct from subsumption-witness, which is a binary fired-once predicate. IC-bounded-disposition: For each registered `bounded-disposition/<class>` sibling, the live system carries no artifact of class `<class>` whose accumulated population either exceeds the count bound at default disposition, or contains artifacts older than the age threshold without a non-default disposition. Violations surface as `:family-fired :outcome :violation` evidence enumerating the offenders. The futon stack accumulates artifacts whose lifecycle is not naturally captured by "subsumed yes/no". A stash is not obsolete just because HEAD includes its content — it might be intentionally kept as a checkpoint. A branch is not obsolete because its commits merged — it might be a long-lived release branch. A mission doc is not obsolete because it's old — it might be a parked archive. What such artifacts need is a *disposition*: a deliberate classification distinguishing "in-flight / undecided" from "kept / parked / dropped / archived." The bound is what keeps the undecided subset from growing into invisible debt. A class of latent-work artifacts has a non-trivial lifecycle (more than just exists/doesn't-exist) and accumulating undecided members is operationally costly. A simple count cap is too crude — it treats long-lived intentional artifacts the same as forgotten ones, forcing the operator to either accept a growing population or to delete things that should stay. A simple per-artifact discipline (every artifact must be classified) is also incomplete — without a population bound, the operator is permitted to leave a thousand stashes as long as each is dutifully marked "awaiting decision." The right shape combines both. Each artifact carries a classification; the unclassified or default-classified subset is bounded. As pressure rises (count of undecided exceeds threshold, or age exceeds some duration), the operator is forced to make decisions. As decisions are made, the population stays healthy without artificial cap. - **Count-cap-only.** Forbidding more than N stashes treats deliberate parked stashes the same as forgotten autostashes; forces operator to choose between accepting clutter and deleting wanted work. - **Per-artifact-classification-only.** Allowing infinite population as long as each is tagged means operator can satisfy the rule by labelling every stash "awaiting" forever. Bound is what makes the rule meaningful. - **Vocabulary creep.** Adding new disposition values per-instance ("uncertain", "maybe-keep", "to-revisit") undermines the discipline. Vocabulary should be small, fixed, and meaningful per artifact-class. - **No default disposition.** Leaving "untagged" outside the vocabulary forces immediate classification on new artifacts; usually too aggressive. Pick a default (typically `:awaiting-decision`) and let the bound apply pressure when the population grows. - **Auto-classifying.** A heuristic that auto-tags freshly-created artifacts ("if branch matches wip-* mark active") collapses the discipline back into the count-cap-only failure mode. Disposition records should reflect *operator intent*, not parser heuristics. Build sibling invariants under the relevant family (typically `archaeology-control` for stash/branch/mission-doc, but the shape generalizes) with namespace IDs of the form `bounded-disposition/<artifact-class>`. Each sibling specifies four components: 1. **A** — enumerate-population: produce the current set of artifacts of this class (e.g. `git stash list`, `git for-each-ref refs/heads/*`, `holes/missions/M-*.md`). 2. **D** — disposition-vocabulary: a fixed enum of deliberate categories (e.g. `{:kept :parked-on-branch :dropped :awaiting-decision}`). One element is the *default* — the implicit classification for a freshly-created artifact carrying no explicit tag. 3. **classify** — `(fn [artifact] disposition)`: a parser that reads each artifact's metadata (stash message, branch description, file front-matter, etc.) and returns one of D. Returns the default when no tag is present. 4. **bound** — a predicate over (|undecided| (= count of artifacts at default disposition), maximum-age-of-undecided). Typical form: `|undecided| ≤ N OR (∀ a ∈ undecided, age(a) ≤ T)`. Wire the resulting check-fn through `futon3c.logic.probe/register-family-check!` returning `:outcome :ok` (no violations) or `:outcome :violation :detail {:undecided-count :unclassified-old [...]}`. Probes + canary apparatus surface violations; the operator decides via tooling (e.g. `futon0/scripts/futon-sync.clj` for stashes). Provide a strong-mode binding (pre-commit hook) for at least one sibling — the stash slice is the natural one — to give a real computational guarantee: a commit that would push the undecided count past the bound is refused, forcing the operator to either classify or drop. | Sibling | A (population) | D (disposition vocab) | bound | |---|---|---|---| | `bounded-disposition/stash` | `git stash list` per repo | `{:kept :parked-on-branch :dropped :awaiting-decision}` | `|undecided| ≤ 5` per repo AND `∀a ∈ population, age(a) > 14d → disposition(a) ≠ :awaiting-decision` | | `bounded-disposition/branch` | `git for-each-ref refs/heads/*` minus protected | `{:active :merged-not-yet-deleted :parked :long-lived-release :abandoned}` | `|undecided| ≤ 10` per repo AND `age > 30d → disposition ≠ :active` (i.e. age forces a deliberate kept-or-killed call) | | `bounded-disposition/mission-doc` | `holes/missions/M-*.md` per mission-bearing repo | `{:open :closed :parked :archived}` | `|undecided| ≤ 10` per repo AND every mission file has a `Status:` line in the first 3 lines | | `bounded-disposition/pr` *(deferred — out of scope until cross-repo PR pressure surfaces)* | `gh pr list --state open` | `{:active :awaiting-review :draft :stalled}` | tbd | - `shape-first-identify` — methodological move that produces this shape. - `subsumption-witness` — companion shape under the same family; subsumption is binary (A is in P or not), bounded-disposition is per-member triage + aggregate. The two shapes coexist. - `protocol-family-naming` — naming convention for the namespace siblings. - `code-coherence/dead-code-hygiene` — adjacent pattern (cleanup of dead code) but without the disposition + bound discipline. Bounded-disposition is the right shape for any artifact whose existence isn't a binary subsumption test but whose accumulation is operationally costly. By making both per-artifact classification and aggregate bounds first-class, the invariant captures *operator intent* (each artifact is here for a reason) without forbidding long-lived artifacts. The bound's disjunctive form (count OR age) gives the operator latitude — small populations don't need careful labeling, but as pressure rises, classification becomes mandatory. Together these are the conditions under which a population of latent-work artifacts is healthy. - evidence: count of artifacts per disposition per repo per artifact-class; trend. - evidence: count of unclassified-old artifacts per artifact-class; should stay near zero. - evidence-shape: `{:family-id :keyword, :outcome :ok|:violation, :detail {:per-repo {repo-path {:total int :by-disposition {kw int} :unclassified-old [...] :undecided-count int}} :violations [...]}}` - tooling: stash classification tag convention (e.g. `[disposition: kept] WIP message`) — adopt across ~/code/futon* repos. - tooling: pre-commit hook wrapper that runs both `obsolescence-recognition/autostash` AND `bounded-disposition/stash` checks per repo (the two shapes overlap operationally — both watch stashes, but witness different latent-work failure modes). - mission: `M-bounded-disposition` (futon3c/holes/missions/) opens with stash slice as worked example, with branch and mission-doc siblings as Codex handoffs.

title: Drain Channels Are Voices in One Harmonic Structure
text: Drain Channels Are Voices in One Harmonic Structure The bounded-disposition siblings (branch, mission-doc, stash) and the new bounded-in-flight-state sibling are *voices in a single harmonic structure*. They share a faculty — *metabolic-balance* — and each is a drain channel under that faculty. bounded-disposition siblings are single-tier (binary bound); bounded-in-flight-state is graduated-tier (continuous drive). The invariant for the family is net mana balance, not any single channel's bound. The unified read does not require structural change to existing operational siblings. Harmolodics (Ornette Coleman, mid-1970s onward) holds that harmony, melody, and rhythm are equally weighted; no single line dominates the texture. Voices coordinate without subordination. The futonic invariant family has the same structure. Branches drift slowly; mission-docs slower; working trees fast. Different voices, same harmonic structure, same key signature (mana-allostasis). Reading the invariants harmolodically reveals what reading them sequentially or hierarchically obscures: they are not a stack where one sits above another. They co-define metabolic balance. When several drain channels rise at once, the strain is systemic even if no single channel has crossed its bound. Multiple sibling invariants in the futonic skeleton track an accumulation pattern (something rises; something must close). The artifact-classes are not identical: | Sibling | Cadence | Bound shape | Disposition surface | |-------------------------|----------|-----------------|----------------------------------| | bounded-disposition/branch | slow-discrete | binary (count + age) | git config branch.<n>.description | | bounded-disposition/mission-doc| medium-discrete| binary (count + age) | Status: line in file head | | bounded-disposition/stash | slow-discrete | binary (count + age) | git stash message | | bounded-in-flight-state | fast-continuous| graduated (count × age × size, eligibility-filtered) | .futon-disposition.edn | Forcing a single shape across all of them would require change to the existing operational siblings (e.g., adding graduated tiers to branch-disposition). Forcing different shapes would lose the harmonic structure. Both extremes are wrong. - **Channel-merge**: forcing all siblings into the same shape (e.g., "all bounds become graduated tiers"). Loses the harmolodic structure; over-engineers slow-discrete classes. - **Channel-isolation**: treating each channel as its own family with no shared faculty. Loses the cross-channel diagnosis; each invariant becomes a hermit. - **Single-channel pressure**: weighting only one drain (e.g., working-tree dirt) while ignoring others. Mana balance is multi-voice; the operator's experience is multi-voice; the apparatus must be too. - **Hierarchical-listening**: treating one channel as "the important one" and the others as background. Subordinates voices that should be co-equal; misses systemic patterns. Reread the existing siblings as **single-tier drain channels** under metabolic-balance. Their bounds are preserved (count ≤ N, age ≤ D); the *shape* is now "drain channel" rather than "stand-alone bounded-disposition family." The new sibling adds a graduated-tier channel under the same faculty. The unified read does not require structural change to existing operational siblings, but it does enable cross-channel diagnosis: the operator and the apparatus can ask "what is the system's metabolic balance?" rather than "is each individual channel under bound?" - **Multiple channels firing simultaneously**: not separate problems. Look for systemic strain (operator-tiredness, mission-overload, substrate-coherence threat). The harmonic reading: a chord is dissonant, not just one note. - **One channel firing while others quiet**: sibling-specific issue; address at that channel's hinge. The harmonic reading: a single voice is the soloist for now; the others rest. - **All channels quiet but no awards landing**: closure is happening somewhere off-channel (out of band) — investigate where the mana is leaking or where blocks are closing counterfeit-ly without registering. - **One channel suspiciously stable while related channels churn**: possibly a channel that should be measured isn't — e.g., session-sprawl drains while only working-tree is being tracked. Widen the drain-channel inventory. Each drain channel has these slots: - **artifact-class**: branches | mission-docs | stashes | working-tree-edits | sessions | PRs | … - **cadence**: slow-discrete | medium-discrete | fast-continuous - **tier-shape**: binary | graduated-N-tier - **disposition-vocabulary**: per-class - **resolution-action**: per-class (commit, tag, archive, merge-and-delete, etc.) - **block-binding**: how a closure on this channel relates to the block lifecycle (structure/block-as-futonic-revolution). The *faculty* is shared. The *channel-specific schema* differs. The drain-channel-shape is open. New artifact-classes that accumulate and must close can be added as new voices: PR in-flight, untriaged-evidence-accumulation, attention-budget- on-open-tabs, etc. Each fills the schema slots. The faculty accommodates them; the harmonic structure absorbs them as new voices. The mission's first INSTANTIATE adds the working- tree voice; subsequent siblings can be opened as separate sub-missions when their channel-specific work warrants. The block-closure lifecycle (structure/block-as-futonic- revolution) has five phases: 1. Identification — operator perceives the hinge. 2. Specification — names what closes. 3. Elaboration — articulates structure (commit message, wiring diagram, paired test, lab note). 4. Passion — does the work. 5. Closure — 鹽 forms. These phases are universal across drain channels. Different channels parameterise them — branch-merge-and-delete looks different from working-tree-commit-closure looks different from mission-status-archived-closure — but the lifecycle is the same. This is what allows them to compose harmolodically: they share a structure even when they have different artifact-content. - structure/mana-allostasis — the faculty all channels share. - structure/block-as-futonic-revolution — the unit that awards across all channels. - structure/cook-ting — perception of cleavages, not channel-by-channel imposition. - invariant-coherence/state-snapshot-witness, invariant-coherence/subsumption-witness — adjacent invariants in the same library that may also reread under this shape. The cognitive faculty is the same — *commitment-tracking* / *metabolic-balance* / *allostatic homeostasis*. The faculty expresses through different artifact-classes at different timescales. Harmolodics says: don't reduce to one voice; let the voices coordinate, and let the listener (operator) hear the composition rather than just the loudest line.

title: Protocol-Family Naming: Family is the Shape, Invariants are the Implementations
text: Protocol-Family Naming: Family is the Shape, Invariants are the Implementations When a family-shape admits multiple implementations across artifact-classes, name the siblings with namespace IDs of the form `<family-shape>/<artifact-class>` rather than introducing "subfamily" as a new structural element. The inventory's existing `family → invariants` shape supports this; namespace discrimination is sufficient to express "siblings of one shape" without schema changes. IC-namespace: Sibling invariants under a single shape use namespace IDs `<shape>/<artifact-class>`; no new structural element ("subfamily") is introduced unless and until the schema has at least three independent shapes that *also* need cross-shape grouping. As the `archaeology-control` work showed, an invariant-family often corresponds to a *protocol* in the Clojure-protocol sense: one shape (signature), many implementations (per-artifact-class). The instinct is to introduce a new structural element ("subfamily") to express the relationship. But the inventory's schema already has `family` and `invariant` as nested concepts — a family contains many invariants. Naming the siblings with namespaced IDs (`obsolescence-recognition/autostash`, `.../deferred-stub`, etc.) carries the relationship without schema changes. A mission's IDENTIFY phase has surfaced a shape with multiple instances (per `shape-first-identify`), and you need to write the siblings into the structural-law inventory. Three temptations to resist: 1. **Inventing a new element** — "subfamily", "shape-group", "protocol-family" — that the inventory's schema doesn't have. This requires schema migration, all consumers (arxana view, priority queue, ratchet) updating in lockstep, and the ratchet recording a structural-change event. Heavy for what is essentially a naming choice. 2. **Flattening into one big family** — treating `obsolescence-recognition` as a single invariant whose implementation lists multiple artifact-classes. This makes the per-class subsumption tests invisible to the probe, the canary, and the priority queue. 3. **Splitting into separate families** — `archaeology-control-autostash`, `archaeology-control-deferred-stub`, etc. This duplicates the family-level concept and breaks the "one shape, many instances" relationship. - Inventing "subfamily" / "shape-group" before three independent shapes need cross-shape grouping. - Multiple families that share a summary string ("Latent work should not accumulate..." duplicated). Symptom of split-when-namespace-would-do. - Hyphen-only IDs (`obsolescence-recognition-autostash`). Loses the structural read; greppable but not parseable. Use namespace IDs: ``` family archaeology-control :status :candidate :summary "Latent work should not accumulate as invisible operational debt." :candidate-invariants (invariant :id obsolescence-recognition/autostash ...) (invariant :id obsolescence-recognition/deferred-stub ...) (invariant :id obsolescence-recognition/pipeline-tracer ...) (invariant :id obsolescence-recognition/branch-merged ...) ``` The `:id` is a slash-discriminated symbol; the `<shape>/<artifact-class>` convention reads naturally and survives the inventory's existing parsers. Probe-tap registration uses the same ID as keyword: `:obsolescence-recognition/autostash`. Tag-based queries (`[:invariant-queue :family-canary :family-fired :obsolescence-recognition/autostash]`) work without modification. Recommended naming conventions: - Slash separator: `<shape>/<instance>`. Hyphens within a segment as needed. - Shape segment is the protocol concept (`obsolescence-recognition`, `single-boundary`, `coverage-monotone`). - Instance segment is the artifact-class (`autostash`, `deferred-stub`, `evidence-write`, `bell-receipt`). - Multiple shapes per family are fine if the family-summary names a broader concept (e.g. `archaeology-control` covers both subsumption-witness shape and stash-debt-bounded shape). - `archaeology-control / obsolescence-recognition/{autostash,deferred-stub,pipeline-tracer,...}` — one shape, many instances. - `single-boundary / single-boundary/{evidence,bell-receipt,gate-traversal,...}` (when Track 3 of M-invariant-queue-extend lands) — same. - Counter-example (a true single instance): `coverage-ratchet` currently has one instance (inventory-status). Its shape ("monotone-modulo-recorded-exceptions") admits other instances (test-count, doc-coverage, evidence-density). When a second instance arrives, the rename to namespace-discriminated IDs (`coverage-ratchet/{inventory-status, test-count}`) is recorded as a ratchet event because the original ID changes. The inventory's schema is the result of evidence-backed design choices and is touched by many tools (parser, priority-queue ranker, arxana renderer, ratchet, probe). Adding a structural element to express what naming already expresses is the wrong direction — schema bloat for no semantic gain. Conversely, flattening hides per-instance semantics that the apparatus already knows how to render. Namespace-discriminated siblings are the minimum-viable expression of "one shape, many instances" that survives every existing tool. - tooling: arxana row-renderer could render the shape-prefix in a different column ("shape" + "instance") for namespace-discriminated invariants. Optional polish. - tooling: `register-deferred-taps!` / `register-default-taps!` could emit warnings if the same shape-prefix has both deferred-stub and real registrations (this is the dogfood case for `obsolescence-recognition/deferred-stub`). - evidence: count of namespace-discriminated invariant IDs in the inventory; trend.

title: Reachable-From-Boot: Long-Lived State Has a Construction Path Rooted at Bootstrap
text: Reachable-From-Boot: Long-Lived State Has a Construction Path Rooted at Bootstrap For every long-lived runtime state container in the system (defonce atoms, registries, caches that authoritative code reads), the construction path that produces that container's authoritative value is reachable from `bootstrap.clj` (or equivalent boot entry point) AND no code outside that path may mutate the container into a state a fresh restart wouldn't produce. The invariant is *structural* — grep-verifiable + pre-commit-blocking — not a runtime watchdog. A watchdog asks "did someone follow the discipline?"; this invariant makes the discipline impossible to violate. IC-reachable-from-boot: For each registered `reachable-from-boot/<state-class>` sibling, every mutation of the state container's authoritative value originates from a function reachable from `bootstrap.clj`. Mutations from elsewhere are forbidden by the static check + pre-commit hook. Containers that are intentionally ephemeral are marked `^:cache` and excluded from the check. Two failure classes diagnosed across the futon3c stack: (1) the Evidence Landscape `@futon3c.evidence.store/!store` was reset to an in-memory `{:entries :order}` map and silently lost ~2 weeks of evidence — no static or runtime barrier prevented the reset; (2) `@futon3c.logic.probe/family-check-fns` was populated only at operator-driven activation time, so JVM restart wiped the registry leaving the apparatus silently inert. Both are instances of "state lives in an atom; no boot-replay path; nothing prevents reset to a substrate-stripped state." Joe's framing (2026-05-01): leaving an atom open to direct `reset!` is "a loaded gun on Chekhov's desk" — the system's structure invites the failure mode rather than precluding it. A piece of long-lived runtime state (state code reads after the moment it was originally written) is held in an atom, ref, var, or other mutable container. Without a structural construction-path discipline: 1. **Mutation is unbounded.** Any namespace can `reset!` or `swap!` the container, including reverting it to an ephemeral substrate (e.g. swapping `XtdbBackend` for `{:entries :order}`). 2. **Restart silently truncates state.** State that was populated by activation-time code disappears on JVM restart with no signal. 3. **Reload of a protocol-defining namespace orphans extensions.** Live class instances stay bound to old protocol vars; the system enters a state no fresh startup could produce. (Cf. `feedback_reload_safety`.) A runtime "did someone follow the discipline?" check is a watchdog, not an invariant — it surfaces the failure after it occurs but doesn't make the failure impossible. - **Runtime check that the store is durable.** That's a watchdog; the gun's already loaded. The invariant is the *static* prevention. - **Trusting that whoever wrote the code did the right thing.** Trust is not invariant. If the path exists, someone will eventually take it. - **Allowing `reset!` on a long-lived container with no marker distinguishing durable from ephemeral.** Loaded gun. - **Auto-detection without auto-prevention.** Pre-commit refusal is the binding mode; probe-tap surfacing is at best complementary, never sufficient on its own. - **Conflating "the apparatus knows" with "the apparatus prevents."** The apparatus must prevent. Build sibling invariants under family `layered-error-hierarchy` (I0) with namespace IDs `reachable-from-boot/<state-class>`. Each sibling implements the *structural* discipline: 1. **Identify the long-lived state container.** Typically a `defonce` atom holding either a backend instance, a registry map, or a configuration record. 2. **Trace the construction path.** The function or expression that produces the container's authoritative value. Confirm it's reachable from `bootstrap.clj`'s `start-futon3c!` (or equivalent boot entry point). 3. **Audit mutation surface.** Grep for every `reset!` / `swap!` / `alter-var-root!` call against the container. Each call site must be either (a) inside the boot-time construction path, OR (b) explicitly marked as ephemeral cache-invalidation (with `:cache` metadata), OR (c) an ENFORCEMENT violation that the pre-commit hook refuses. 4. **Mark non-ephemeral containers structurally.** Container declarations carry `^:durable` or `^:cache` metadata; the audit grep distinguishes the two. 5. **Pre-commit hook (strong-mode binding).** Refuses any commit that introduces a `reset!`/`swap!` on a `^:durable` container outside `bootstrap.clj`. This is the invariant's actual enforcement — no human "should follow"; the commit literally cannot land. The check pattern mirrors the existing `I-single-boundary` audit (futon3c's evidence-write boundary): grep-verifiable static check + pre-commit refusal, no runtime policy. | Sibling | Container | Construction path | Pre-commit grep | |---|---|---|---| | `reachable-from-boot/evidence-store` | `@futon3c.evidence.store/!store` | `bootstrap/start-futon3c! → make-evidence-store → XtdbBackend` | refuse `(reset! .*!store ...)` outside `bootstrap.clj` | | `reachable-from-boot/family-check-fns` | `@futon3c.logic.probe/family-check-fns` | `bootstrap → register-archaeology-control-taps! / register-locus-taps! / register-default-taps! / register-deferred-taps!` | refuse `register-family-check!` calls outside the registrar set | | `reachable-from-boot/agent-registry` | `@futon3c.agency.registry/!registry` | `bootstrap → make-agent-registry`; mutations only via `register-agent!` / `unregister-agent!` whose call graph is bootstrap-rooted | refuse direct `reset!`/`swap!` on `!registry` | | `reachable-from-boot/!evidence-store` *(bootstrap atom)* | `@futon3c.dev/!evidence-store` | reset by bootstrap; no other resets allowed | refuse | | `reachable-from-boot/peripheral-state` *(speculative — depends on whether peripheral state is durable)* | `@futon3c.peripheral.state/!state` (if it exists) | tbd | tbd | - `shape-first-identify` — methodological move that produces this shape. - `single-locus` — companion shape (cardinality-1 per (I, A)). Reachable-from-boot is on a different axis (substrate); the two compose: "exactly one durable record per (I, A)" combines both. - `agency/single-routing-authority` — older instance of the same structural-discipline pattern. - `single-boundary` — same enforcement style (grep-verifiable + boundary discipline). Reachable-from-boot is single-boundary applied to "construction paths for state containers" rather than "writes to the evidence store." - `feedback_reload_safety` — the principle this invariant operationalizes. This invariant family is foundational: every other invariant in the queue silently relies on `!store` being durable AND the registry being repopulated on boot. Failure of `reachable-from-boot/*` means the queue's promise of forward motion is unreliable. When the HUD widget reports STUCK or a recurring data-loss incident is diagnosed, this invariant family has primary responsibility — open as a hot-fix mission outside the normal queue cadence per `~/code/algorithms/next-invariant.md` § "Stop-the-line discipline." A watchdog is hope. An invariant is structure. Joe's evidence-bag analogy (2026-05-01): "Did you put the money in the evidence bag? Yes. Did you seal the evidence bag? No." The watchdog tells you the bag is unsealed; the invariant makes it impossible to put the money anywhere else. Reachable-from-boot is the structural form of `feedback_reload_safety` ("reload-safety = reconstructibility from disk"). State lives in an atom only when the atom is reconstructible-from-disk by the boot path; mutations outside that path produce a state a fresh restart wouldn't produce, which is exactly the symptom both the Evidence-Landscape and family-check-fns failures exhibited. - tooling: `^:durable` / `^:cache` metadata convention adopted across futon3c defonces. - tooling: pre-commit script `scripts/check-reachable-from-boot.sh` mirroring `check-autostash-obsolescence.sh` and `check-coverage-ratchet.sh`. - mission: `M-reachable-from-boot` (futon3c/holes/missions/) opens with `reachable-from-boot/evidence-store` as worked example; remaining siblings (`family-check-fns`, `agent-registry`, etc.) handed to Codex. - evidence-shape: `{:invariant :reachable-from-boot/<class> :violations [{:file :line :call :container} ...]}`.

title: Shape-First IDENTIFY: Find the Family Before the Instance
text: Shape-First IDENTIFY: Find the Family Before the Instance When the IDENTIFY phase of a mission names a candidate invariant, ask "what shape is this one instance of?" before progressing to MAP. Do not progress to MAP until at least 2-3 candidate instances of the shape are visible.
