Active dynamic: early in a programme, evidence arrives slowly and cadence suffices; as measurement waves multiply, event-driven becomes more defensible; as the posterior tightens, cadence may again be appropriate. - Silent recompute: outputs change without readers being notified - Schedule-only, no events: major evidence waits for cadence; urgency of significant observations is lost - Events-only, no cadence: recomputes only when the author remembers; baseline continuity suffers - Timestamp-missing: outputs circulate without the information that would let readers correlate them with evidence - Log-as-theatre: recompute log exists but is uninformative ("rerun on 2026-05-01") Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. (1) Scheduled-only: weekly or monthly recompute on a declared cadence; all evidence arriving between recomputes waits. Gives up latency. (2) Event-driven: each T1 wave completion and each assumptions-v2.edn change triggers a recompute; no fixed calendar. Gives up predictability. (3) Hybrid: cadence for routine (monthly baseline recompute); event-driven for major waves (cross-institutional evaluation completion, significant assumption revisions). Gives up simplicity. The paper currently operates informally — recomputes happen when the author reruns. Operational use at UKRN-S requires a declared composition. Engaged when: every published recompute output carries a timestamp and evidence-revision identifier; the current schedule (or declared mix) is published; readers can see which evidence triggered the most recent recompute. Failing when: recomputes happen silently; readers cannot tell which version they are looking at; design-state changes propagate without recompute traceability. Self-application requires rerun: ukrns/self-application's claim is that the artefact instantiates its argument. Every rerun is a micro-instance of the cycle; a rerun that never happens leaves the claim aspirational. Measurement-wave pairing: ukrns/measure-where-least-sure commits to observations whose results will move the model. If those observations complete but the model does not recompute, the observational commitment is broken. The recompute schedule is how observations become model updates. Design-state versioning: ukrns/design-as-function-of-evidence requires that service changes trace to evidence updates. Every recompute is a candidate version-event; the schedule determines how the version lineage accrues. Predictability as commons good: institutions plan around the design state. Event-driven changes produce planning friction; cadence-driven changes produce planning predictability. The schedule is a service commitment to the network. Mechanic, in short: Mechanic: when and why the model reruns. Serves: self-application, computation-as-exploration, design-as-function-of-evidence, measure-where-least-sure. Axis: event-driven ↔ cadence-driven. Without this pattern: the notebook form is packaging, not method. - Declare the current composition in project documentation - Timestamp every notebook output with assumptions-v2.edn revision at point of compute - Publish a recompute log: when the model was rerun, what triggered it, what changed - Cross-reference with ukrns/design-state-lineage (the versioning mechanic downstream) - For paper time: even if informal, record the compute-date and evidence-revision in each published version

title: Make Local Success Shareable
text: Make Local Success Shareable A distributed training service does not become a learning system just because good work happens locally. Local success has to become shareable evidence: something that other institutions, partners, and funders can inspect, reuse, or act on. Every service event therefore sits on an axis between shareability gain and governance cost. The service should be explicit about what is worth sharing, what it costs to share it responsibly, and when the extra governance burden is justified. The current paper's background and synthesis point to the same problem from two directions. First, the three lines of evidence — training delivery, what can currently be measured, and sector priorities — are often not joined up. Second, funder and policy cycles matter to whether local work becomes visible beyond the institution that did it. A service that leaves training outcomes, evaluation findings, and operational learning trapped locally will keep recreating the same work in parallel and will struggle to build wider recognition for what it does. The pattern operates on the axis: shareability gain ↔ governance cost. Irreducible: making evidence portable, reusable, and externally legible usually requires extra governance work. Avoiding that work keeps things easy locally, but it also keeps the learning trapped. Real costs: some things are cheap to share, such as a training plan, a scaffold, or a summary of what was tried. Other things, such as downstream evaluation, cross-institution comparison, or evidence that could affect institutional reputation, require much more consent, handling, and trust. Active dynamic: the governance cost of sharing should fall as the network builds routine practice, trusted formats, and repeatable agreements. But it never falls to zero, and the service still has to choose where the higher-cost sharing really pays. - Local-success trap: good work happens, but no one outside the host institution can learn from it - Governance-free sharing: evidence is pushed outward without the consent, attribution, or handling needed to do it responsibly - Governance-without-reuse: governance effort is paid, but the resulting evidence is too thin or too obscure to matter - Post-dependent memory: the shared layer depends on a specific funded role and disappears when that role ends - Sector disconnect: the service shares internally but never in forms that connect to funder or partner conversations - Archive-without-consequence: evidence is technically deposited, but nothing downstream uses it Choose what to make shareable, and cost the governance honestly. (1) Low-governance shared layer: make planning materials, role definitions, routine findings, and annual scenario outputs shareable first, while holding back heavier cross-institution evidence until the governance surface is ready. Gives up some comparative power. (2) Governance-first build-out: invest early in the agreements and processes needed for higher-value cross-institution evidence sharing. Gives up speed. (3) Subset sharing: build the fuller shared layer with a smaller group of institutions willing to carry the burden first, and let the rest of the network inherit what is learned from that arrangement. Gives up uniformity. These compositions are not ranked in the abstract. The right one depends on what evidence the service most needs to move from local usefulness to network usefulness. Engaged when: the service can say what each event leaves behind for the network; the governance burden of sharing is named rather than assumed away; and the shared layer persists beyond the immediate funding cycle or project team. Failing when: every institution has to rediscover the same things for itself; governance work is performed ceremonially; or the shared artefacts disappear with the post or grant that created them. Network learning requires a shared layer: The paper's central move is from isolated training activity toward a coordinated learning system. That move fails if evidence never leaves the place where it was produced. Wider recognition depends on shareable evidence: Funders and policy actors cannot act on local success they cannot see. A service that wants sector-level standing needs forms of evidence that travel beyond the originating institution. Persistence matters as much as publication: A one-off shared output is not yet infrastructure. The pattern is about creating deposits that later cycles can inherit, revise, and build on. Governance is part of the work, not an afterthought: The question is not whether evidence should be shared in the abstract, but which evidence is worth sharing at which governance cost. Making that trade explicit is what keeps the pattern from becoming either secrecy by default or openness as a slogan. Mechanic, in short: Derived from the paper's need to connect local delivery, usable evidence, and sector recognition into one operating story. Answers the service-level version of the visible-impact and shared-maintenance problems: what one institution learns should become part of the network's usable memory. Mapped to the learning loop at the deposit step: evidence produced locally enters a shared layer so later actors can build on it. Coordination requirement: Low for routine artefacts, high for cross-institution evaluation and anything carrying reputational consequence. - Decide, for each class of event, what the network-level deposit is meant to be - State the governance cost of that deposit before treating it as routine - Prefer deposits that can survive role turnover and funding-cycle turnover - Make at least some outputs legible not only internally but to funders, partners, and incoming member institutions - Use this pattern alongside measurement selection and design revision, so shared evidence is both chosen deliberately and acted on

title: Provision at Network Scale, Selectively
text: Provision at Network Scale, Selectively Put a capability at network scale only when it genuinely pays at network scale. The current paper's five-role design makes this concrete: evaluator, convener, researcher-advisor, and parts of training management create cross-institution value that a single institution cannot easily recreate for itself, while institutional leads remain local because local uptake, local relationships, and local priorities cannot be centralised without losing the point. The discipline is not to centralise everything, and not to leave everything local, but to place each capability where its gains are real. The paper's design argument depends on cross-institution learning. That means some capabilities need a home above the level of any one institution: comparing evidence across sites, maintaining a common operational picture, carrying sector relationships, and stewarding the parts of the analytical toolkit that should not be reinvented locally. At the same time, institutions still need their own people to translate, adapt, and carry the work in context. The question is therefore not whether UKRN Services should act centrally or locally in general. It is which roles and functions only pay once they are placed at network scale. The pattern operates on the axis: local fit ↔ network leverage. Irreducible: the more a role is embedded in local context, the less it can serve many institutions at once. The more a role is built for comparison, shared maintenance, or sector coordination, the more it benefits from being held once above the institutional level. Real costs: network-scale provision gains comparability, continuity, and one-to-many efficiency, but it can lose local nuance and can become a single point of capacity risk. Local provision gains trust, context, and institutional fit, but it can duplicate work, compress too many functions into one person, and leave cross-institution learning under-provisioned. Active dynamic: the right placement can change as the service matures. A function that needs to be central in Year 1 may later support stronger local uptake. A function that is safely local in a small network may need more central support once the network grows. - Centralise-everything: UKRN Services absorbs roles whose value depends on local ownership - Leave-everything-local: cross-institution comparison, evaluation, and shared maintenance remain too thin to function - Role-compression return: local actors are expected to carry too many distinct functions at once - Hidden scale choice: a role is placed centrally or locally by habit, not by published reasoning - Context-blind centre: a network role operates without a route for local realities to reshape its work - Post-dependent centre: a central capability disappears with the grant or post that created it Place each role or capability where its main gain is real, and say why. (1) Capability-by-capability placement: keep institutional leads local, hold the evaluator and convener at network scale, keep methodological support above the day-to-day rhythm, and place training management where common coordination genuinely helps. This is closest to the current paper. It gives up the simplicity of one blanket rule. (2) Strong centre: place most capabilities in UKRN Services and use local actors mainly as contact points. Gives up local ownership and some contextual responsiveness. (3) Light centre: use UKRN Services mainly for convening and leave most capabilities local. Gives up much of the cross-institution learning that justifies the service in the first place. These compositions are not ranked in the abstract. The pattern exists to force an explicit argument role by role. Engaged when: the service can say for each role or capability what is gained by its current placement, what is lost, and why that loss is acceptable; the placement is revisited as the network grows. Failing when: centralisation or localisation is treated as a default ideology; institutions cannot see why a role sits where it does; or the same person is quietly carrying several roles because the scale choice was never really made. Cross-institution roles only pay at network scale: Evaluation comparison, convening across institutions, and stewardship of shared analytical or operational infrastructure all depend on seeing more than one institution at once. Those functions lose much of their value if they are fragmented into local copies. Context-bearing roles still need local ownership: Institutional uptake does not happen abstractly. Someone in or near the institution still has to carry the local relationships, timing, and translation work that the centre cannot honestly substitute for. The paper's evidence already points to under-provisioned shared capability: One of the design pressures the paper is responding to is that some forms of evaluation and cross-institution learning were simply not happening reliably at local level. Network scale is justified where the alternative is not a rich local version, but absence. Persistence matters: A network-scale capability is only worth building if it can survive the initial bootstrap and the funding cycle that enabled it. Otherwise the centre briefly carries the role and then drops it, leaving no durable gain behind. Mechanic, in short: Derived from the paper's five-role system and its claim that some cross-institution capabilities only pay once they are held above the single-institution level. Answers the service-level question of where shared capability should sit if the aim is real cross-institution learning rather than symbolic central coordination. Mapped to the learning loop at the provision step: once the service knows what needs to happen, it has to decide where that capability lives. Coordination requirement: Medium to high, depending on how many institutions depend on the capability and how much local variation it must absorb. - Maintain an explicit role-and-capability register stating what sits centrally, what sits locally, and why - Test each central role against a persistence question: would this capability survive beyond the bootstrap year and the post currently carrying it? - Keep a visible route by which institutional leads can reshape the work of central roles - Revisit placement at the Year-2 decision rather than assuming the bootstrap arrangement is permanent - Use this pattern downstream of diagnosis and alongside the evidence-selection pattern, since capability placement determines what the service can actually observe and compare

title: Publication Cadence — Canonical vs Snapshot Artefacts (Implementation Pattern)
text: Publication Cadence — Canonical vs Snapshot Artefacts (Implementation Pattern) A paper that is re-computable from evidence can be published in two forms: the living document (continuously updated, reflecting the current evidence state) and the snapshot (frozen at a moment, citable, DOI-bearing). The service states which composition it is running on the axis between living-only, snapshot-only, and both, and resolves the citation ambiguity that arises when a paper has multiple states. The publication composition is declared. Readers can find both the current state and a citable snapshot. Each snapshot declares its evidence-revision and compute-date. Citation paths are explicit. This implementation pattern specifies the artefact-publication mechanic behind ukrns/self-application. The meta-pattern claims the artefact instantiates its argument; this pattern addresses the practical question of how that artefact is published — as a moving target, a series of frozen snapshots, or both. Without a declared cadence, "which version am I reading" becomes unanswerable. The pattern operates on the axis: living document (continuously-updated canonical version) ↔ frozen snapshots (versioned fixed publications with citable identifiers). Irreducible: a single publication cannot be simultaneously maximally current AND maximally citable as a fixed object. Real costs: living costs archival durability — a snapshot citable today may differ from the same URL tomorrow; frozen costs currency — citable versions drift further from the current evidence state over time. Active dynamic: early drafts favour living (claims are forming); as claims stabilise, snapshots become appropriate; archival norms for academic work favour snapshots. - Ambiguous citation: "the paper" cited by URL changes silently; citing reader sees different content than intended - Living-without-history: current version has no revision history; prior states irrecoverable - Snapshots-without-revisions: snapshots exist but do not declare their evidence-revision; cannot be reproduced - Stale-snapshot-only: the most recent snapshot is years old; the self-application claim is unverifiable - Citation-ambiguity-unowned: the project has not decided what readers should cite; different citations proliferate Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. (1) Living-only: current HTML (or notebook) with visible revision history; no frozen snapshots. Gives up archival citability. (2) Snapshot-only: versioned PDFs or archived HTML with DOIs at each publication event; intermediate states not published. Gives up currency. (3) Both: living current version + periodic frozen snapshots, each snapshot declaring its evidence-file revision and compute-date. Gives up simplicity; serves both readerships. Working papers typically need (3); the paper-draft-16-april is an instance of an intermediate snapshot (marked by date in filename). Engaged when: readers can find both the current state and the most recent citable snapshot; each snapshot declares its evidence-file revision and compute-date; the composition is declared. Failing when: "the paper" is ambiguous — readers citing different URLs think they are citing the same document; snapshots exist but do not declare their evidence-revision; the living document drifts without visible history. Citation integrity: an academic artefact that readers cite must be citable as a specific object. Snapshots give citation integrity; living documents do not. A paper that is both a living document AND cited in grant applications requires snapshots for the citation paths. Currency integrity: a paper that argues for design-as-function-of-evidence and is five years out of date undercuts its own argument. The living document is what demonstrates the self-application claim. Reader-need differentiation: different readers want different things. A funder reviewing a proposal wants the current state; a peer reviewer citing the work in a rebuttal wants a fixed target. Composition (3) serves both. Cross-pattern: publication-cadence is downstream of ukrns/design-state-lineage (snapshots are checkpoints in the lineage) and a sibling of ukrns/cycle-position-publication (both publish design states at chosen intervals). Mechanic, in short: Mechanic: how the artefact is published (living, snapshot, both). Serves: self-application's artefact-instantiation claim. Axis: living document ↔ frozen snapshots. Without this pattern: "which paper" is ambiguous; self-application cannot be demonstrated. - Declare the current composition (likely (3) living + periodic snapshots) - Each snapshot carries: compute-date, assumptions-v2.edn revision, DOI or equivalent identifier - Living version carries a visible "current compute-date" and "current assumptions revision" - A clear statement: "to cite this paper in academic work, cite [snapshot DOI]; to read the current state, see [living URL]" - Cross-reference with ukrns/design-state-lineage and ukrns/cycle-position-publication

title: Reader as Diagnostic Participant (Meta-Pattern)
text: Reader as Diagnostic Participant (Meta-Pattern) A paper that states a tension, names two or three compositions, and refuses to rank them is addressing the reader as a participant in the decision, not a consumer of a conclusion. The working paper's reader exercises are not decoration; they are the points at which the reader is explicitly invited to pick a position on an axis and justify it. The paper teaches its reader how to read design patterns. The service states which composition it is running on the axis between reader-as-consumer and reader-as-diagnostic-participant. For each axis in the working paper, the reader is explicitly invited to pick a position and justify it. The exercises are load-bearing: the paper's structure teaches pattern-reading through them. For UKRN-S operational documents, the composition on the reader-as-participant axis is a deliberate choice per document and per audience, not a default. This meta-pattern is about the address of the working paper — whom it is written for and in what posture — and, by projection, about how UKRN-S could address its own network of institutions, trainers, and funders. The five main patterns follow a Tension / Composition / Check structure that deliberately makes axes visible without prescribing a single answer. The reader exercises (Reader — diagnose your current programme; Reader — which of these five would you commission first; Reader — what does this table let you say, and what does it explicitly not support?; Reader — if you had resources for Step 1 only, would you still progress?) are the places where the reader is invited into the diagnostic itself. Take the exercises out and the axes revert to statements; the reader becomes a consumer again. The pattern operates on the axis: reader-as-consumer (receives conclusions; reads for information) ↔ reader-as-diagnostic-participant (is invited to pick a position; reads for decision). Irreducible: the same section cannot simultaneously deliver a closed conclusion and invite an open choice. A reader confronted with 'you must decide which composition you would run' has a different reading experience than one shown 'the authors recommend composition X'. Real costs: a consumer-oriented paper is faster to read, easier to cite, and respects the reader's time; a participant-oriented paper demands more of the reader and produces more friction. Both orientations carry genuine costs. Active dynamic: the right orientation depends on the reader and the moment. Early in a paper's lifecycle, when the argument is forming and the decision is genuinely open, participation is productive. As claims harden and decisions are made, participation becomes performative (the reader is invited to agree with a choice already taken). Audiences also differ: funders may want conclusions; institutional leads may need to participate; trainers may need to see themselves in the diagnosis. - Conclusory exercises: the 'Reader — pick a position' is answered by the paper two sentences later - Decorative exercises: exercises present but unrelated to the pattern's axis; ornamental rather than pedagogical - Hidden recommendation: three compositions stated, one discreetly preferred by diction; the reader reads through the preference despite the non-ranking - Uniform consumer address: the paper addresses every reader as a consumer regardless of what is being decided; no participation invited - Uniform participant address: the paper demands participation from every reader including those who need closure (e.g. funders under decision pressure); produces frustration rather than engagement - Context-less invitation: 'Reader — pick a composition' without the context the reader would need to answer; invitation is formal rather than real Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. (1) Exercises at section boundaries: each section ends with a Reader exercise that asks the reader to pick a position on the section's axis; the answer is yours, the paper provides the framework. This is the working paper's current approach. Gives up reading speed; demands more of each reader. (2) Exercises consolidated at end: one 'working with this paper' section at the end collects all the diagnostic invitations; the body of the paper reads as a consumer paper; the exercises are a separate, opt-in layer. Gives up the axis-by-axis participation; keeps the consumer reading path clean. (3) No exercises, maximum consumer-paced: the paper states the tensions and compositions but does not explicitly invite the reader to pick; the reader may infer the invitation or not. Gives up the pedagogical move of teaching pattern-reading; keeps the paper's surface the shortest. These compositions are not ranked; the paper is at Composition (1) by deliberate choice and the exercises are load-bearing for the pedagogical claim (see BECAUSE). Engaged when: the paper (or service document) explicitly names axes, unranked compositions, and invites the reader to pick; exercises are load-bearing rather than decorative; the reader who skips the exercises has a legible but diminished reading. Failing when: the paper names tensions but quietly recommends one composition; exercises present but conclusory (their 'answers' are given by the paper); the reader is addressed uniformly as a consumer regardless of the decision being described; the participatory surface is ornamental rather than pedagogical. Pattern-reading is learned: The Tension / Composition / Check structure is not self-explanatory on first encounter. A reader meeting it for the first time has to be shown, not told, that the compositions are genuinely unranked and that picking among them is the reader's work. The exercises are the teaching moments. Take them out and the Tension / Composition / Check structure reads as a presentation of options from which the authors have discreetly chosen one; put them in and the structure reads as a framework for shared decision. Unranked compositions require invitation: A paper that names three compositions and stops leaves the reader to guess the authors' preference. A paper that names three and invites the reader to pick one makes the non-ranking explicit. Without the invitation, the reader's default is to hunt for the authorial preference; with it, the reader's default is to consider their own position. The invitation changes the reading posture. Refuses authoritative closure: The exercises are not merely participatory in form; they are epistemically humble in content. 'The answer is yours; the point is that the answer lets UKRN-S justify the next T1 budget on uncertainty-reduction grounds, not on general interest' explicitly refuses to tell the reader what to do. This is the same epistemic stance as ukrns/computation-as-exploration (prior, not posterior) applied to the paper's rhetoric. Diagnostic reading teaches diagnostic acting: A funder or institutional lead who has read the paper participatorily has already done some of the work ukrns/diagnose-before-prescribing asks UKRN-S to do. The reading rehearsal transfers: having named a binding constraint on paper, they are readier to recognise one in practice. This is the meta-pattern's projection into the main patterns. Projection into main patterns: UKRN-S's own address to its network could maintain the same posture. Commissioned service documents, profile diagnoses, measurement-wave justifications could all invite the institution to pick a position rather than delivering a service recommendation. The meta-pattern is thus not only about reading the paper; it is about addressing the network. Audience-shifting caveat: The right address depends on audience. A funder's ingestion path may need more closure than a trainer's. A paper (or service) that invites participation uniformly will be read as indecisive by some and respectful by others. The service composes — per document, per audience — the right participation level. Mechanic, in short: Derived from the working paper's explicit reader-exercise scaffold and the Tension / Composition / Check structure those exercises animate. Meta-pattern character: describes the paper's address to its reader and, by projection, UKRN-S's address to its network. Projection into main patterns: participatory reading rehearses participatory decision-making; ukrns/diagnose-before-prescribing, ukrns/measure-where-least-sure, and ukrns/open-the-triangle all describe decisions that would benefit from institutional participation in the same posture the paper rehearses with its readers. Axis framing follows the same Tension / Composition / Check structure as the main patterns. The self-referential character — a pattern about addressing the reader that uses the same pattern form to address its own reader — is deliberate. Coordination requirement: Low at paper time (single author team can choose the posture); Medium to High at service time (consistent participatory address across the network's communications requires coordination). - For each axis in the working paper, maintain a reader exercise that invites the reader to pick a position on that axis - Make the exercises genuinely open: the paper provides the framework for answering, not the answer - Distinguish axes where the authors do take a baseline position (e.g. ukrns/measure-where-least-sure favours VoI-first) from axes where they do not — the reader should know which is which - For UKRN-S operational documents: consider the same posture for service communications; where appropriate, invite the recipient to pick a position rather than delivering a recommendation - Audience-check each exercise: does this audience have the context to answer? if not, provide the context before the invitation - Track which exercises land: which are read, which are skipped, which produce discussion

title: Reader Run Path — Minimum Reproducibility Infrastructure (Implementation Pattern)
text: Reader Run Path — Minimum Reproducibility Infrastructure (Implementation Pattern) A paper that claims self-application is only as strong as the infrastructure an actual reader needs to rerun it. The service states which composition it is running on the axis between full reproducibility (a reader runs the notebook and reproduces the current outputs) and accessible readout (the paper declares enough in an annex for a reader to reimplement the computation in any language). Both endpoints serve different readers; neither alone is sufficient for long-horizon reproducibility. The current reader-run composition is declared. At least one path works for its declared audience. A fallback for tooling decay is maintained. This implementation pattern specifies the reader-facing reproducibility mechanic behind ukrns/self-application. The meta-pattern claims the artefact is re-computable; this pattern addresses the practical question of what infrastructure a reader needs. Without a declared reader-run path, the self-application claim is aspirational for most readers and will decay as the compute environment ages. The pattern operates on the axis: full reproducibility (reader runs the notebook in a declared environment) ↔ accessible readout (the paper's annex contains enough equations, data, and protocols for first-principles reconstruction in any language). Irreducible: a single infrastructure cannot simultaneously be maximally one-click-runnable in today's tooling AND maximally independent of any specific tooling for long-term preservation. Real costs: reproducibility costs tooling maintenance — a declared environment will decay as dependencies age; readout costs rerun fidelity — a reader reconstructing from first principles may reproduce the approach but not bit-for-bit match. Active dynamic: technical readers in the near term appreciate reproducibility; non-technical readers need readout; archival readers in the far future need readout (tooling will have changed). - Unspecified environment: reader attempts to rerun, discovers dependencies are not declared, gives up - Environment-decay: the Docker image stops building; the rerun path is broken and nobody notices - Annex-incomplete: readout is claimed but the annex is missing details needed for first-principles reconstruction - Fallback-missing: primary path depends on specific tooling; when tooling decays, self-application is lost - No reader-feedback channel: failures are unreported; the maintainer never learns the rerun is broken Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. (1) Notebook + environment: fully-reproducible containerised environment (Docker, Nix, or similar) that locks dependencies; reader runs the notebook and reproduces current outputs. Gives up low-barrier access. (2) Static + reimplementation annex: the paper publishes equations, levers, uncertainty model, sampling protocol, and declarative assumptions file in enough detail that a reader can reconstruct the computation in any language. Gives up one-click rerun. (3) Both: containerised environment for near-term rerun + reimplementation annex for long-term preservation and first-principles access. Gives up simplicity; double maintenance. The paper-draft-16-april has Annex B, which satisfies Composition (2); the notebook (Clojure/Clay) satisfies Composition (1) partially. Operational use would benefit from declaring the composition as (3) with both paths declared. Engaged when: the composition is declared; at least one of the rerun paths works for the declared audience; the fallback composition (typically readout) is maintained even if the primary is available. Failing when: the paper claims self-application but no reader can actually rerun; the notebook runs but only in an undeclared environment; the annex is missing details needed for reconstruction; there is no fallback for when the primary path decays. Near-term vs long-term reproducibility: ukrns/self-application wants re-computability. Near-term: readers today want to rerun. Long-term: readers in 20 years want to reconstruct when the current tooling is obsolete. These are different audiences served by different compositions. Reader posture differentiation: technical readers can use a containerised environment; non-technical readers cannot but may want to understand what the computation does. Composition (2) is accessible to any reader who reads mathematics; Composition (1) is accessible only to readers with the tooling. Graceful degradation: the compute environment will eventually decay. When Docker images stop building, what happens? Composition (2) is the standing fallback: the reimplementation annex remains readable even when the environment is obsolete. Projects with only Composition (1) lose their self-application property when tooling decays. Declared access level: readers should know before attempting what level of reproducibility the paper supports. A paper that claims self-application but whose rerun fails on first attempt undermines trust. Declaration manages expectation. Mechanic, in short: Mechanic: what infrastructure a reader needs to rerun or reconstruct the computation. Serves: self-application's re-computability claim. Axis: full reproducibility ↔ accessible readout. Without this pattern: self-application is aspirational and decays with the compute environment. - Declare the current composition in the paper or project documentation - If (1): specify the environment (Docker image, Nix flake, or equivalent); test the rerun from scratch periodically - If (2): ensure Annex B is complete enough for reimplementation (equations, factor lists, lever definitions, uncertainty model, sampling protocol) - If (3): maintain both paths; declare which is primary and which is fallback - Invite reader feedback: someone who tries to rerun and fails should have a channel - Cross-reference with ukrns/publication-cadence (snapshots need rerun-path documentation at snapshot time)

title: Scale Register — Publishing Capability Scale Choices (Implementation Pattern)
text: Scale Register — Publishing Capability Scale Choices (Implementation Pattern) Every capability the network could provide — evaluation analysis, coordination/liaison, scaffold maintenance, any future addition — has a scale choice (per-institution vs network-scale) that must be inspectable. The service maintains a register of these choices with rationale, date, and revision history, and states which composition it is running on the axis between central register and distributed per-capability documentation. The register lists every capability the network could provide. Each entry has scale, rationale, date, revision history. Contestation channel is declared. This implementation pattern specifies the publication mechanic behind ukrns/provision-at-network-scale. The main pattern's invariant requires scale choices to be published and revisable; without a register, those choices exist in project-memory rather than as public artefacts institutions can contest. The pattern operates on the axis: central register (one maintained document listing every capability and its scale decision) ↔ distributed per-capability documentation (each capability described in its own document, with scale decision inline). Irreducible: a single documentation strategy cannot simultaneously maximise centralised coherence and distributed depth. Real costs: central costs coherence maintenance — keeping the register aligned with reality — and creates a single point of obsolescence; distributed costs findability — readers may not know every capability exists or may not find its scale decision easily. Active dynamic: small capability sets favour central; large sets favour distributed; mixed strategies become attractive as the set grows past roughly 10 capabilities. - Incomplete register: capabilities exist operationally but are not registered - Rationale absence: scale stated without reasoning; choice appears arbitrary - Stale revision: rationale dated years ago; reality has moved - No contestation channel: institutions have no declared way to flag mis-scaling - Register-as-table-only: the capability trade-off table in the paper is treated as the register; the table is a snapshot, a register is a living artefact Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. (1) Central register: a single artefact (markdown, EDN, or similar) listing every capability with scale, rationale, date, revision history. Gives up per-capability depth. (2) Capability-by-capability docs: each capability has its own document including scale decision and rationale. Gives up single-point findability. (3) Both — central index + per-capability deep docs: index lists names and current scale; each entry links to the capability's own doc. Gives up simplicity; doubles maintenance. The paper currently operates at a proto-(1) level via the capability trade-off table in §2; operational use requires a living register. Engaged when: every current capability is findable in the register (or via the index); each entry has scale, rationale, date, revision history; institutions can contest choices via a declared channel. Failing when: some capabilities exist but are not in the register; entries have scale without rationale; rationale exists but is dated years ago without revision; contestation has no channel. Contestability: ukrns/provision-at-network-scale's invariant requires institutions to be able to contest scale choices. Contestation is only possible if the choice is findable and its rationale inspectable. The register is the publication mechanic that makes contestation possible. Asymmetric trade-offs: the main pattern is built on the observation that capabilities have different trade-off shapes. The register is where those shapes are compared side by side; losing the register collapses the asymmetry argument. Revision history: as the network grows, scale choices may shift — a capability viable at one scale today may shift tomorrow. The register's revision history is the mechanism that makes scale evolution legible rather than silent. Cross-pattern: the register is a particular kind of deposit (ukrns/open-the-triangle); it is itself a service-event with openness gain (institutions can see the current provisioning map) and governance cost (someone must maintain it). Mechanic, in short: Mechanic: how capability scale choices are published and revised. Serves: provision-at-network-scale's invariant. Axis: central register ↔ distributed per-capability docs. Without this pattern: scale choices exist in project memory, not as contestable public artefacts. - Declare the current composition (most likely (1) central register at start) in project documentation - Create the register as an artefact (not merely a table inside the working paper); make it findable from the project root - Every entry: name, current scale, rationale, date, revision history, contestation channel - Cross-reference from the working paper's §3 capability trade-off table to the register - At network scale: allow institutions to flag capabilities they think are mis-scaled

title: Self-Application — The Artefact Instantiates Its Claim (Meta-Pattern)
text: Self-Application — The Artefact Instantiates Its Claim (Meta-Pattern) A paper that argues for 'design as a function of evidence' and is itself a static, frozen PDF undermines its own claim by example. The working paper is a notebook that loads the evidence file, recomputes the model, and emits the argument — so a reader with updated evidence can see the design shift. Form instantiates claim. The service states which composition it is running on the axis between static-artefact and instantiating-artefact. The working paper is re-computable from a declarative evidence file and a documented computational environment. Every published version states its evidence-file revision. The artefact's lineage is preserved so a reader can see the history of argument shifts against evidence shifts. This meta-pattern is about the construction of the working paper and, by projection, about how UKRN-S could publish its own design state. If the main patterns describe a learning system that updates design as evidence accrues (ukrns/design-as-function-of-evidence), then an artefact that describes such a system without being one makes a weaker argument than an artefact that is one. The meta-pattern is media-theoretic: medium as message. The paper can be re-run because the medium supports it. The pattern operates on the axis: static artefact (frozen document, snapshot of claims) ↔ instantiating artefact (re-computable, argument emitted from evidence on each run). Irreducible: a single artefact cannot be maximally static (frozen, universally readable, dependency-free) AND maximally instantiating (re-computable from live data, reflecting evidence-state-of-today). These are different kinds of object. Real costs: static artefacts are cheaper to produce, easier to archive, familiar to readers, and survive infrastructural decay; instantiating artefacts require computational infrastructure, active maintenance, and readers (or institutions) with the technical capacity to rerun. Both carry real cost. Active dynamic: at publication time, the instantiating form has high production and reader cost; as notebook tooling matures, cost drops and instantiation becomes viable for more artefacts. A decade from now, the current paper's tooling will likely be obsolete; the static record is the durable one. The right balance shifts over the lifetime of the medium. - Claim-without-instance: argues for evidence-driven design but is itself a frozen document with no re-runnable lineage - Embedded evidence: assumptions hard-coded in the document body; changes require manual editing rather than updating a data file - Inert computation: the notebook runs but its outputs do not depend on the evidence file; reruns produce identical results - Untracked lineage: published versions do not declare which evidence-file revision they were computed from; the reader cannot tell what has changed - Tooling lock-in: the artefact depends on specific infrastructure that will evaporate; no fallback composition is maintained - Performative self-application: the artefact is packaged as runnable but no reader actually reruns; form without function Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. (1) Notebook-as-paper: the artefact is a live notebook; a reader with the evidence file and the computational environment reruns to see the current design state. Gives up durability and frictionless reading; requires active tool maintenance. (2) Static paper + declarative EDN: the paper is published as a static document but accompanied by the assumptions file (assumptions-v2.edn) and a reimplementation pointer (Annex B); a motivated reader can reconstruct the computation from first principles. Gives up the live-rerun experience; keeps the archival property of static papers. (3) Companion repository: a static paper + a separate runnable notebook in a versioned repository, with an explicit mapping from paper sections to notebook cells. Gives up unified presentation; keeps both audiences served (archival readers + technical rerunners). These compositions are not ranked; the paper's current form is closest to Composition (1) with Composition (2) as fallback. The choice may shift as tooling and archival norms evolve. Engaged when: the artefact can be re-run with an updated evidence file and the argument shifts accordingly; the re-run process is documented and reproducible; the relationship between the published version and the live state is itself inspectable (e.g. version history, git log). Failing when: the artefact claims to be a function of evidence but cannot actually be re-run; the evidence file is embedded in the document body rather than separable; re-runs produce the same output regardless of input changes (computation inert); the artefact is published as a static snapshot without a re-runnable lineage. REPL discipline (linked: t4r/ pattern library): Read-Evaluate-Print-Loop is the computational form the paper borrows. Each run of the notebook is: read the assumptions; evaluate the model; print the argument; loop back when evidence changes. This is not decorative: the loop is what makes the design-as-function-of-evidence claim concrete rather than aspirational. Ontogenetic accretion (linked: ukrns/open-the-triangle): The working paper is itself a deposit. Each version captures the design state at a point in time; the notebook lineage traces how the design evolved as evidence accrued. The artefact IS a growth ring in the programme's architecture. Medium as message: The paper does what it says. A reader who sees the notebook rerunning after an evidence update sees the argument's claim instantiated rather than described. This is stronger evidence than prose: the claim is demonstrated rather than asserted. Projection into main patterns: UKRN-S's design state could be published in the same form. Institutions could see the current population model, the current diagnosis for their profile, the current service-design cycle, as output of a live computation from the current evidence file. The update-policy choice (ukrns/design-as-function-of-evidence) becomes visible in the versioning of the artefact: every re-run is a potential update; every skipped re-run is a qualifying absence. Pre-empts self-undercutting: A paper arguing for 'services should update as evidence arrives' that is itself a frozen snapshot creates the strongest available objection to its own thesis. Self-application is the method for dissolving that objection. The inverse objection (why should anyone trust a moving target?) is real but not symmetric: the trust objection applies to services and artefacts alike and is answered by the update-policy discipline (ukrns/design-as-function-of-evidence). Mechanic, in short: Derived from the working paper's self-application stance: the notebook form is not a packaging choice but a methodological one. Meta-pattern character: describes how the paper is made and, by projection, how UKRN-S could publish its design state. Projection into main patterns: ukrns/design-as-function-of-evidence specifies that the service updates on evidence; this meta-pattern specifies that the service's artefacts can themselves be instances of that update. ukrns/open-the-triangle specifies that deposits persist; this meta-pattern specifies the form those deposits take. Axis framing follows the same Tension / Composition / Check structure as the main patterns. Coordination requirement: Medium (single-author team can adopt at paper time; institutional operationalisation requires shared tooling and maintenance). - Maintain the working paper as a rerunnable notebook; any published version (PDF, HTML, archive) declares which evidence-file revision it was computed from - When publishing a new version, surface what changed: which evidence updates triggered which argument shifts - Package the notebook and the assumptions file together so a reader can reproduce the computation - For operational use at UKRN-S: consider publishing the design state as a live notebook that updates when measurement waves complete - Maintain a mapping from paper sections to notebook cells (Annex B already partially does this) - Record a deprecation plan: when the current tooling becomes obsolete, how will the artefact's claim survive? (Composition 2 is the standing fallback.)

title: Separate Direct, Indirect, and Out-of-Scope Levers (Sketch)
text: Separate Direct, Indirect, and Out-of-Scope Levers (Sketch) Not every institutional condition is equally movable by a network service. A design that types its own levers is more honest, more governable, and easier to evaluate than one that implies uniform control. The current paper's design section already distinguishes between conditions UKRN Services can move by contract or routine, conditions it can influence only through evidence and pressure, and conditions that remain prior constraints. The pattern operates on the axis: undifferentiated influence claim ↔ typed leverage claim. Real costs: typing leverage narrows the design's apparent power and exposes where it depends on action by others. Name the direct levers, the indirect levers, and the out-of-scope conditions explicitly, and keep the out-of-scope ones visible in later verification.

title: Separate Evidence Gaps from Implementation Decisions (Sketch)
text: Separate Evidence Gaps from Implementation Decisions (Sketch) Some uncertainties belong to the evidence base and must be resolved or explicitly carried forward; others are implementation choices that properly belong to UKRN Services once the design is accepted. A paper that mixes the two makes its own gaps look larger than they are and makes implementation ownership harder to see. The current working paper now distinguishes open questions about impact and learning from hand-off questions about resourcing, evaluator configuration, partnerships, and topic priority. That separation is doing real governance work for the reader. The pattern operates on the axis: unresolved evidence need ↔ owned implementation choice. Real costs: separating the two exposes where the paper cannot yet close a claim, and it also exposes where the implementing team cannot defer a judgment by asking for more analysis. Name the evidence gaps explicitly; name the implementation decisions explicitly; and refuse to let one masquerade as the other.

title: Treat Funder Cycles as Operational Rhythm (Sketch)
text: Treat Funder Cycles as Operational Rhythm (Sketch) Periods of active ringfenced funding and periods without it produce different patterns of institutional movement. A design that ignores that rhythm will misread the environment as random variation. The current paper's sector-priorities track and its closing finding both identify ringfenced funding as a decisive enabling condition for collaborative research-culture work. The pattern operates on the axis: funding cycle as background ↔ funding cycle as explicit operating condition. Real costs: acknowledging the funding rhythm narrows what can honestly be promised in quieter periods and makes the design more contingent on external timing than a cleaner abstract model would prefer. Build plans, expectations, and interpretation around the funding rhythm explicitly rather than treating it as noise outside the design.

title: Worked Contrast — Paired Concrete Cases That Show the Model Biting Differently (Meta-Pattern)
text: Worked Contrast — Paired Concrete Cases That Show the Model Biting Differently (Meta-Pattern) An abstract model states conditional dependencies; a single case instantiates them. Two contrasting cases that occupy different positions in the model's space — and that therefore fall into different modes — show the model biting differently. The working paper's FG2A-P1 (delivery-gated) and FG3-A (multiply-constrained) are the paired worked contrast; neither case alone would have produced the same legibility. The service states which composition it is running on the axis between abstraction-at-population-scale and concreteness-at-case-scale. For each major modelling claim in the working paper (and in UKRN-S operational diagnosis), at least one pair of worked cases is traced through the model; the pair is chosen to show the claim biting differently; the selection rationale is explicit; worked cases are updated as evidence updates. This meta-pattern is about the rhetoric of the working paper and, by projection, about how UKRN-S could maintain diagnostic anchors in its operational work. The population model is abstract (D × A, gate/support, mode tree). The Table 1 ten-profile sweep is intermediate. The worked examples are concrete. FG2A-P1 is traced through the model to show delivery-gating; FG3-A is traced through to show multi-constraint. The pairing is not redundant — each case reveals what the other does not — and the contrast is load-bearing for the diagnose-before-prescribing pattern (ukrns/diagnose-before-prescribing). The pattern operates on the axis: abstraction (population-level, model-level statements) ↔ concreteness (case-level, profile-level instantiations). Irreducible: a single statement cannot be simultaneously maximally abstract (covering all cases) and maximally concrete (tracing one case through in full detail). They answer different reading needs. Real costs: abstraction without concrete leaves the reader unable to see what the model claims means operationally; concreteness without abstraction is anecdote and does not generalise. Both carry real costs when taken alone. Active dynamic: a reader unfamiliar with the model needs more concrete; a reader deep in the data needs less. As the paper's audience shifts over time — from authors and peer reviewers to funders, institutional leads, trainers — the right abstraction/concreteness balance shifts. Early cycles may favour concreteness; later cycles, with trained readers and accumulated evidence, may favour abstraction. - Single-case-as-representative: one profile treated as 'the case' without contrast; the reader cannot see what the model discriminates - Catalogue drift: every profile traced without selection; loses the discriminative power of contrast - Politically-chosen cases: worked cases picked because they carry institutional weight rather than because they expose model behaviour - Rhetorical-only concreteness: worked cases present for legibility but not linked explicitly to abstract claims; reader can read either layer but not bridge them - Stale worked cases: cases not updated as evidence base shifts; current claim and worked example contradict - Abstraction-only: claims stated without concrete instantiation; reader without the model in hand cannot follow Operate an explicit move on the named axis (see substructure below); steward the pattern against the declared discipline. (1) Paired contrast: two worked cases positioned to show the model biting differently (FG2A-P1 delivery-gated + FG3-A multiply-constrained). Gives up the depth of a single-case deep dive; gains legibility of the model's differential behaviour. (2) Single deep case: one profile traced through in exhaustive detail — every NPT factor, every lever effect, every mode-probability update. Gives up the contrast that shows the model's differential behaviour; gains density of evidence for one institution. (3) Population overview + one representative: the ten-profile table + one 'typical' case. Gives up the contrast and the depth; gains communicative simplicity. These compositions are not ranked; the paper is at Composition (1) deliberately, and the pairing is what makes the multiplicativity claim (ukrns/diagnose-before-prescribing BECAUSE) concrete. Engaged when: at least two worked cases are traced through the model, and the pair is chosen to show the model biting differently (different binding constraints, different modes, different lever-response profiles). The selection rationale is explicit. Failing when: a single case is offered as representative without a contrast; all cases are traced without selection (catalogue drift); the paired cases are chosen for political salience rather than to show the model's differential behaviour; the relationship between abstract claims and concrete cases is not made explicit. Contrast reveals the axis: A single worked case illustrates the model's machinery; two contrasting cases illustrate what the model discriminates between. FG2A-P1 has strong architecture (A = 0.63) but weak delivery (D = 0.46) — the D × A gate is delivery-gated, and a scaffold intervention (Step 0) would move it toward multiplied. FG3-A has weak both dimensions (D = 0.33, A = 0.21); no single-dimension lever suffices. The two cases together show WHY diagnosis matters: the same lever bundle would produce different effects on each. This is the multiplicativity claim made concrete. Mode-space legibility: The three modes (Multiplied, Absorbed, Mismatch) are abstract until a case falls into each. The paired contrast maps concrete profiles to mode-space positions: FG2A-P1 falls closest to mismatch at baseline (low D, architecture stronger than delivery); FG3-A falls deeper in mismatch (both dimensions below threshold). A reader who has traced both can read the Table 1 profile sweep without further translation. Abstraction ladder: The paper's rhetoric uses a three-rung ladder — abstract model (Annex B equations) → intermediate population sweep (Table 1/2) → concrete paired cases. Each rung supports the next. Removing the concrete rung collapses the ladder; a reader jumping from Annex B to Table 2 has no handhold. Projection into main patterns: UKRN-S's operational diagnostic work could maintain paired anchor cases that represent the span of the profile space. When a new institution joins the network, matching it against the anchors is the first step; the anchors are the operational instance of ukrns/diagnose-before-prescribing's binding-constraint-signature claim. The meta-pattern thus projects into service practice, not only paper rhetoric. Not every case is worth tracing: The paired contrast's discipline is selective — two cases chosen because they expose different model behaviours. A paper that traces every case collapses to a catalogue (Composition variant: population overview, but without overview-level claims). The selection itself is part of the pattern: which two cases, and why this pair. Mechanic, in short: Derived from the working paper's use of the FG2A-P1 / FG3-A paired worked example to make the multiplicative-gate claim concrete. Meta-pattern character: describes a rhetorical discipline in the paper and, by projection, an operational discipline for UKRN-S's diagnostic work. Projection into main patterns: ukrns/diagnose-before-prescribing's binding-constraint signature is abstract; anchor cases make it operational. As a meta-pattern, worked contrast is how the paper teaches the reader to diagnose. Axis framing follows the same Tension / Composition / Check structure as the main patterns. Coordination requirement: Low at paper time; Medium at service time (anchor cases require maintenance as the profile map evolves). - For each major modelling claim, maintain at least one worked pair that shows the claim biting differently in different profile positions - Choose worked cases to span the model's discriminative dimensions (e.g. delivery-gated vs. multiply-constrained), not to represent 'typical' cases - State the selection rationale: why these two, not two others - For operational use at UKRN-S: maintain a small set of anchor profiles that new institutions can be matched against during diagnosis (ukrns/diagnose-before-prescribing) - Update worked cases as the evidence base updates; stale worked cases are worse than no worked cases (they suggest a diagnosis that no longer holds) - Preserve the abstraction ladder: abstract → intermediate → concrete; do not skip the concrete rung

title: Annotation as Commitment
text: Annotation as Commitment Interpretive notes should be able to graduate from observations into commitments — named actions with owners, timelines, and completion criteria — so that collective sense-making produces accountable follow-through. You are designing the bridge between interpretation and action within a facilitated programme. This does not apply when annotations are purely scholarly or archival. A pilot's interpretive notes surface actionable patterns — "these three stories describe the same unmet need" or "this contrast link reveals a policy gap." Notes that remain observations create a culture of noticing without acting. The gap between insight and response is where community trust erodes. Allow any interpretive note to be promoted to a commitment: an action item with an owner, a deadline, a success criterion, and a link back to the note and its source stories. Commitments appear in a steward-visible tracker alongside the constellation. When annotation becomes commitment, the interpretive layer stops being a commentary system and becomes a planning tool. The constellation is no longer only a picture of the past — it is a surface for coordinating the future. next[Extend the interpretive note schema with optional commitment fields (owner, deadline, criterion, status).] next[Design the steward dashboard view that shows open commitments alongside the constellation.] next[Test with one pilot: do promoted commitments actually get completed at a higher rate than unpromoted notes?]

title: Cluster as Agenda Item
text: Cluster as Agenda Item Allow participants to flag spatial clusters or arc concentrations as agenda items so that patterns visible in the constellation become inputs to structured deliberation. You are bridging spatial perception and collective decision-making. This does not apply when the constellation is used purely for exhibition or archival purposes. Participants notice a recurring pattern — several stories linked by causal arcs, a dense cluster around a shared harm, an isolated story that should be connected. Noticing is not the same as acting. Without a mechanism to capture the observation and route it to a deliberation process, spatial insight dissipates when the viewer looks away. Provide a "flag this pattern" gesture (click, long-press, voice, annotation) that captures the cluster, its constituent stories and links, and a free-text framing question. The flag becomes an agenda item in a facilitation queue visible to stewards. Agendas grounded in visible spatial patterns carry their evidence with them. The facilitator does not need to re-explain the observation — they can point at it. next[Define the minimal data a flag must carry (cluster IDs, framing question, flagger identity).] next[Prototype a flag gesture in one projection (VR controller, web click, or terminal command).] next[Design how flags surface in the stewardship layer — queue, dashboard, or meeting agenda.]

title: Decision Provenance
text: Decision Provenance Every decision that emerges from deliberation should trace back to the stories, links, and flagged patterns that motivated it, creating an auditable chain from lived experience to collective action. You are designing accountability into a system where community stories inform real decisions. This does not apply to purely exploratory or artistic uses of the constellation. A facilitated session produces a decision — fund a programme, change a policy, allocate resources, create a new pilot. If the decision is recorded without its evidential context, it becomes an assertion rather than a conclusion. Participants who were not present cannot verify the reasoning. Future stewards cannot learn from the process. Link each decision record to the agenda flag that prompted it, the stories and arcs that constituted the evidence, the session notes, and the participants involved. Store this chain as a first-class object alongside stories and links. Provenance is how deliberation becomes trustworthy. Communities that can trace "we decided X because stories A, B, C showed pattern P" are better equipped to revisit, revise, and defend their choices. next[Define the decision record schema (decision text, linked flags, session ID, participants, date).] next[Sketch how decision records appear in the constellation — a new node type? an annotation on existing arcs?] next[Identify one real deliberation case to model retroactively as a provenance chain.]

title: Federated Cosmoses
text: Federated Cosmoses Multiple independent constellations should be able to federate — each visible as a node in a meta-level view — so that separate organisations, programmes, or communities can maintain sovereignty while discovering cross-boundary patterns. You are designing for a network of organisations that each run their own story worlds but want selective interoperability. This does not apply to single-organisation deployments with no external connections. Several organisations each maintain their own VSAT/VSATLAS installations — a university, a community group, an NGO, a farming cooperative. Isolated installations cannot reveal patterns that span organisational boundaries. A migrant story in one installation and a policy story in another may describe the same systemic failure, but neither community sees the connection. Define a federation protocol: each installation publishes a summary (story count, cluster structure, link types, anthology list) without exposing raw content. A meta-constellation renders each installation as a single node — click to enter that cosmos. Opt-in cross-boundary links allow specific stories to bridge cosmoses when both parties consent. Federation preserves sovereignty (each community owns its data and governance) while enabling the emergent patterns that only appear at scale. This is the digital-library equivalent of inter-library loan: you do not merge the libraries; you create a protocol for sharing what each is willing to share. next[Define the minimal federation summary schema (what an installation publishes about itself).] next[Prototype the meta-constellation view with two synthetic installations.] next[Design the consent workflow for cross-boundary linking (both stewards must approve).] next[Evaluate whether existing protocols (ActivityPub, Solid, IIIF) could carry the federation data.]

title: Projection Independence
text: Projection Independence Deliberation patterns should be defined independently of any specific rendering technology so the same structures work across VR domes, AR overlays, 2D graphs, hypertext pages, and terminal interfaces. You are designing for longevity across hardware generations and interaction paradigms. This does not apply when the system is permanently bound to a single platform. The patterns of connection, clustering, anthology, and deliberation outlive the specific technology used to render them. Coupling patterns to a particular renderer (A-Frame, Three.js, a specific headset SDK) means they die when the technology does. The Quest 2 is already dated; the Steam Frame is not yet shipping; AR glasses are nascent; Nelsonian hypertext requires no 3D at all. Define the deliberation layer (flags, decisions, commitments, return loops) as data structures and interaction contracts, not as rendering code. Each projection surface implements the contract: — VR dome: flag by pointing, decision appears as a glowing node — AR glasses: flag by gaze, decision pins to a physical wall — 2D web: flag by click, decision appears in a sidebar — Terminal: flag by command, decision appears in a ledger The pattern library describes the contract; implementations vary. Projection independence is how a pattern library outlives its first implementation. The VSATLATARIUM flexiargs describe one projection; the VSATELIER flexiargs describe what must be true across all of them. next[Extract the interaction contracts from the VSATLATARIUM patterns into projection-neutral specs.] next[Prototype one deliberation pattern (cluster-as-agenda) in two different projections to verify independence.] next[Evaluate futon4 (Nelsonian hypertext) as a second projection surface for the same pattern set.]

title: Return Loop (Outcomes as New Stories)
text: Return Loop (Outcomes as New Stories) Outcomes of actions taken from the constellation should re-enter it as new stories, closing the loop between seeing, deciding, acting, and witnessing. You are designing a living system where action feeds back into shared knowledge. This does not apply to one-off analyses where no follow-up is expected. A community acts on a pattern surfaced by the constellation — they run a programme, change a practice, allocate a resource. If the outcome of that action is never recorded as a story, the constellation becomes a static snapshot of the past. The community cannot see whether their actions changed anything. Encourage (or structure) the creation of outcome stories: what happened after the decision, what changed, what surprised. These stories enter the constellation as new nodes. Links from the decision record to the outcome story close the loop visually — an arc from "we decided" to "this is what happened." The return loop transforms the constellation from a diagnostic instrument into a learning cycle. Each pass through see → deliberate → act → witness deepens the community's understanding of its own situation and its capacity to change it. next[Define an "outcome story" template that prompts for before/after, surprises, and unresolved questions.] next[Design the visual representation: how does a return-loop arc differ from an interpretive link?] next[Identify one completed action from an existing pilot and retroactively model the return loop.]

title: Session as Rehearsal
text: Session as Rehearsal Treat each facilitated session with the constellation as a rehearsal — a bounded, low-stakes space where participants practice the skills of collective interpretation, deliberation, and commitment before applying them to consequential decisions. You are introducing deliberation practices to groups that have not previously done collective sense-making. This does not apply to experienced deliberation teams who need no scaffolding. Participants are new to interpreting linked stories and producing shared decisions from spatial patterns. Jumping straight to consequential decisions in an unfamiliar medium risks poor outcomes and eroded trust. Structure early sessions as rehearsals: use a small anthology, set a low-stakes question, walk through the full cycle (explore the constellation → flag a pattern → discuss → decide → record the decision). Debrief the process itself, not just the content. Graduate to consequential sessions once the group has practised the cycle. An atelier is a place of practice before it is a place of production. The deliberation skills — reading space, articulating patterns, translating observations into commitments — are learned through doing, not through instruction. Rehearsal lowers the cost of error and builds the group's confidence in its own capacity. next[Design a 90-minute rehearsal session plan using a 3-story anthology.] next[Define the debrief questions that distinguish process learning from content learning.] next[Test whether groups that rehearse produce better-provenance decisions than groups that do not.]

title: Accountable Use of Proof-of-Concept Funds
text: Accountable Use of Proof-of-Concept Funds Use the proof-of-concept budget to answer the specific “does linking add value” question instead of building a finished system. You are framing how proof-of-concept funds should be spent so funders (and other stakeholders) can see the value of "story linking" versus broader platform build-out. This does not apply once the linking question is already answered or the phase is post-PoC. Funders care whether minimal linking increases organisational value in the proof-of-concept phase. Spending on general development could end with no evidence for that question. Allocate funds to build the minimal feature, run pilots, and extract concrete offerings so the phase ends with documented value. Focusing budget on a falsifiable question is more accountable than diffuse build-out. next[Prepare the funder overview linking feature, pilots, and outcomes to the central question.] next[Define a success threshold (e.g., ≥2 pilots show improved shared insight) to trigger post-PoC build-out.]

title: Askew Layer
text: Askew Layer Add an interpretive “askew” layer where contributors propose arcs, passages, and conceptual bridges without modifying originals. You are designing a narrative system where contributors can explore interpretations and relationships without altering canonical stories, preserving authorial integrity while enabling sense-making. This does not apply when the canonical layer can be edited by mutual consent. Canonical stories must be preserved yet contributors need room to explore relations. Forcing links into the canonical layer violates narrative sovereignty and breeds incoherence. Add an interpretive “askew” layer where contributors propose arcs, passages, and conceptual bridges without modifying originals. Interpretive overlays let relational meaning emerge while protecting authorial integrity. next[Define a lightweight "askew" proposal schema and review workflow.] next[Prototype one askew bridge on an existing story pair.] next[Define apply/avoid signals (e.g., "canon locked" vs "canon editable").] next[Record one case where askew prevented a canonical conflict and one where it added noise.] next[Consolidate with vsatlas/non-destructive-relational-layers and retire this pattern once merged.]

title: Audience Shift
text: Audience Shift Design for peer-to-peer audiences by enabling reciprocal storytelling loops and navigable inter-story connections. You are rethinking platform design so audiences become active participants who respond to and connect with each other’s stories, rather than remaining passive viewers. This does not apply to one-way broadcast archives where participation is not a goal. The platform centres display logic so stories attract passive spectators. Communities require environments where participants recognise and respond to one another as peers. Design for peer-to-peer audiences by enabling reciprocal storytelling loops and navigable inter-story connections. Shifting the audience from spectators to participants restores agency, dialogue, and collective problem-solving. next[Prototype one reciprocal loop (respond, remix, or co-author) in the UI.] next[Measure how often participants move from viewing to contributing.] next[Define an apply signal (e.g., >60% sessions are view-only) and an avoid signal (e.g., high safety risk for public replies).]

title: Current Strength and Gap
text: Current Strength and Gap Recognise that VSAT already excels at self-authored stories but does not yet help organisations see what a cohort’s stories reveal together. You have built a system that supports individual storytelling but that doesn't yet help people see collective patterns across stories. Partners such as ACMi adopt VSAT for elegant individual storytelling. They cannot inspect the collective field; there is no support for linking or comparing stories to surface shared diagnosis. Treat “collective understanding of stories” as the unmet need and scope any proof-of-concept around that gap. Without framing the gap explicitly, pilots will chase polish rather than the organisational question. next[Write an internal note summarising the current strength + explicit gap to anchor partner briefings.] next[Define a gap indicator (e.g., no cross-story links or shared themes in partner debriefs) and note when the pattern stops applying.]

title: Economic Resonance Layer
text: Economic Resonance Layer Allow emergent clusters to attach lightweight economic tools (mutual aid, microcredit, resource maps) to relational arcs. You are exploring how narrative connections can be paired with lightweight economic tools so relational meaning aligns with material mutual support. This does not apply when there is no willingness to manage shared resources. Treat this as future work until core linking is validated. title: Festival Model
text: Festival Model Treat the manifold as a festival—an evolving scene where newcomers, veterans, and stewards co-create shared worlds. Cultural vitality emerges from collective gatherings, ongoing creation, and interwoven practices. Treat the manifold as a festival—an evolving scene where newcomers, veterans, and stewards co-create shared worlds. text: Isolarion Drift Introduce a manifold layer where canonical charts overlap voluntarily so resonances can emerge without rewriting originals. Groups need shared meaning rather than atomised testimony. Introduce a manifold layer where canonical charts overlap voluntarily so resonances can emerge without rewriting originals. title: Minimal Feature and Pilots
text: Minimal Feature and Pilots Build only the minimal linking feature and test it with one or two tightly scoped pilots. This does not apply when the linking loop is already validated for the Budget is small and the linking concept is unproven with real groups. Shipping broader features before testing risks consuming funds without answering the central question. target cohort.
